title: Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0
description:
## Why this epic exists
The 2026-10-08 reality check (commit `c808a6e`) found that all 583 pre-existing beads were closed
while the core promise was not met. The README says `asx` "ports asupersync's full semantic model
to ANSI C" with Rust parity proven by conformance fixtures. Instead:

- **Parity gates were vacuous.**
  - `make conformance` reported `fixture_records=70 parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0
    pass=true`.
  - No C code interprets fixture ops.
  - Fixtures were synthesized by the capture tool, not recorded from asupersync.
  - A fixture with op `launch_missiles` passes.
  - codec-equivalence and profile-parity compare digest strings already stored in the fixtures.
  - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
- **Real drift vs Rust `5e60b1c4c` (0.6.0) went undetected.** Examples:
  - reversed budget-priority semiring;
  - cleanup budget enforced as a hard kill;
  - region close ordering;
  - Finalizing admission;
  - leak-policy default;
  - missing cancel attribution chains;
  - poll-race loser drain;
  - task-group FIRST_OK/tie-break;
  - the scheduler (arena-index sweep vs Rust's lanes and seeded one-step picker).
- **Real C bugs.**
  - The trace digest ignores everything after 1024 events.
  - Barrier is not reusable.
  - `notify_one` loses wakeups.
  - Watch receivers report phantom changes.
  - An actor reply is lost if the actor exits right after replying.
  - The HTTP server is starved by 4 idle connections and never enforces its drain timeout.
  - The run deadline is ignored while blocked in epoll.
  - A UBSan hit in `supervisor.c:367`.
- **CI has never passed.** Every `ci.yml` run on record failed at format-check (6 violations in 2
  files). Locally, format-check prints SKIP because clang-format isn't installed.
- **Coverage is far below the claim.** About 13% of Rust 0.6.0's semantic surface overall, about
  24% of the kernel-like subset. Inventory docs are pinned 19,722 Rust commits back.
- **The README is wrong in many places.** Counts, 8 non-compiling samples, 12 contradictions,
  unenforced resource classes, an embedded CI matrix that silently skips, no wasm32 or MSVC
  builds, and TLS that is a plaintext passthrough.

## Goal
Turn `asx` into a port whose Rust faithfulness is **proven by an honest, fail-closed differential
oracle against asupersync 0.6.0**. Fix every semantic drift and bug that oracle and the audit
expose, and make every README claim generated from evidence.

## Milestones (each has a gate bead)
- **M-α:** honest gates plus critical bug fixes.
- **M-β:** oracle online, with K1 as the first unit fixed under it.
- **M-γ:** kernel and scheduler parity.
- **M-δ:** channel, sync, time and actor parity.
- **M-ε:** proof breadth (cross-arch, record/replay, fuzz soak, sanitizers, footprint).
- **M-ζ:** surfaces, performance and governance.

## Structure
One child epic per workstream:
- W0 truth and gates
- W1 oracle
- K kernel
- S scheduler
- C channels
- Y sync
- T time
- A actors
- L lab/trace
- RB runtime robustness
- RP record/replay
- M metamorphic
- R resource contract
- P performance
- E embedded/portability
- SEC memory safety
- X surfaces and owner decisions
- G governance

## Done when
All six milestone gate beads are closed with evidence. The README parity table is generated from
oracle output. CI is green and blocking on every listed gate.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**

- Evidence-required bead closure.

title: Fix the 6 clang-format violations that have blocked every CI run since inception
description:
## Problem
`gh run list --workflow ci.yml --status success` returns nothing, and the last 200 runs all
failed. In every run the `check` job fails at the "Format check" step (exit 2). Every downstream
job is skipped as a result: unit, conformance, profile parity, fuzz, e2e, compiler matrix and
embedded matrix. None of those gates has ever executed in CI.

Locally, `make format-check` prints `SKIP (clang-format not found)` because clang-format isn't
installed on the dev machine or the rch workers. Agents therefore believed the gate passed.

With clang-format **18.1.8** (the Ubuntu 24.04 `ubuntu-latest` version; reproducible via
`uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`) there are exactly 6 violations in 2 files:
- `src/runtime/runtime_internal.h` (3)
- `tests/unit/net/test_http_wire.c` (3)

## Plan
1. Run the dry run with the pinned version and inspect it:
   `find include src tests \( -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' \) -print0 | xargs -0 uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format --dry-run --Werror`
2. Apply the formatting changes **manually** with an editor. Per AGENTS.md, do not run a
   code-modifying script. The changes are whitespace or line-wrapping only.
3. Re-run the dry run: there must be 0 errors.
4. Confirm the CI workflow installs a clang-format version that matches 18.1.8 behaviour. If
   `apt` on `ubuntu-latest` gives a different major version, pin it, for example
   `pip install clang-format==18.1.8` in `ci.yml`, so local and CI agree. Note that the runner
   label migrates to Ubuntu 26 on 2026-10-19.

## Success criteria
- The pinned dry run prints 0 violations across `include/ src/ tests/`.
- `ci.yml` pins the formatter version explicitly.
- A pushed commit gets past the "Format check" step in CI; record the run URL in the close reason.

## Tests
None new. This is a formatting-only change. The full local gate (`make build test`) must still
pass.

title: Stop tracking compiled ELF binaries under tests/fuzz (owner approval required for removal)
description:
## Problem
5 compiled ELF binaries are tracked in git under `tests/fuzz/` and `tests/unit/fuzz/`. Find them
with:
```
git ls-files tests | xargs file | grep ELF
```
Build artifacts in git bloat the repo, drift from source, and can mislead reviewers and agents.

## Plan
1. Add patterns to `.gitignore` so new binaries aren't tracked.
2. **Ask the owner for explicit written permission** to remove the tracked binaries from the
   index (`git rm --cached <paths>`). Per AGENTS.md RULE 1 (no deletion without permission),
   never run this without that approval. Record the approval text, the command and the time in
   the close reason.
3. If permission is denied, document why they stay.

## Success criteria
`git ls-files | xargs file | grep -c ELF` returns 0 (with approval), or a documented owner
decision to keep them.

title: e2e suite: avoid nested rch offload in OpenWrt packaging, isolate its build dir, add per-scenario timeouts
description:
## Problem
On 2026-10-08, `rch exec -- make test-e2e` took **17.5 min**. The packaging family alone
(`GATE-E2E-PACKAGE`, `tests/e2e/openwrt_package.sh`) took about 12 min; the other 21 families
together took about 5. The cause is a chain:
- `openwrt_package.sh` calls `tools/packaging/openwrt/build_package.sh`;
- its `run_build_cmd` (`:55-75`) with `ASX_USE_RCH=auto` runs `rch exec -- make ... build
  PROFILE=EMBEDDED_ROUTER CODEC=BIN DETERMINISTIC=1`;
- when the suite is *already* running on an rch worker, `rch` is on that worker's PATH (verified:
  `/home/ubuntu/.local/bin/rch`, env `RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1`), so it offloads a second time.

Two more problems:
- **Hidden coupling.** The nested build writes `build/lib/libasx.a` for ROUTER/BIN into the shared
  `build/` dir (`BUILD_DIR := build` is not profile-specific, `Makefile:323`), clobbering the
  CORE library other steps may use.
- **No per-scenario timeout.** A real hang would block until rch's 1800 s kill.

## Plan
1. The Makefile exports `ASX_IN_RCH=1`, or detects the rch worker environment.
   `build_package.sh` auto mode runs locally when it is already inside rch.
2. The packaging build uses an isolated build dir. Make the Makefile `BUILD_DIR` overridable
   (`BUILD_DIR ?= build`) and pass `BUILD_DIR=build/pkg-router`.
3. `tests/e2e/run_all.sh` wraps each family in `timeout ${E2E_FAMILY_TIMEOUT:-300}`. A timeout is
   a FAIL with the family log path and the elapsed time.
4. Log per-family wall time in the suite JSONL so regressions are visible.

## Success criteria
- `rch exec -- make test-e2e` finishes in under 7 minutes.
- `sha256sum build/lib/libasx.a` is identical before and after the suite.
- A test family that sleeps 600 s is reported FAIL at the timeout. Add it as an opt-in self-test,
  `E2E_SELFTEST_TIMEOUT=1`.

title: Evidence-required bead closure: wire lint-evidence into CI; parity-claiming beads must link oracle evidence
description:
## Problem
Beads were closed with evidence that couldn't prove the claim: parity "passes" from a gate that
compared nothing, and a browser runtime closed without a wasm build. `make lint-evidence` exists

`lint-schema-validation` are skipped in CI too.

1. Push.

an explicitly labelled non-blocking job until milestone M-β, after which it becomes blocking.

title: STRICT_GATES mode: missing formatter/analyzer/toolchain is a FAILURE, not SKIP; pinned reproducible tool versions
description:
## Problem
These targets print SKIP when a tool is missing:
- `make format-check` (`Makefile:603-615`): clang-format;
- `make lint` (cppcheck), probably;
- possibly others: run `grep -n 'SKIP' Makefile tools/ci/*.sh`.

AGENTS.md tells agents to run these gates. Because the tools aren't installed locally or on rch
workers, every agent "passed" format-check while CI failed it on every push. The same
fail-open pattern appears in `ci-embedded-matrix` (`FAIL_ON_MISSING=0` skips cross targets) and
in `fuzz-smoke` (the Rust binary is optional).

## Plan
1. Add `STRICT_GATES ?= 0` to the Makefile.
   - When it is 1, every SKIP-on-missing-tool path becomes `exit 1` with a clear message saying
     how to get the tool.
   - CI sets `STRICT_GATES=1` globally.
2. Reproducible tool acquisition without system installs:
   - **clang-format:** `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`. Add a `CLANG_FORMAT ?=`
     variable that defaults to `clang-format` when present, else the uvx form when `uvx` exists.
   - **cppcheck:** document the pinned version. If it's unavailable via uv/pip, use the CI
     container or apt.
3. Inventory every SKIP path in the Makefile and `tools/ci/*.sh`, in a table in the bead close
   reason: which tool, what the strict behaviour is, and how to obtain the tool.
4. Update AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" to say `STRICT_GATES=1` and give the uvx clang-format
   command.

## Success criteria
- On a machine without system clang-format but with uvx, `make format-check STRICT_GATES=1`
  passes on a clean tree and fails on a deliberately misformatted file.
- With the tool absent and no uvx, it FAILS.
- `grep -n SKIP` inventory: every remaining SKIP is reachable only when `STRICT_GATES=0`.

## Tests
A shell test `tests/gates/test_strict_gates.sh`:
- runs format-check with `PATH` stripped of clang-format and uvx, expecting failure under
  `STRICT_GATES=1`;
- feeds a temp copy of a source file with a formatting error through the formatter and expects
  failure. Do not modify the tracked file.

Structured log lines go to `build/test-logs/gates.jsonl`.

title: Make the conformance gates fail closed now: 0 comparisons = FAIL, rename fake lanes honestly, digest recompute, sabotage negative control
description:
## Problem
`tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` currently does three things:
- a jq check that fields are present, the digest matches a regex, and provenance equals
  `docs/rust_baseline_inventory.json` (around `:437-458`);
- a generated `fixture_runner` that decodes each fixture and calls
  `asx_codec_cross_codec_verify` (around `:321-339`), which encodes to JSON and BIN, decodes, and
  compares fields (`src/runtime/equivalence.c:177-232`);
- codec/profile lanes that compare the `semantic_digest` strings already stored in fixture files
  (around `:515-569`).

No C runtime function is ever called. `make conformance` on 2026-10-08 printed
`fixture_records=70 parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 fail=0 ... pass=true`.

A sabotaged fixture still passes. Its op is `launch_missiles`, it has 50 events of kind
`NonexistentKind`, `tasks: -1`, and digest `sha256:dede…`. A copy is at
`/data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-asupersync-ansi-c/91742396-525f-4214-b4af-ee5de903e8de/scratchpad/agents/parity_audit/fx/sabotaged.json`;
reconstruct it if that path is gone.

The 4 `combinator-contract-001` fixtures (commit ea460a5) were hand-written. They use a bead ID
as `capture_run_id` and C status names, and their `semantic_digest` does not recompute from their
own contents. The other 66 do recompute.

## Plan
1. **Rename the lanes to what they are.**
   - The current conformance checks become `make fixture-integrity` (schema plus provenance) and
     `make codec-roundtrip` (codec encode/decode equality).
   - These stay green and blocking.
2. **`make conformance` must mean "Rust parity".**
   - Fail when `comparable_parity_records == 0`, with the message:
     `NO RUST PARITY EVIDENCE: oracle not yet implemented (see W1)`.
   - Fail when any record's digest came from the fixture rather than from executing the C
     runtime. The interpreter in W1.5 provides an `engine_identity` field; until it exists, every
     record is non-comparable.
3. **Digest recompute check.**
   - Every fixture's `semantic_digest` must recompute from its own `expected_events` using the
     documented algorithm.
   - The 4 hand-written combinator fixtures fail this. Quarantine them by moving them under
     `fixtures/rust_reference/_quarantine/`, which needs owner approval because it is a file
     move. Alternatively mark them `"provenance_class": "hand_authored"` and exclude them from
     the Rust-parity lane. Don't delete them.
4. **`capture_run_id` must be a UUID.** Unknown ops (`unknown_op:*` user traces) fail
   fixture-integrity.
5. **Negative-control fixtures**, checked in under `fixtures/negative_controls/`:
   - the sabotage fixture;
   - a fixture whose digest doesn't recompute;
   - a fixture with a non-UUID run ID.

   Each must fail the respective gate. Add a test asserting the gates FAIL on them.
6. **CI.** The Rust-parity lane runs as a clearly labelled non-blocking job
   ("rust-parity (pending oracle W1)") until milestone M-β. Then flip it to blocking. Don't hide
   it.
7. **Docs.** Update the README and `docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md` so they no longer claim Rust parity
   (pairs with W0.4c and W0.5).

## Success criteria
- `make conformance` exits non-zero on the current corpus and prints the honest reason.
- `make fixture-integrity` and `make codec-roundtrip` pass on the 66 recomputable fixtures and
  fail on the negative controls.
- A test script `tests/gates/test_conformance_fail_closed.sh` exercises all of the above and logs
  JSONL.

title: Generate every README count/table from machine-readable sources; lint-docs fails on hand-edited numbers
description:
## Problem
The README's numbers are wrong and drift with every commit:

| Claim | Actual (2026-10-08) |
|---|---|

| 204 test programs | 219 |
| 149 unit | 159 |
| 20 or 17 e2e | 22 |
| 3 conformance | 6 |
| 125 headers | 127 |
| 123 C sources | 131 |
| 75 docs | 79 |
| 23 parity units | 30 |
| core 19 headers | 22 |
| runtime 28 headers / 37 files | 29 / 38 |
| sync 8 files | 9 `.c` + 1 `.h` |
| platform 3 files | 7 |
| arena table: regions 64, tasks 256, obligations 256, MPSC 32 | 8, 64, 128, 16 (`ASX_MAX_*` macros) |
| CI diagram "148 unit", "17 scenarios" | 159, 22 |
| badges (L12-L14) | same wrong numbers |

`tools/count_inventory.sh` exists. Check what it computes.

## Plan
1. Extend `tools/count_inventory.sh` (or add `tools/docs/gen_readme_facts.sh`) to emit
   `build/docs/readme_facts.json`:
   - `ASX_API` count (unique);
   - header count, both total and per family;
   - source count per subsystem;
   - test programs per category;
   - examples, vignettes and docs counts;
   - `FEATURE_PARITY` units;
   - arena capacities per profile and resource class, from the macros, by compiling a tiny
     program that prints them;
   - CI job count.
2. In the README, wrap each generated value in markers such as
   `<!-- fact:asx_api_count -->1916<!-- /fact -->`, including in tables and badges.
3. `make lint-docs` regenerates the facts and fails on any mismatch, with a diff. Add
   `make docs-facts-update` to rewrite the marked values. This rewrites a doc, not code, so it's
   allowed; still review the diff.
4. Wire `lint-docs` into the CI `check` job (it already has an "API docs" lint; extend or add).

## Success criteria
- Changing a marked number in the README makes `make lint-docs` fail with a precise diff.
- All current README numbers are correct.
- CI runs `lint-docs`.

## Tests
`tests/gates/test_readme_facts.sh` mutates a temp copy of the README and asserts that the lint
fails. Logs JSONL.

title: Fix the 8 non-compiling README code samples and compile every README C sample in CI
description:
## Problem
These README C samples do not compile against the real headers:

| README lines | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| L1052-1056 | `asx_cx_narrow` argument order is reversed; `ASX_CAP_NETWORK` doesn't exist | real order is `(parent, child, caps)`; use a real capability |
| L1193 | `asx_plan_dag_id` doesn't exist | the type is `asx_plan_id` |
| L1209 | `asx_cleanup_push` called with 3 args | it takes 4 |
| L1266 | `asx_task_state_is_terminal` / `asx_region_state_is_closing` don't exist | `asx_task_is_terminal` / `asx_region_is_closing` |
| L1384-1389 | `asx_stream_map`, `asx_stream_map_poll`, `asx_stream_status` don't exist; init signature differs | use the real stream API |
| L1414-1424 | no `max_polls_per_step` field; no `asx_lab_run` | `max_polls`; `asx_lab_run_scenario` |
| L1642 | `asx_abi_feature_flags()` doesn't exist | use the real query |
| L1644 | `ASX_E_NOT_SUPPORTED` doesn't exist (also referenced in `wasm_abi.h:72`) | use a real status |

The quickstart at L83-123 does compile and run (exit 0).

## Plan
1. Fix each sample against the real API (read the headers). If a sample illustrates an API that
   *should* exist per Rust parity, track that in the relevant parity bead and still make the
   sample compile against today's API.
2. Fix `include/asx/abi/wasm_abi.h:72` (the nonexistent `ASX_E_NOT_SUPPORTED`).
3. Add `tools/docs/extract_c_samples.sh`, which pulls README code fences marked ` ```c ` (fragments
   can use a wrapper template with `main`) and compiles each against `include/` with the strict
   warning set, then links `libasx.a`.
4. Add `make lint-readme-samples` to the CI check job.

## Success criteria

title: Resolve the 12 README contradictions and replace overclaims with honest, evidence-linked scoping
description:
## Contradictions to resolve (line numbers as of `c808a6e`)
1. **CLI.** L297-301 and the FAQ at L1882 say no standalone `asx` executable ships, while
   L56-60, L175, L205-217 and L452 describe `make cli` building `build/bin/asx`, and L1782
   describes "the `asx doctor` command". Truth: `make cli` builds it; `make install` does not
   install it.
2. **Reactor.** L1844 says native reactor backends are "not yet shipped", while L1345 says an
   epoll reactor is installed. Truth: POSIX live builds ship epoll (Linux) with a poll(2)
   fallback; kqueue, IOCP and io_uring are absent (io_uring returns PERMISSION_DENIED).
3. **Threading.** L1116 and L1286 say "single-threaded walking skeleton", while L1280 describes a
   cross-thread waker and a pthread blocking pool. Truth: one scheduler thread, plus
   blocking-pool threads in POSIX live builds.
4. **Multi-core.** L1251 ("Phase 4 multi-threaded dispatch") and L1560 ("future") conflict with
   L506 ("Multi-core"). Truth: PARALLEL lanes are logical (`native_live_enabled` is hard-coded 0
   at `parallel.c:403-420`).
5. **"Full semantic model."** L37 and the comparison table at L147-160 overclaim. Truth: about
   24% of the kernel-like Rust surface and about 13% overall, with known drift. Replace with
   honest scoping and a link to the generated parity table.
6. **WASM and Windows.** L140, L495, L557 and L951 claim both. Truth: there is no wasm32 build
   target anywhere, and Win32 has no native I/O and no CI build.
7. **Parity claims.** L54, L509, L1588, L1618 and L1570 claim cross-profile and Rust digest
   parity and that the runner "replays each fixture through the C runtime". Truth: false until
   W1 lands; say so.
8. **Resource classes.** L131 and L491-502 call the class limits "concrete limits". Truth: they
   are validated, not enforced (bead R1).
9. **`make check`.** L631 calls it the "Full CI gate", but L1546 says that is `check-ci`, which
   also omits `formal-check`.
10. **E2E list.** L1493 vs L613 vs the tree give 17, 20 and 22 e2e programs. L1500-1510 lists
    `e2e_browser_smoke.c`, which never existed; only `browser_smoke.sh` exists.
11. **Channel headers.** L599 lists `include/asx/channel/`, which doesn't exist; channel headers
    live in `include/asx/core/`.
12. **Stale register rows.** The README's references to `DEFERRED_STUBS_REGISTER` rows for
    win32 and io_driver are out of date (pairs with W0.5).

## Other overclaims
| README | Claim | Truth |
|---|---|---|
| L1527 | "no suppression flags" | `-Wno-unused-parameter` is used |
| L1533 | "eight lint gates run before merge" | CI skips `lint-evidence`, `lint-semantic-delta` and `lint-schema-validation`; `formal-check`, `size-gate` and `slo-gate` aren't in CI |
| L1725 | "All 8 jobs must pass" | CI never passed (until W0.1b) |
| L1859 | embedded CI covers mipsel/armv7/aarch64/RISC-V + QEMU | the lanes skip; there is no RISC-V lane and QEMU is off |
| L1620 | fixtures in "both JSON and BIN formats" | the BIN files are JSON |
| L1886 | "200-400 KB library, R1 under 64 KB RAM" | unmeasured (bead R3) |
| L831-843 | FNV-1a digest offset basis `0x517cc1b727220a95` | not FNV's basis (`0xcbf29ce484222325`); the digest also ignores events after 1024 (bead RB1) |
| L147-160 Rust column | — | Rust has a built-in circuit breaker (`combinator/circuit_breaker.rs`), epochs, a deadline monitor, metrics histograms, Lean/TLA artifacts, kqueue/io_uring/Windows reactors, TLS and a wasm crate |

## Plan
Edit the README so every statement is true at HEAD. Where a feature is in progress, say "in
progress" and link the bead. Add a short **"Status vs asupersync 0.6.0"** section near the top:
- what is proven;
- what drifts;
- what is missing.

Link `docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md` and, once W1 exists, the generated parity table.

## Success criteria
A fresh reviewer reading the README finds no contradiction, and every capability claim maps to a
test, gate or bead. Record the claim-to-evidence list in the close reason.

description:
## Problem
All 583 beads were closed at check time, but several closure claims are false:
- **`bd-1eqo.16` (browser runtime).** Closed as completed, yet `include/asx/abi/wasm_abi.h` says
  the browser runtime is "deferred to bd-1eqo.16", and no wasm32 target exists anywhere.

  "parity pass" evidence). Their evidence was the self-referential gate.

- wake-driven scheduler (`11026f1`);
- task groups (`32f5e3c`);
- obligation holders and leak policy (`fc66c9e`);
- cancel masking (`57bcc37`);
- HTTP/1.1 (`322f655`), WebSocket (`ea13a33`), RaptorQ (`37631f0`), security primitives
  (`a978cc7`);
- native reactor and sockets (`ee94f37`), native fs/process/signal (`3792017`), DNS (`e75b70f`);
- channels/sync wake-driven (`66009de`);
- actors (`f4fc216`).

   - reopen it, if the work is still owed; or

title: [RB] Runtime robustness and ergonomics found by real end-to-end usage
description:
## Why
Building real programs against the library exposed defects that unit tests hide:
- the trace digest ignores everything after 1024 events (critical: it makes replay verification
  vacuous);
- the default build fakes networking and busy-spins;
- the HTTP server is starved by 4 idle connections, never enforces its drain timeout and binds
  only loopback;
- compile-time caps can't be overridden;
- 13 of 159 unit suites fail in POSIX-live mode, which CI never runs;
- a UBSan hit in `supervisor.c:367` and an ASan stack-use-after-return in `test_rt.c`;

- `ASX_MUST_USE` friction (an example fails `-Werror`);
- library/app config mismatches go undetected;
- `asx doctor` always reports HEALTHY.

title: RB1 Trace digest ignores every event after the first 1024 (replay verification vacuous at scale) - make it a rolling digest
description:
## Bug (verified)
In `src/runtime/trace.c`:
- `asx_trace_emit` (`:97-106`) stores only the first `ASX_TRACE_CAPACITY` (1024) events and then
  just increments `g_trace_count`.
- `asx_trace_digest` (`:166-180`) hashes only the stored prefix.

So two runs that diverge **after** event 1024 produce the **same digest**. Evidence: a 1000-task
swarm gave `17ba9890164d5fd7` in deterministic runs, in live runs with different message orders,
and in a run deliberately perturbed late. About 100 tasks are enough to saturate the buffer.

Related problems:
- `asx_trace_event_count` (`:108-113`) clamps, which hides the overflow.
- The "ring buffer" in the README (L833) is actually a prefix buffer.
- The digest's "FNV-1a offset basis" is `0x517cc1b727220a95` (`:167`, and in README L838), but
  the FNV-1a 64-bit offset basis is `0xcbf29ce484222325`. The event log digest elsewhere uses the
  correct one (e2e output shows `event_log_digest=0xcbf29ce484222325`).

This undermines the README's central promises: "Deterministic replay and trace hashing",
"Trace digests are hash-stable", the telemetry tiers ("digest computed" even in ULTRA_MIN), and
replay verification.

## Fix
1. **Rolling digest.** Update the digest inside `asx_trace_emit` for *every* event, independent of
   storage. Include the event sequence (emitted total). Define finalization as mixing in the total
   count.
2. **True ring buffer.** Keep the last N events for forensics, configurable via `#ifndef`-guarded
   `ASX_TRACE_CAPACITY` (RB4).
3. **Counters.** Expose `asx_trace_emitted_total()` and `asx_trace_dropped()`, and fix the count
   API docs.
4. **Constants.** Use the real FNV-1a offset basis, or document clearly that it's a custom seed.
   The canonical cross-engine digest is SHA-256 over vocabulary v2 (W1.2); this FNV digest is the
   C-internal fast digest, so say so.
5. **Replay.** Replay verification (`asx_replay_*`) compares rolling digests plus per-window
   checkpoints. The hindsight and replay modules must handle more than capacity correctly.
6. **Telemetry tiers.** ULTRA_MIN computes the rolling digest with zero storage, which is the
   README promise, made true.
7. **Fixed digests.** Update any digest value hard-coded in tests or fixtures that changes.
   Explain this in the commit; it's a legitimate spec fix, not drift.

## Tests
- Perturbing event #5000 changes the digest.
- Identical 100k-event runs give identical digests.
- ULTRA_MIN digest == FORENSIC digest.
- Ring contents are the last N.
- e2e: a 1000-task swarm with a late perturbation → the digest differs (the e2e program from the
  audit, reproduced in `tests/e2e/`).

title: RB2 Default build fakes networking: MEMORY backend listen "succeeds" on port 0 and accept loop busy-spins ~1M polls
description:
## Bug
Plain `make build` produces CORE with `DETERMINISTIC=1`, which means the MEMORY net backend. A
user's HTTP server built that way:
- has `asx_server_listen` return OK with port 0 and no OS socket;
- spins its accept task for 999,999 polls until the run budget is exhausted.

Nothing tells the user they're on the fake backend. README examples give no compile line saying
real I/O needs `PROFILE=POSIX DETERMINISTIC=0` (plus `-lpthread -lrt` and
`-DASX_LOCKFREE_SINGLE_THREAD=0` per the audit).

## Fix
1. The MEMORY backend parks accept/recv on in-memory readiness (wake-driven) and never spins
   (pairs with S2).
2. Listening on a port in MEMORY mode either works deterministically on an in-memory port
   namespace (reported port ≠ 0) or returns an explicit status. Pick one, document it, and test
   it.
3. Add `asx_net_backend()` / `asx_runtime_describe()` so apps can log which backend is active.
   `asx doctor` (RB8) reports it.
4. README "Native I/O" gets the exact build line for real I/O, and a pkg-config/CMake hint.

## Tests
- The MEMORY accept loop with no clients ends `WOULD_BLOCK` in under 10 polls (not 1M).
- The listen behaviour test.
- A doctor output test.

title: RB3 HTTP server robustness: >4 conns, header/idle/request timeouts, enforced drain timeout, bind address, configurable limits, slowloris test
description:
## Bugs (from real e2e)
- **Connection cap.** `ASX_HTTP_SERVER_MAX_CONNS=4`: 4 idle TCP connections make every other
  client time out (curl rc=28); with 3 idle, requests are served in 0.3 ms.
- **No timeouts.** There is no header-read, idle or request timeout.
- **Drain timeout ignored.** `drain_timeout_ms` is never read (only reference: `src/net/server.c:24`).
  A client stuck mid-request held shutdown for 12.03 s with a 5 s drain timeout configured.
- **Loopback only.** `asx_server_listen` hardcodes `asx_socket_addr_loopback` (`server.c:53`),
  and `asx_server_config` has no address field.
- **Compile-time limits.** Inline body 4096 bytes, 16 headers, 256-byte URI.

Rust's HTTP server has timeouts, a drain signal, and connection limits with overload policy (see
`/dp/asupersync/src/http`, `src/server`).

## Fix
1. Configurable connection cap with an overload policy: reject with 503, or stop accepting
   (backpressure).
2. Header-read, idle and request timeouts as task timers.
3. Drain timeout enforced: after it expires, cancel the remaining connection tasks with SHUTDOWN.
4. A bind address field (IPv4/IPv6, any or specific).
5. Limits in config, bounded by compile-time maxima.
6. Keep-alive max requests per connection.

## Tests
`tests/e2e/http_robustness.sh` against a real native server, with JSONL logs:
- slowloris (N slow clients) does not block a fresh client;
- 64 concurrent keep-alive clients;
- drain with stuck clients finishes within drain_timeout + ε;
- bind to `0.0.0.0` / `::`.

title: RB4 Every capacity macro must be overridable: add #ifndef guards to ASX_TRACE_CAPACITY, ASX_MAX_CHANNELS, ASX_MAX_TIMERS, ASX_MAX_WAKERS, etc.
description:
## Bug
`ASX_TRACE_CAPACITY`, `ASX_MAX_CHANNELS`, `ASX_MAX_TIMERS` and `ASX_MAX_WAKERS` have no `#ifndef`
guard, so users can't raise them without editing headers. Other `ASX_MAX_*` macros can be
overridden (commit `bfb4739` made arena caps overridable). Defaults are small: 64 tasks,
8 regions, 16 channels (capacity ≤ 64), 16 TCP streams.

## Fix
1. Audit every capacity macro (`rg -n '#define ASX_(MAX|.*CAPACITY)' include src`).
2. Add a guard and a static assertion of sane bounds to each.
3. Document the full list (generated table, W0.4a).
4. Make resource-class defaults derive from them consistently (R1).

## Tests
A build test compiles the library and a smoke test with every macro overridden (e.g. ×4), runs
the smoke, and asserts the capacities via the query API.

title: RB5 POSIX-live unit suite fails 13/159 suites; add CI lane running full unit suite with PROFILE=POSIX DETERMINISTIC=0
description:
## Bug
Building and running the unit suite with `PROFILE=POSIX DETERMINISTIC=0`: 146/159 pass. 13 fail,
with or without sanitizers. Mostly these are tests that inject a virtual clock, the ghost reactor
or entropy hooks and assume the deterministic backends:
- `test_sleep.c:108`
- `test_deadline.c:79`
- `test_io_driver.c:336`
- `test_parallel.c:966`
- `test_hooks.c:201`
- …and others; see the audit log
  `/data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-asupersync-ansi-c/91742396-525f-4214-b4af-ee5de903e8de/scratchpad/e2e/t7/plain-posix.log`.

`test_process_native` fails when PATH contains unsearchable directories (EACCES). `execvp`
semantics skip those, but the C PATH lookup doesn't.

CI runs the unit suite only in deterministic mode (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:756`); only
`test_net_native` runs live (`:766`).

## Fix
1. Make each failing test mode-aware: either install deterministic hooks explicitly in live
   builds, or skip with an explicit, logged reason. A skip must be visible in counts, never silent.
2. Fix the PATH search to skip EACCES/ENOENT directories like `execvp`.
3. Add a CI job: `make test-unit PROFILE=POSIX DETERMINISTIC=0` (and ASan/UBSan via E5).

## Tests
The new CI lane is green, and the counts are reported (pass / fail / explicit-skip).

title: RB6 Sanitizer findings: UBSan memcpy(NULL,0) in supervisor.c:367; ASan stack-use-after-return in test_rt.c live builds
description:
## Findings
1. **UBSan, library.** `src/actor/supervisor.c:367` calls `memcpy(s->specs, children, 0)` with
   `children == NULL`. It is reachable from the public API via `asx_supervisor_start(..., NULL, 0)`,
   which `tests/unit/actor/test_supervisor.c:217` calls and says is allowed. A null pointer to
   memcpy is UB even with size 0, and this breaks the plan §2.1.1 UB-elimination contract.
2. **ASan, test bug, live builds.** `tests/unit/runtime/test_rt.c:59` (`add_one`, run on a
   blocking-pool worker) and `:449-457` assume `asx_spawn_blocking` completes synchronously, which
   is true only on CORE. The assertion fails, the test returns early, and the worker thread later
   reads the dead stack variable `input` (stack-use-after-return).

## Fix
1. Guard the memcpy (`if (count > 0)`). Audit for the same pattern:
   `rg -n 'memcpy\(|memmove\(|memset\(' src`, checking for possibly-NULL with possibly-0.
2. Make `test_rt.c` wait for blocking completion (park/poll until done) and keep `input` alive in
   static or heap storage for the duration.

## Tests
The ASan+UBSan lane (E5) is clean on CORE and POSIX-live. Add a regression test for
`supervisor_start(NULL, 0)` under UBSan.

title: RB7 Live mode: asx_scheduler_run budget deadline ignored while blocked in epoll (hangs past deadline)
description:
## Bug (gdb-verified)
In live POSIX mode, `asx_scheduler_run(rid, &budget)` with a budget deadline of now + 200 ms hung
indefinitely in `epoll_wait`:
- `sched_block` at `src/runtime/scheduler.c:548`;
- called from `sched_idle` at `:595`.

The task was parked on I/O and the run budget's deadline was never used to bound the reactor
wait. A region-level budget deadline works (0.20 s), because it arms a task timer.

## Fix
1. When idle, bound the reactor block by min(next timer deadline, run budget deadline).
2. When the run deadline passes, return the documented status, consistent with the README's
   description of run budgets. Decide between `ASX_E_POLL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` and a deadline
   status, and document it.
3. Check the same for the poll quota: a run quota should not be consumed while blocked, and the
   block must not be infinite when the quota is 0.

## Tests
- Live-mode test: a task parked on a socket that never becomes ready; run with a +200 ms deadline
  → returns within 200 ms ± 50 ms.
- Also under `rch exec` CI (timing tolerance documented).

title: RB8 Ergonomics: ASX_IGNORE_RESULT, examples build under -Werror in CI, lib/app config fingerprint check, real asx doctor probes
description:
## Findings
1. **`ASX_MUST_USE`** expands to `warn_unused_result`, and GCC does not honour `(void)` casts
   against it. Every ignored `asx_task_wake`, `asx_region_get_state` etc. needs a dummy variable,
   which is why `examples/ex_join_set.c:57,72` fails `-Werror`. The shipped example breaks the
   project's own policy, and the examples smoke doesn't build with `-Werror`.
2. **Undetected config mismatch.** An application compiled with a different `ASX_PROFILE_*`,
   `ASX_DETERMINISTIC` or `ASX_MAX_*` than `libasx.a` silently misbehaves: struct sizes, handle
   layouts and backends differ.
3. **`asx doctor`** inspects only a freshly created in-process runtime, so it always reports
   "8 pass, HEALTHY". It reports "io driver initialized" even on CORE, and silently accepts an
   unknown `--format=yaml`.
4. After `asx_scheduler_run` returns OK, the region is still OPEN and not quiescent, which
   surprises users. Document this, or adopt Rust scope semantics (K4).

## Fix
1. Provide `ASX_IGNORE_RESULT(expr)`, which is portable (assign to a dummy). Fix the examples and
   build all examples with `-Werror` in CI.
2. Config fingerprint: the headers define `ASX_CONFIG_FINGERPRINT`, a hash of profile,
   determinism, codec, every `ASX_MAX_*` and struct sizes. `asx_runtime_init` (via a macro
   wrapper that passes the app's fingerprint) compares it to the library's and returns
   `ASX_E_CONFIG_MISMATCH` (a new status, appended).
3. Doctor probes the clock (monotonic progress), the reactor (self-pipe round trip), sockets
   (loopback bind), threads (blocking-pool round trip), entropy (OS read) and the active backends.
   It rejects unknown formats.
4. Documentation for (4).

## Tests
- An app built with mismatched `ASX_MAX_TASKS` → init returns `CONFIG_MISMATCH`.
- Doctor on CORE reports no native backends; on POSIX-live it reports pass for each probe.
- The examples build with `-Werror`.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.
4. **Tests are required.**
   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.
   - E2E scripts emit detailed structured JSONL logs: `ts`, `run_id`, `layer`, `suite`, `test`,
     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.
5. **Never delete a file or directory without explicit written owner permission**
   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.
6. **Don't run code-modifying scripts** (AGENTS.md). Make code changes manually.
7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.
8. **Close only with evidence.** The close reason must name test names, gate output and artifact
   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.
9. **Rust line numbers drift.** Treat cited `file:line` anchors as grep starting points and
   re-verify them at the pinned rev.

Orientation-only living plan: `docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md`. This bead is meant to be
sufficient on its own.

title: Root-cause CI flakiness on main (19 of 30 recent runs failed or cancelled; e.g. native_host and automotive_watchdog in run 38277425775)
description: Found by the 2026-10-12 reality check. Of the last 30 CI runs on main, 19 failed or were cancelled; run 38277425775 failed the e2e families native_host and automotive_watchdog, which passed on neighbouring commits. Some failures were real regressions fixed later, some may be timing-dependent tests (live POSIX, real sockets, wall-clock watchdogs). A flaky gate trains everyone to rerun until green, which hides real regressions. Work: list every failed job on main in the last 3 days with gh, classify each as real regression (cite fixing commit) vs flaky; for each flaky test, find the nondeterminism (timing assumptions, shared ports, /tmp collisions, ordering) and fix it in the test or code; never by adding retries or loosening assertions.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A classified list of failed main jobs (last 3 days) is in the bead comments, each with cause
- [ ] Each flaky test fixed at its root cause (no retry loops, no widened timeouts without a stated physical reason)
- [ ] The fixed e2e families pass 20/20 consecutive runs on a worker (cite the run)

comments.author: BlueRaven
comments.text:
[bd-9kll.10.9] Classified failures, every non-success push run on main, 2026-10-11 06:21 UTC .. 2026-10-12 16:26 UTC (26 runs, from `gh run list` + per-job logs via the jobs API).

Result: no timing flake. Every failure has a deterministic code, test or process cause and a fixing commit; no run went green by rerun. Nothing was retried, no assertion was loosened.

CLASS A. Real test bug: live-lane tests assumed wall-clock timing (6 runs)
- Runs 38117784936, 38118266129, 38118666129, 38118685163, 38118706904, 38118713922
- Lanes: compiler matrix (gcc/clang/clang-21, POSIX) "Unit suite, live POSIX (DETERMINISTIC=0)", sanitizers test-tsan and test-asan-live. The same five lanes failed in all six runs.
- Cause: the race_timeout and hedge wake tests ran on the real clock in the live build.
- Fix: a1539f3 (the tests run on the virtual clock in live builds too). Run 38136038083 (a1539f3) is green.

CLASS B. Real analyzer findings: check job, "Static analysis (section 10.7)" (9 runs)
- 38174517831, 38177777356, 38177782775, 38179461625, 38180492079, 38181748029, 38191576876 -> f293568 (two findings in the retry code)
- 38207309450, 38215366507 -> 266611b (unused reads in the authorization negative control)
- The check job fails, so 12 other jobs are skipped: one finding hides every other lane. Each run's finding is deterministic for its SHA.
- Mapping by lane/step and commit time; the individual findings of the first seven runs were not re-fetched.

CLASS C. Process/policy: "Lint (anti-butchering proof block)" (4 runs)
- 38181712737 (8227ffaa), 38204470769 (179e11ac), 38215071534 (352b9372), 38248217550 (74e5d4a0)
- The gate judges every commit message in the pushed range, so one commit without a valid Guarantee Impact block fails the range, deterministically.
- Not a code fix and not flaky. Mitigation: run `tools/ci/check_anti_butchering.sh` on the range before a push (the Landing procedure).

CLASS D. Real test bug: x87 precision under -m32 (3 runs)
- 38198308621, 38221729485, 38223422520: lane "32-bit x86 (-m32)" / "Unit suite (-m32)"
- Fix: 09328d1 (retry_policy_constructors_are_rusts compares the jitter with the literal rounded to double, so it passes under x87). Run 38225558081 (the first push after it) is green.
- 38198308621 matched by lane and step; its log was not re-fetched.

CLASS E. Real test bug (uninitialized forged permit obligation) + whole-run cancellation (2 runs)
- 38219165278 (e03ec463): failures in tsan unit suite, -m32, MSVC (CORE, WIN32), QEMU mips/mipsel/aarch64/armv7 unit suites; the rest cancelled.
- 38220166550 (841946a7): failures in MSVC (CORE, WIN32) and QEMU mipsel unit suites; 25 other jobs cancelled.
- Fix: 1af9626 (test(channel): initialize the forged permit obligation); the -m32 part is class D (09328d1).
- The cancellations are whole-run (all remaining jobs of two pushes 11 minutes apart). ci.yml has no `concurrency:` group, so nothing in the workflow cancels a run: these were cancelled from outside (manual / API). I did NOT add a concurrency group: it would explain no run here, and a main push must never be cancelled by a later one (the release gate needs evidence at the exact SHA).

CLASS F. Real regression: empty scenario rule tags (1 run)
- 38248717907 (aecbf6bf): conformance, "Oracle schemas (vocabulary v2, scenario DSL v2, example scenarios)".
- Fix: 84ca5f4 (supply real rule tags for the actor and race witnesses). Run 38250744794 (84ca5f4) is green.

CLASS G. Real regression: mixed-mode link refused by the build identity check (1 run)
- 38277425775 (e08cacb3): e2e scenario suite, native_host and automotive_watchdog. e08cacb (bd-9kll.10.8) made asx_runtime_init refuse a caller/library with a different profile, codec or DETERMINISTIC value; both families linked the shared build/lib/libasx.a built in another mode.
- Fix: 78a280e (each family builds its own library in its own BUILD_DIR). Run 38285643322 (the first push after it) is green.

Totals: A 6 + B 9 + C 4 + D 3 + E 2 + F 1 + G 1 = 26.

Hardening from the audit of the remaining families (commits below; neither explains a recorded failing run):
- e0b39f9 tests/e2e/posix_adapter_smoke.sh builds into ${E2E_BUILD_DIR}/posix-adapter-smoke. It was the one family left that rebuilt the shared build/ with PROFILE=POSIX DETERMINISTIC=0; any family run after it would hit the class G refusal. Same defect as run 38277425775.
- 1c3cc88 tests/e2e/e2e_posix_adapter_smoke.c wait_result hang guard 200 -> 10000 polls (200 ms -> 10 s of 1 ms sleeps). Stated physical reason: a descheduled worker thread on a loaded runner must not read as a lost result. The success path and every assertion are unchanged.

Audited, no change: tests/e2e/http_robustness.sh. It polls readiness (no fixed sleep for startup); its elapsed-time assertions are bounded by ASX_E2E_HTTP_SLACK_MS (default 1500 ms) and the lane is DETERMINISTIC=0 by design. No recorded run failed there, so changing it would be speculative.

Open (needs a worker, not run here): the acceptance criterion "the fixed e2e families pass 20/20 consecutive runs on a worker" for native_host, automotive_watchdog, posix_adapter_smoke.

title: [RP] Native record/replay: reproduce real native-mode failures exactly in the lab
description:
## Why
The README promises: "Reproduce production failures exactly". Today determinism holds only for
lab runs whose inputs are already deterministic. Nothing records a native run's nondeterministic
boundary inputs (readiness, reads, clock, entropy, signals, blocking completions, process exits)
or replays them.

## Done when
- A native HTTP server run under load with client resets and a SIGTERM drain is recorded.
- It replays bit-exactly in the lab 100/100 times.

- The journal survives a crash and restart.

title: RP1 Native boundary journal: record every nondeterministic input of a live run (readiness, reads, accepts, clock, entropy, signals, blocking completions, exits)
description:
## Why
The README promises "Reproduce production failures exactly" and "Every failure can be
reproduced". Determinism is currently demonstrated only for lab runs whose inputs are already
deterministic. A live (native) run's nondeterminism comes from its boundary inputs, and nothing
records them. `src/runtime/hindsight.c` has a 256-entry ring and a boundary taxonomy, but it isn't
persisted or replayable.

## Design
- A journal, `asx_journal`, with a versioned binary format (little-endian, length-prefixed
  records, SHA-256 chain every K records). Each record is a (trace seq, boundary kind, payload).
- Boundary kinds:
  - reactor readiness set (fd/handle IDs remapped to stable journal IDs);
  - read/recv results: bytes, or length plus hash in "shape" mode;
  - write/send partial lengths;
  - accept/connect results;
  - clock reads;
  - entropy draws;
  - signal deliveries;
  - blocking-pool completion order;
  - process exit statuses;
  - DNS results.
- Recording is a runtime option. Storage goes to a user sink (file, ring, flash) with per-profile
  defaults: RAM ring on ROUTER, with bounded flash writes.
- Overhead budget: with recording on, ≤ 10% throughput loss on the HTTP keep-alive bench (P1).

## Tests
- Unit tests per record type.
- A journal round-trip test.
- An overhead bench.

title: RP2 Lab replay backend: substitute every native boundary from the journal under the lab clock; report first divergent boundary
description:
## Plan
1. A replay backend implements the net, fs, process, signal, clock, entropy and blocking hooks
   by serving recorded results in sequence.
2. The replay scheduler runs in deterministic mode, and the canonical digest must equal the
   recorded run's rolling digest (RB1).
3. If the journal diverges (a requested operation doesn't match the next record) or is exhausted,
   stop with a report: trace seq, expected boundary, actual request.
4. Tools: `asx replay <journal>` CLI and `asx_journal_replay()` API.

## Tests
- Record → replay digest equality on unit scenarios.
- Divergence detection with a tampered journal.
- Exhaustion handling.

title: RP3 E2E proof: record a real native HTTP server under load + resets + SIGTERM drain; replay bit-exactly 100/100; reproduce a captured race
description:
## Plan
`tests/e2e/native_record_replay.sh`:
1. Start a native HTTP/1.1 server with recording on.
2. Drive load: curl and Python clients, keep-alive, injected client resets, mid-request
   disconnects.
3. Send SIGTERM to trigger the drain.
4. Replay the journal 100 times in the lab and assert an identical rolling digest every time.
5. Plant a deliberate order-dependent bug behind `-DASX_TEST_RACE`, record until it triggers,
   and show that replay reproduces it at the same trace seq 100/100.

JSONL logs include the journal hash, the digests, and the divergence seq if any.

## Success
Green in CI's native lane (POSIX live), with artifacts uploaded.

description:
## Why
The plan's "Crash/Restart Replay Continuity Gate" (§10.6) is currently satisfied by `continuity_restart.sh` with no
native journal. A real crash loses in-flight state unless the journal is persisted correctly.

1. Per-profile persistence policy: POSIX uses fsync every N records or at a time interval; ROUTER

   watchdog-aligned flush.

   prefix, which yields the digest prefix matching the recorded checkpoints.

- POSIX: asx_posix_journal_file_* (src/platform/posix/journal_posix.c): write(2) sink, fsync(2) commit, O_EXCL create.
- EMBEDDED_ROUTER: asx_journal_flash: RAM ring, writes only whole committed prefixes, only when min_flush bytes wait, never beyond wear_budget/area; at budget the stream stays in RAM until the ring fills, then the journal is incomplete and flash keeps its prefix.
- FREESTANDING/CORE/HFT/AUTOMOTIVE/WIN32: caller sink + commit_fn. asx_journal_profile_store() names it.

Format v2: CHAIN payload 48 bytes (hash, trace events, trace digest), hash covers the trace bytes; a window closed by an off-thread record, and finish's chain, carry zeros and no ASX_JOURNAL_REC_TRACE_CHECKPOINT flag. Reader exposes chain_end_pos/seq/records.

Recovery replay (journal_replay.h): asx_replay_open_prefix / asx_journal_replay_prefix serve the committed prefix of a cut or damaged stream, verify each window's trace checkpoint at the window's last record (DIVERGED "trace checkpoint"), end at the cut with ASX_REPLAY_E_CUT and the seq of the first uncommitted record; a program that ends inside the prefix is a cut. scheduler.c: a failed active replay ends the run at the next round (ASX_E_REPLAY_MISMATCH), one-line line-neutral edit; without it a task treating a refusal as "try again" spins for ever. asx replay prints the prefix (text + json).

Tests: test_journal.c (+12), test_journal_replay.c (+9, 2 live), cli_smoke.sh (+1). E2E: tests/e2e/native_crash_continuity.sh, make test-e2e-native-crash-continuity, family GATE-E2E-CRASH-CONTINUITY: reference run replays exactly; 50 seeded kill offsets (ASX_E2E_KILL_POINTS, ASX_E2E_SEED) with SIGKILL from the recorder's own sink at that byte (file exactly that long, torn tail), each survivor's replay ends REPLAY_CUT at the seq the prefix names, every committed record served, no native network call, last verified checkpoint equals the recorder's logged one; a damaged byte ends the prefix before its window.

Not done: planted -DASX_TEST_RACE control, fs results, WIN32 file store, RP1 overhead bench; SIGKILL cannot inflict kernel crash/power loss (the fsync's job). First-run suspects: DIVERGED "trace checkpoint" (a trace event between an adapter's OS call and its journal note), kill offsets not reached (cc.runs_were_killed), timing loops in the script.

plain C CI across every profile:
- spawn-order permutation, no-op task insertion and budget-meet nesting;
- cancel monotonicity;
- real profile substitution (replacing the fake profile-parity gate);
- real codec round-trip of runtime-produced traces;
- worker-count, time-scaling and replay invariance;

title: R1 Enforce R1/R2/R3 resource-class limits at runtime (currently only range-validated; arenas fixed for every class)
description:
## Bug
The README's "Resource Classes" table (L483-494) promises concrete per-class limits. For R1:
4 regions, 16 tasks, 32 timers, 16 obligations, 8 channels, 64 trace events. R2 and R3 scale up.

In reality:
- `src/runtime/hooks.c:91` and `src/runtime/profile_compat.c:176` only range-check the class.
- The real capacity is the compile-time arena for **every** class: 8 regions, 64 tasks,
  128 obligations, 16 channels.
- The resource-pressure gate fills `ASX_MAX_*`, not the class limit.

So an R1 deployment can use 64 tasks, and the "deterministic exhaustion at class limit" promise
is false.

## Fix
1. Each `asx_runtime` carries the effective class limits (from the class table, ≤ arena sizes).
2. Every allocation path (region, task, timer, obligation, channel, trace store) checks the class
   limit first and returns the documented exhaustion status. Failure-atomic: no partial mutation.
3. Alternatively, a compile-time class selects the arena sizes (`ASX_CLASS_R1` sets `ASX_MAX_*`),
   with a runtime check for the configured class ≤ the compiled one. Pick one approach and
   document it.
4. Extend `make resource-pressure-gate` to hit the class limits for R1/R2/R3 and assert the exact
   status and snapshot.

## Tests
- Per class × resource: fill to the limit; the next allocation fails with the exact status; the
  snapshot is unchanged.
- Digest parity across classes for scenarios within the R1 limits (M5).

title: R3 Footprint gate: release builds per profile/class measured in CI vs owner-approved targets (+ ASX_KERNEL_ONLY build per D6)
description:
## Problem
Plan §11 footprint targets:
- CORE kernel-only < 64 KB (hard < 128 KB);
- EMBEDDED_ROUTER with trace < 128 KB (hard < 256 KB).

These have never been measured in CI; `size-gate` isn't in CI. The debug CORE archive today is
712 KB text and 1.46 MB BSS. A release build was not measured, and the tree now includes HTTP,
WebSocket, RaptorQ, SHA and more. README L1886 claims "200-400 KB" and "R1 RAM under 64 KB",
both unverified.

## Plan
1. **Owner decision D6.** Either add an `ASX_KERNEL_ONLY` build that links only kernel modules
   (core, runtime kernel, channel, time, sync), which plausibly meets the targets, or restate the
   targets. Record the decision.
2. **Measure.** `make size-report` produces per profile × class × {debug, release} figures:
   - text/data/bss per object file, via `size` per `.o`;
   - totals;
   - linked footprint for a minimal app (the quickstart), which is what users pay.
3. **Gate.** Put `size-gate` in CI, observe-only first, then blocking, with baselines refreshed
   under the governance in `tools/ci/size_cold_start_baselines.json`.
4. **README.** Footprint numbers are generated from the report.

## Success
The report runs in CI, the targets are met or restated with owner sign-off, and the README
numbers are generated.

title: P1 C-vs-Rust comparative benchmark harness mirroring asupersync benches/runtime_vs_tokio.rs (same host, same minute, cv%)
description:
## Why
There is no comparative evidence. Rust publishes per-op p50 numbers from
`/dp/asupersync/benches/runtime_vs_tokio.rs` (README "Measured against tokio", 2026-10-05):

| Workload | Rust asupersync |
|---|---|
| spawn+join, current-thread | 3.0-7.1 µs |
| yield, current-thread | 0.30-0.57 µs |
| mpsc ping-pong, current-thread | 1.26-1.76 µs |
| TCP request/response | 30-44K round trips/s |
| HTTP/1.1 keep-alive GET | 22K req/s on 1 connection |

The C port has only self-benchmarks (`tests/bench/bench_runtime.c`). The C runtime is
single-threaded with static arenas, so it may be much faster per operation. That should be
measured, not assumed.

## Plan
1. In `tools/twin_run` (or a sibling `tools/perf_compare`), a Criterion-style harness that runs,
   in **one process**, the same workloads on asupersync (current-thread runtime and lab) and on
   `asx` (via FFI, release build, `-O2`):
   - spawn+join;
   - yield;
   - mpsc ping-pong;
   - cancel latency (request → completed);
   - timer churn (arm/cancel 10k);
   - region open/close;
   - TCP RR over loopback (POSIX live);
   - HTTP/1.1 keep-alive.
2. Report p50/p95/p99, throughput and **cv%**. Results with cv > 5% are flagged as noise.
3. Both engines run in the same minute on the same rch worker. Record the host fingerprint.
4. History ratchet in `.bench-history/<bench>.latest.json`, with keep-gate thresholds: primary
   −3%, geomean −5%, per-row −10%.
5. Profile-first: any optimization work cites a flamegraph frame ≥ 0.1% self-time. Record
   rejected ideas in `docs/progress/perf-negative-results.md`.

## Success
A published table (artifact plus a README section generated by P3) with honest numbers and cv,
re-runnable with one command (`rch exec -- make perf-compare`).

title: E1 Embedded CI matrix actually runs: fix toolchain triplet mismatch, FAIL_ON_MISSING=1, enable QEMU, add RISC-V
description:
## Bug
`ci.yml`'s embedded-matrix job installs `*-linux-gnu-gcc` cross compilers, but the Makefile's
embedded targets look for `*-openwrt-linux-musl-gcc`. With `FAIL_ON_MISSING=0`, all three targets
are **skipped**, and the job would "pass" with no cross build at all. QEMU execution is disabled
(`RUN_QEMU_IN_MATRIX=0`). There is no RISC-V lane, although the README (L1720, L1859) claims
mipsel, armv7, aarch64 and RISC-V plus QEMU.

## Fix
1. Make the triplets consistent. Either use musl cross toolchains (musl.cc tarballs, or zig cc as
   a cross driver, which is honest and reproducible) or the `*-linux-gnu` toolchains with an
   explicit note.
2. `FAIL_ON_MISSING=1` in CI.
3. Enable QEMU user-mode runs of the unit-smoke and conformance interpreter on each target.
4. Add riscv64 and the big-endian MIPS target (see E6).

## Success
The embedded job actually compiles and runs on each listed arch, with logs showing the
cross-compiler path and the QEMU run per target.

description:
## Problem
The README claims WASM and browser support (L140, L508, L1638-1648), but no wasm32 target exists
in the Makefile, CMake or CI. `ASX_PROFILE_BROWSER` is compiled only for the host. Bead
`bd-1eqo.16` (browser runtime) was closed anyway (see W0.6). Plan §10.7.4 calls a wasm
determinism oracle "high-value".

## Plan
1. Add `make build-wasm32` using clang `--target=wasm32-wasi` (wasi-sdk) for CORE and BROWSER.
   Fix any portability issues that come up.
2. Build the conformance interpreter CLI for WASI. Run the fixture corpus under wasmtime and
   compare digests with x86_64.
3. Decide (D-later) whether to ship JS bindings for the browser profile, and track that separately.
4. README: accurate wasm statement.

## Success
The CI lane builds and replays the corpus under wasmtime with identical digests.

title: E5 Sanitizer lanes in CI: ASan+UBSan (CORE and POSIX-live), TSan (blocking pool, cross-thread waker, signal self-pipe)
description:
## Problem
No sanitizer lane runs in CI. There is no Makefile ASan target; `build_asan.sh` writes to an
in-repo `build_asan/`. The audit found a real UBSan bug (RB6) and an ASan test bug. The POSIX-live
mode has real threads (blocking pool, cross-thread waker lock, signal self-pipe) and has never run
under TSan.

## Plan
1. Add `make test-asan` and `make test-tsan`, with `BUILD_DIR` overridable and output under
   `build/asan`.
2. CI lanes:
   - ASan+UBSan on CORE and POSIX-live unit suites, plus the e2e subset;
   - TSan on POSIX-live suites that exercise the threads.
3. Use `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1`.

## Success
The lanes are green. RB6 is fixed first.

title: E6 Cross-architecture semantic identity: replay Rust-captured fixture corpus under QEMU (aarch64, armv7, mipsel, mips BE, riscv64, i386) + wasm32; digests must match x86_64
description:
## Why
The embedded-first promise depends on the same semantics on router SoCs. Many routers (ath79 and
similar) are **big-endian MIPS**, and the BIN codec, digest code and handle packing are exactly
where endianness bugs hide. The repo has `robustness_endian.sh`, but no cross-arch replay of a
semantic corpus.

## Plan
1. Cross-build the conformance interpreter CLI (W1.5) for each arch, statically linked.
2. Under qemu-user, replay the full fixture corpus (W1.7). Compare canonical digests and
   snapshots against the x86_64 run.
3. CI: on push run aarch64 and mips (BE); nightly run all of them.

## Success
Identical digests across all architectures. Any difference is a bug, fixed with a regression
test.

description:

The C port parses untrusted input: HTTP/1.1, WebSocket, DNS, the JSON/BIN codecs, RaptorQ and

fuzzing against Rust, and no `-fanalyzer`/clang-tidy lanes.

Every parser has an ASan+UBSan libFuzzer harness, differential parser fuzzing against Rust is
clean, 24 h soaks are clean, and a regression corpus is replayed in CI.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: leading empty line (C ignores per RFC 9112 2.2, Rust rejects)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2, tools/ci/parser_differential.py): asupersync 5e60b1c4c (`Http1Codec`) rejects a request that has an empty line before the request line; the C parser (`asx_http_parser`, HTTP request) accepts it.

Family: `c-accepts/rust-rejects:BadRequestLine [leading-empty-line]`. 59 of 2000 inputs (seed 1) and 922 of 20000 (seed 7, `--c-require-host 0`) diverge this way; it is the largest family and it masks every other difference on those inputs.

Minimized input (CRLF, then a request):

    \r\nGET / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n          (C with Host not required)
    \r\nGET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost:\r\n\r\n  (C defaults)

- Rust: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "BadRequestLine"}`
- C: `complete`, method GET, target `/`, version HTTP/1.1, consumed 20 bytes (the leading CRLF is skipped)

Classification: **Rust deviation from a SHOULD; C follows the RFC.** RFC 9112 section 2.2: "a server that is expecting to receive and parse a request-line SHOULD ignore at least one empty line (CRLF) received prior to the request-line". The C parser tolerates leading empty lines by design (`ASX_HTTP_MAX_LEADING_EMPTY_LINES`, include/asx/asx_config.h; checked at src/net/http.c).

Suggested action: keep the C behaviour; record it as an intentional semantic delta in docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md (C is more lenient where the RFC says SHOULD) and report it upstream (low). If fidelity to asupersync is wanted instead, setting that limit to 0 makes the C parser reject a leading empty line; add a fixture in tests/conformance either way.

Reproduce: `twin_run parse-diff http-request FILE` (tools/twin_run, `parse-diff`) and the C driver (`make parser-diff-build`, build/parser-differential/http_request FILE).

title: parser-diff HTTP request: origin-form target starting // (C accepts, Rust rejects)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): an origin-form request target that starts with `//` is rejected by asupersync 5e60b1c4c and accepted by the C parser.

Family: `c-accepts/rust-rejects:BadRequestLine [target=double-slash]`. 6 of 2000 inputs (seed 1), 4+ of 20000 (seed 7).

Minimized input:

    GET // HTTP/1.1\r\na:\r\n\r\n       (and with Host: for the C default)

- Rust: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "BadRequestLine"}`
- C: `complete`, method GET, target `//`

Rust's rule (src/http/h1/codec.rs, `validate_request_target_name`): "origin-form MUST NOT start with // (ambiguous or potential smuggling vector)". RFC 9110/9112 define absolute-path as `1*( "/" segment )`, which allows an empty first segment, so `//` is syntactically valid there; RFC 3986 path-absolute does not allow it, and a `//x` target is read as a network-path reference by many components.

Classification: **C lenient relative to Rust; Rust is a deliberate hardening.** The port's contract is Rust semantics (semantic delta budget 0), so unless the owner records a decision to keep the C behaviour, the C parser should reject a target that starts with `//`.

Suggested action: reject `//`-prefixed origin-form targets in src/net/http.c with `ASX_HTTP_PERR_BAD_TARGET`, add the minimized request as a unit case in tests/unit/net and a fixture; then remove this family from tools/ci/parser_differential_known.txt.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: absolute-form target with empty authority (C accepts, RFC 9110 4.2.1 MUST reject)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): an absolute-form request target with an empty authority (`http:///p`) is rejected by asupersync 5e60b1c4c and accepted by the C parser.

Family: `c-accepts/rust-rejects:BadRequestLine [target=absolute-empty-authority]`. 2 of 2000 inputs (seed 1).

Original input and minimized input:

    GET http:///p HTTP/1.0\r\nUser-Agent: t\r\n\r\n
    GET a:/// HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n          (minimized; the scheme is irrelevant to the C parser)

- Rust: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "BadRequestLine"}` (src/http/h1/codec.rs: "absolute-form MUST have a non-empty authority", br-asupersync-w6u4cn)
- C: `complete`, method GET, target `http:///p`

Classification: **C bug (RFC 9110 section 4.2.1).** "A sender MUST NOT generate an 'http' URI with an empty host identifier. A recipient that processes such a URI reference MUST reject it as invalid." RFC 9112 section 3.2.2 requires absolute-form for proxies; a recipient of `http:///p` must answer 400.

Suggested action: in src/net/http.c's request-target validation, reject an absolute-form target whose authority is empty (the text between `://` and the next `/`, `?` or `#`) with `ASX_HTTP_PERR_BAD_TARGET`; unit test with the minimized input; remove the family from tools/ci/parser_differential_known.txt.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: CONNECT authority with empty port (C accepts, Rust rejects)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): a CONNECT request whose authority-form target has an empty port (`a:`) is rejected by asupersync 5e60b1c4c and accepted by the C parser.

Family: `c-accepts/rust-rejects:BadRequestLine [target=authority-empty-port]`. 9 of 2000 inputs (seed 1), 1+ of 20000 (seed 7).

Minimized input:

    CONNECT a: HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n         (a Host: line for the C default)

- Rust: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "BadRequestLine"}` (`validate_connect_authority`: the port must be non-empty and all digits)
- C: `complete`, method CONNECT, target `a:`

Classification: **C lenient; spec ambiguity resolved by Rust.** RFC 9112 section 3.2.3 authority-form is `uri-host ":" port`, and RFC 3986 defines `port = *DIGIT`, so an empty port is grammatical; RFC 9110 section 9.3.6 says the target "consists of only the host name and port number of the tunnel destination", which an empty port is not.

Suggested action: align the C parser with Rust (a CONNECT target needs a non-empty numeric port): `ASX_HTTP_PERR_BAD_TARGET`; unit test with the minimized input; remove the family from the known list.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: duplicate Host (Rust accepts, C rejects per RFC 9112 3.2)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): a request with two Host header fields is accepted by asupersync 5e60b1c4c and rejected by the C parser (`ASX_HTTP_PERR_DUPLICATE_HOST`, 400).

Family: `rust-accepts/c-rejects:duplicate-host`. 24 of 2000 inputs (seed 1), 360 of 20000 (seed 7); includes `Host`/`host`/`HOST` case variants.

Minimized input:

    GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost:\r\nHost:\r\n\r\n

- Rust: `complete`, headers `[["Host",""],["Host",""]]`, consumed 32
- C: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "duplicate-host"}`

Classification: **Rust deviation from a MUST; C is correct.** RFC 9112 section 3.2: "A server MUST respond with a 400 (Bad Request) status code to any HTTP/1.1 request message that lacks a Host header field and to any request message that contains more than one Host header field line or a Host header field with an invalid field value." At 5e60b1c4c the HTTP/1 codec and server never inspect Host (grep of src/http/h1 finds no check), so a request with conflicting Host lines reaches the application (host-confusion).

Suggested action: keep the C behaviour; record the delta (C stricter) in docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md; report upstream to asupersync (P2: host confusion). If the C parser must stay fidelity-exact to the Rust codec instead, `limits.require_host = 0` removes the missing-Host half only; duplicate Host is rejected regardless, so that would need a limit.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: HTTP/1.1 without Host (Rust accepts, C rejects per RFC 9112 3.2)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): an HTTP/1.1 request without a Host header field is accepted by asupersync 5e60b1c4c and rejected by the C parser with its default limits (`require_host = 1`, `ASX_HTTP_PERR_MISSING_HOST`, 400).

Family: `rust-accepts/c-rejects:missing-host`. 17 of 2000 inputs (seed 1, C defaults). With `ASX_DIFF_REQUIRE_HOST=0` (or `--c-require-host 0`) the family disappears.

Minimized input:

    GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n

- Rust: `complete`, headers `[]`, consumed 18
- C: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "missing-host"}`

Classification: **policy / layering difference; Rust deviates from a MUST.** RFC 9112 section 3.2 requires 400 for an HTTP/1.1 request that lacks Host. The C parser enforces it in the parser (configurable); asupersync's HTTP/1 codec and server do not check Host at this rev. C is RFC-correct. Same upstream observation as the duplicate-Host family.

Suggested action: keep the C default; the differential's CI step runs with both configurations so the Host policy cannot mask other differences. Record in docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md; report upstream together with the duplicate-Host family.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: extension method (Rust accepts, C closed set returns 501)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): a request whose method is a valid token but not one of the nine in `asx_http_method` (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS, CONNECT, TRACE) is accepted by asupersync 5e60b1c4c (`Method::Extension`) and rejected by the C parser (`ASX_HTTP_PERR_UNKNOWN_METHOD`, 501).

Family: `rust-accepts/c-rejects:unknown-method`. 18 of 2000 inputs (seed 1), 157 of 20000 (seed 7). Includes lowercase `get`, `G#ET`, `T`.

Minimized input:

    a / HTTP/1.1\r\na:\r\n\r\n

- Rust: `complete`, method `a`, target `/`, headers `[["a",""]]`
- C: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "unknown-method"}`

Classification: **by design (closed method set); both are permitted by RFC 9110 section 9.1** ("An origin server that receives a request method that is unrecognized or not implemented SHOULD respond with the 501 (Not Implemented) status code"). The difference is real for fidelity: asupersync hands an extension method to the application, the C kernel cannot represent one.

Suggested action: owner decision. Either extend `asx_http_method` (and the parser) with an extension-method representation for fidelity, or record the closed set as an accepted delta in docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md. Until decided the family stays in the known list.

title: parser-diff HTTP request: chunk extension with no name '5;' (Rust accepts, C rejects)
description:
Found by differential parser fuzzing (bd-9kll.16.2): a chunk-size line with a bare semicolon and no extension name (`5;`) is accepted by asupersync 5e60b1c4c and rejected by the C parser (`ASX_HTTP_PERR_BAD_CHUNK_EXTENSION`, 400).

Family: `rust-accepts/c-rejects:bad-chunk-extension`. Found in the larger campaign (10 of 20000 inputs, seed 7, `--c-require-host 0`); the 2000-input run did not reach it.

Minimized input:

    POST / HTTP/1.1\r\na:\r\nTransfer-Encoding:chunked\r\n\r\n5;\r\naaaaa\r\n0\r\n\r\n

- Rust: `complete`, method POST, body `aaaaa` (5 bytes)
- C: `{"kind": "error", "detail": "bad-chunk-extension"}`

Classification: **Rust lenient; C follows the grammar.** RFC 9112 section 7.1.1: `chunk-ext = *( BWS ";" BWS chunk-ext-name [ BWS "=" BWS chunk-ext-val ] )`; the name is required, so `5;` is not a chunk-ext. Chunk-extension handling is a request-smuggling surface, so accepting a malformed one is the less safe side.

Suggested action: keep the C behaviour; record the delta in docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md and report upstream (low). Other shapes (`5;ext=1`, `5;x="y"`, `05`, `5 `, `a`) were in the corpus and the two parsers agreed on them.

title: X0 Owner decisions D1-D7 needed for the bridge program (record in docs/OWNER_DECISION_LOG.md)
description:
## Decisions (each with a recommendation)
| ID | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | Align cancel-kind ordinals with Rust (`LinkedExit=10`, `Shutdown=9`; currently C has 7 and 10). This is an ABI break. | Align now (AGENTS.md: no backcompat), **and** encode kinds by name in the canonical vocabulary. |
| **D2** | Default leak policy: PANIC (Rust parity) vs LOG (current C). | PANIC everywhere. The policy is semantic; users may override it explicitly. |
| **D3** | Provide unbounded MPSC (Rust has it). | Yes, but forbidden by capability in profiles declaring `ASX_FORBID_UNBOUNDED_QUEUE`; "unbounded" means bounded by the arena, failure-atomic. |
| **D4** | TLS (currently a plaintext passthrough named TLS). | A hook-based `asx_tls_provider` interface (BearSSL/mbedTLS/wolfSSL adapters outside the dependency-free core), and rename the passthrough to `asx_tls_null_provider` (test-only). |
| **D5** | QUIC, gRPC, DB, messaging and distributed in-memory models. | Relabel them as deterministic lab models, excluded from README feature claims, with explicit `EXCLUDED` / `MODEL-ONLY` surface rows. |
| **D6** | Footprint targets (CORE kernel < 64 KB). | Add an `ASX_KERNEL_ONLY` build that meets them; otherwise restate the targets. |
| **D7** | Deletions needed by the program. | Approve explicitly, item by item: the tracked ELF binaries (W0.7), the legacy fixtures after the corpus is regenerated (W1.7), `tools/rust_fuzz_target` and `tools/zero_drift_extractor.py` after replacement, `timer_wheel.c` if superseded (T4). |

labels `decision-D1` … `decision-D7` are unblocked.

title: X1 Honest TLS: asx_tls_provider hook interface; rename plaintext passthrough to null provider; adapter example out of core
description:
## Problem
`src/net/tls.c` is a plaintext passthrough ("Real crypto is deferred") behind an API named TLS. A
user can believe traffic is encrypted when it isn't. Rust has real TLS (`/dp/asupersync/src/tls`,

   named `asx_tls_null_provider` and documented as test-only.

   dependency, or document it.
4. The HTTP server and client use the provider when configured.

- No provider → explicit error.
- The null provider round trip is labelled test-only.
- An adapter example builds in a separate optional CI lane.

title: X2 Relabel QUIC/gRPC/DB/messaging/distributed/web/transport/remote in-memory models; register MODEL-ONLY rows; remove README feature claims
description:
## Problem
These modules are in-memory models with no wire protocol:
- **QUIC** (`src/net/quic.c:109`): connect/accept just allocate a slot marked CONNECTED.
- **DB** (`src/net/db.c:127`): `asx_db_execute` returns empty results for every query; the
  `ASX_HAS_DB_*` flags are 0.
- **messaging**: Kafka is compiled out (`asx_config.h:116`); Redis, NATS and JetStream are absent.
- **gRPC, distributed, web, transport, remote**: in-memory.

Some are marked "partial" in the surface register, whose own vocabulary would call them
"stub-only".

## Plan (per D5)
1. Each module's header gets a clear banner: "Deterministic in-memory model for lab scenarios. No
   network protocol. Not a client/server implementation."
2. Register rows become `MODEL-ONLY` in `docs/DEFERRED_SURFACE_REGISTER.md` and FeatureUniverse
   (G3).
3. The README lists them under "Lab models", not as features.
4. Any API that implies success on a real network returns an explicit status.

No README or doc implies these are real protocol implementations.

title: X3 kqueue reactor backend for macOS/BSD (native POSIX live builds)
description:
## Why
POSIX live builds on non-Linux use poll(2), and process-exit waits there poll on a timer. Rust
has a kqueue reactor. macOS is a primary dev platform (AGENTS.md mentions a Mac host).

## Plan
