title: G5 Bind release publication to required evidence at the exact tagged SHA and verified installed artifacts
description:
Problem: release.yml builds archives, checks they are nonempty and publishes on v* tags, without requiring primary CI or performance evidence for that exact SHA. At audited SHA 1df1808d primary CI is green (38139207368) but perf-tail-deadline is red (38139207307); later HFT/size lanes are skipped. DEPLOYMENT_HARDENING already promises all required gates and checksum/signature/consumer smoke before a release. No published GitHub release was observed during this audit.

Deliverable: Define the release-required gate manifest using the kernel milestone contract. Bind every selected result and artifact to the tag's resolved commit and configuration; reject missing, stale, failed, cancelled or unexpectedly skipped required lanes. Optional/deferred lanes must have an explicit scoped rationale, never a silently absent check. Separate fast build/lab status from release readiness so a green evidence dashboard cannot override red SLO output. Resolve provenance of externally collected device evidence explicitly.

Verify archive checksums and signing bundles/provenance, then install/extract in an isolated retained staging directory and compile/run a public-header consumer and CLI health probe for the shipped target. Wire this validation before publication. Make dry-run output concrete and reviewable. Do not publish a tag/release as part of implementation, silently loosen performance budgets, or delete staged files. Missing approval for a policy change remains a documented decision; technical verification proceeds independently.

Context and completion policy: This is the 2026-10-11 reality-check extension of bd-9kll, audited at C commit 1df1808d51ae5ca90c2fdd0c6a351e77091b9c3c. Implement manually in existing files where possible; preserve other agents' work and never delete any file without written owner permission. title: [W1] Honest differential oracle vs asupersync 0.6.0 (twin-run, DSL v2, real fixtures)
description:
## Why
The plan's central promise (plan §9) is Rust↔C conformance with pinned provenance. Today:
- no gate executes fixture ops;
- the capture tool fabricates events;
- provenance is 19,722 commits stale;
- the fuzz differential never runs.

Until a real oracle exists, every semantic fix is unverifiable and drift is invisible. This is
the critical path of the whole bridge program.

- **Pinned rebaseline** to `5e60b1c4c` (git rev pin, because 0.6.0 is not on crates.io).
- **Canonical semantic vocabulary v2.** Cancel kinds by name, outcomes carrying reasons, status
  mapping, snapshot schema, and the independence relation.
- **Scenario DSL v2** with scripted task-body step programs.

    - (c) exact trace under a forced/shared schedule;
  - asserts engine identities differ.
- **Fixture corpus** emitted by the harness, with real provenance.
- **Offline C replay** for CI machines without Rust.
- **Projection completeness test.**
- **Coverage-guided differential fuzzing.**
- **Nightly upstream-drift lane.**

- **A real syn-based constant extractor.**

title: Rebaseline Rust reference to asupersync 5e60b1c4c (0.6.0) with dual-baseline rebase record and non-destructive capture
description:
## Problem
- **The inventory is stale.** `docs/rust_baseline_inventory.json` pins `a9e737d8` (2026-03-12,
  v0.2.7-793), which is 19,722 commits behind `/dp/asupersync` HEAD `5e60b1c4c`.
- **The tools and fixtures disagree.** `tools/fixture_capture` and `tools/rust_fuzz_target` depend
  on `asupersync = "=0.5.0"` (crates.io), and the capture tool hardcodes commit `78b64636`
  (`main.rs:809`, asserted at `:871-874`). The fixtures still claim a9e737d8, because commit
  `91d3810` deliberately kept them.
- **0.6.0 isn't published.** crates.io max is 0.5.0; HEAD is pushed to origin/main.
- **Rebasing is blocked.**
  - `run_conformance.sh` (around `:449-453`) hard-fails any fixture whose provenance differs from
    the inventory.
  - `tools/ci/capture_rust_fixtures.sh` rewrites fixtures in place, which would destroy the
    hand-authored combinator fixtures and any staging.

## Plan
1. **Pin by git rev** in every Rust tool `Cargo.toml`:
   `asupersync = { git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "<full 40-char sha of 5e60b1c4c>", features = [...] }`.
   Capture the full SHA with `git -C /dp/asupersync rev-parse HEAD`. Commit `Cargo.lock`.
2. **Write the plan §1.1 dual-baseline rebase record**, `docs/rebase_records/2026-10-a9e737d8-to-5e60b1c4c.md`:
   - old and new inventories;
   - toolchain (`rustc -Vv` from the nightly actually used);
   - lock hash;
   - the delta classification policy (`intentional_upstream | c_regression | spec_defect |
     harness_defect`) and an owner sign-off field.
3. **Update `docs/rust_baseline_inventory.json`** to the new milestone, `M-beta-oracle`, keeping
   the old entry under history.
4. **Make `capture_rust_fixtures.sh` non-destructive:** write to
   `build/fixture_staging/<run_id>/`, diff against `fixtures/rust_reference/`, and promote only
   via an explicit `make fixtures-promote`, which prints the diff summary.
5. **Teach `run_conformance.sh` provenance enforcement** about the active milestone (single
   baseline per milestone, plan §9.5). Mixing generations is a hard fail.

## Success criteria
- Tools build against the pinned rev via rch (`rch exec -- cargo build --manifest-path tools/twin_run/Cargo.toml` once W1.4 exists; for now, the existing tools).
- The inventory and rebase record are committed.
- A dry capture writes only to staging.

logs JSONL.

title: Real Rust-vs-C differential fuzzing via twin_run: grammar over DSL v2, coverage on both engines, divergence = failure, minimized corpus
description:
## Problem
`tests/fuzz/fuzz_differential.c` treats divergences as "informational, not failures" (`:1296`).
- A failed Rust invocation only warns (`:1171`).
- `--fixtures-dir` is parsed but unused (`:1066,1079,1337`).
- CI never supplies `RUST_FUZZ_BINARY` (`ci.yml:652-654`; `Makefile:1535-1536` defaults it to
  empty).
- The Rust target (`tools/rust_fuzz_target`) makes channel, timer and quiescence ops no-ops
  (`:536-618`) and uses incompatible status numbers.

## Plan
1. In `tools/twin_run`, add a `fuzz` subcommand and a `cargo fuzz` target (libFuzzer via
   `arbitrary`) that generate DSL v2 scenarios from a grammar with weights per unit. Each scenario
   runs on both engines (FFI) and is compared in mode (a) and mode (b), plus mode (c) under a
   recorded schedule.
2. Divergence handling:
   - minimize with ddmin;
   - store it in `fixtures/fuzz_counterexamples/` with schema `asx.fuzz_counterexample.v2`;
   - classify it;
   - an unclassified divergence fails the run.
3. Coverage. Build `libasx.a` with `-fsanitize-coverage=trace-pc-guard` so libFuzzer sees C edges
   too. Add ASan/UBSan on the C side.
4. Retire `fuzz_differential.c`'s Rust path. It stays a C self-determinism fuzzer, renamed
   honestly to `fuzz-c-selfdeterminism`. Delete `tools/rust_fuzz_target` only with owner
   approval; otherwise mark it deprecated.
5. CI: a 5-minute smoke on push, with fixed seeds. Nightly runs a 2 h rch-offloaded campaign
   with corpus persistence.

## Success criteria
- A planted mutant (K1 `min` priority) is found by the fuzzer within 60 s from the seed corpus.
- Nightly runs are clean or produce classified counterexamples.
- `make fuzz-smoke` fails on any unclassified divergence.

title: Nightly upstream-drift lane: recapture against asupersync origin/main HEAD, diff vs pinned corpus, classify, auto-file beads
description:
## Why
The Rust reference moves fast: 1,077 kernel-path commits since February. Parity against a pinned
rev decays silently unless upstream drift is surfaced continuously.

## Plan
1. A nightly job (GitHub Actions schedule, or an rch cron on a worker) that:
   - checks out asupersync origin/main HEAD;
   - builds twin_run against it (path override);
   - captures the full DSL v2 corpus into staging;
   - diffs it against the pinned fixtures.
2. For each changed fixture:
   - compute a `mismatch_signature`;
   - de-duplicate against open beads;
   - file a bead labelled `upstream-delta`. It records the Rust commit range (`git log
     pinned..HEAD -- <files>`), the divergent rules and the minimal scenario.
3. A weekly triage (G4) classifies each delta as `intentional_upstream` (port it),
   `harness_defect` or `spec_defect`, and decides whether to bump the pin using the rebase
   protocol (W1.1).
4. Also run the syn extractor (W1.12) diff and the projection-completeness check (W1.6t) against
   HEAD. A new unprojected `TraceEvent` variant files a bead.

## Success criteria
The lane runs nightly and produces a report artifact. A synthetic upstream change, simulated by
patching a local checkout, produces exactly one bead.

Rust now ships a normative small-step semantics, `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`.
It has a **Canonical Rule Index** (lines 23-77) and rules in §3, for example:
- ENQUEUE, SCHEDULE-STEP, SPAWN, SCHEDULE, COMPLETE-OK, COMPLETE-ERR;
- CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CANCEL-DRAIN,
  CANCEL-FINALIZE;
- CLOSE-BEGIN, CLOSE-CANCEL-CHILDREN, CLOSE-CHILDREN-DONE, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER, CLOSE-COMPLETE;
- RESERVE, COMMIT, ABORT, LEAK.

It also has §1.11 scheduler lanes and §1.8 independence. Rust maps its own code to those rules in
`/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

## Plan
1. **Create `docs/C_REFINEMENT_MAP.md`**, mirroring Rust's map rule by rule. Columns:

   index. The comparator (W1.6) reports fixture coverage per rule against it.

title: Real syn-based zero-drift extractor: emit schemas/rust_kernel_constants.json from asupersync source; check C tables against it
description:
## Problem
`tools/zero_drift_extractor.py` (bead bd-3vt.10) "extracts" Rust structure from **embedded sample
Rust fragments** hardcoded in the Python file (`RUST_REGION_ENUM = """..."""`), not from
`/dp/asupersync`. It can never detect upstream drift. This is the same self-referential pattern
as the fixtures.

## Plan
1. **Write `tools/rust_extract/`**, a Rust crate using `syn`, that parses the pinned asupersync
   source and emits `schemas/rust_kernel_constants.json`:
   - enum variants with discriminants and ordinal order:
     - `TaskState`, `RegionState`, `ObligationState`, `ObligationKind`, `CancelKind`;
     - lane enums;
     - leak policy and escalation enums;
     - restart strategies and policies;
   - `CancelKind::severity()` / cleanup quota / priority tables, extracted from match arms;
   - `Budget::INFINITE` / `ZERO` / defaults;
   - mask depth;
   - cancel-streak limit;
   - attribution bounds (depth 16 / 4096 bytes);
   - supervision intensity defaults (3 per 60 s) and backoff (100 ms to 10 s, ×2);
   - timer-wheel geometry (levels, slots, tick);
   - max timer duration (7 days);
   - mailbox defaults (64);
   - the region/task transition tables, if they are expressible.

   record the source span.
2. **Add `make check-rust-constants`.** It compiles a C program that prints the corresponding C
   values and compares them against the JSON. Each mismatch names the C symbol and the Rust span.
3. **Retire the Python prototype.** Mark it deprecated and stop calling it; deletion needs owner
   approval.
4. **Feed the nightly drift lane** (W1.10) and FeatureUniverse (G3).

## Success criteria
- On the current tree, `make check-rust-constants` reports the known mismatches: budget priority

title: Lean/TLA crosswalk: map asupersync formal theorems/invariants to C witnesses (CBMC harnesses or property tests)
description:
## Why
Rust's formal assets:
- 189 Lean theorems and lemmas (`/dp/asupersync/formal/lean`), with theorem-to-rule traceability
  in `formal/lean/coverage/theorem_rule_traceability_ledger.json` and
  `invariant_theorem_test_link_map.json`;
- a TLA+ model (`formal/tla/Asupersync.tla`).

The C port's formal suite (`tests/formal/`: 6 CBMC harnesses, 6 algebraic suites, litmus) was
written independently. The budget algebra suite even proves the *old* priority semiring.

## Plan
1. **Write `docs/FORMAL_CROSSWALK.md`.** For each Lean theorem that states a kernel invariant,
   record:
   - the theorem name and file;
   - the statement in plain words;
   - the C witness: a CBMC harness (small bounded state), an algebraic property test, an
     invariant-suite assertion, or n/a with a reason;
   - the status.

   Examples: strengthen idempotence/monotonicity, bounded cleanup, obligation conservation (the
   Petri net / VASS accounting), quiescence implies no live obligations.
2. **Translate the TLA+ invariants** into C invariant-suite assertions run under the interpreter
   on every fixture.
3. **Fix the existing C formal suites** that encode drifted semantics (budget priority, after K1).
   Add CBMC harnesses for the new scheduler lane-selection function (after S1) and for the
   barrier round counter (after Y1).
4. **Run `formal-check` in CI** (it is currently not there).

- Every Lean theorem tagged as kernel-invariant in Rust's traceability ledger has a crosswalk row.

title: Statistical parity scoring: per-unit Beta lower bound, ratchet file, e-process divergence monitor; feeds README status
description:
## Why
"Parity" should be a quantified, conservative claim with a known confidence, not a point
estimate. Releases should ratchet so a unit's lower bound can never silently fall.

## Plan
1. For each semantic unit, the fuzz campaign (W1.9) reports N scenarios generated in that unit
   and D unclassified divergences.
2. Posterior: Beta(1 + N - D, 1 + D). Report the 95% lower credible bound, truncated to 6
   decimals. Emit `build/conformance/parity_scores.json`.
3. Write `reports/parity_ratchet.json` (committed), holding each unit's last accepted lower
   bound. `make parity-ratchet` blocks if any unit's LB drops, unless a dated, owner-signed waiver
   exists in `reports/parity_waivers.json`.
4. For long campaigns, use an e-process monitor for the divergence rate (software-invariant
   parameters p₀ = 1e-6, λ = 0.9, α = 1e-3), with a mixture/betting martingale. Stop early when the
   e-value exceeds 1/α (Ville's inequality), which gives anytime validity. Log the e-value
   trajectory.
5. The W0.10 README status section reads `parity_scores.json`.

## Success criteria
- A unit test checks the Beta lower-bound computation against reference values.
- The e-process rejects a synthetic 1e-3 divergence stream within the expected sample count and
  stays below threshold on a clean stream.
- The ratchet blocks a lowered LB.

title: CancelKind ordinals differ from Rust: C declares LinkedExit seventh (Rust: ParentCancelled 7, ResourceUnavailable 8, Shutdown 9, LinkedExit 10)
description:
## Drift
Rust 5e60b1c4c declares `CancelKind` (src/types/cancel.rs:264) as User, Timeout, Deadline,
PollQuota, CostBudget, FailFast, RaceLost, ParentCancelled, ResourceUnavailable, Shutdown,
LinkedExit. The discriminants are 0-10, and Rust derives Ord, Hash and serde on the enum.

C's `asx_cancel_kind` (include/asx/asx_ids.h:149-161) declares LinkedExit seventh. As a result:

| kind | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedExit | 10 | 7 |
| ParentCancelled | 7 | 8 |
| ResourceUnavailable | 8 | 9 |
| Shutdown | 9 | 10 |

Severities and cleanup budgets match. Within each severity class the relative order is the same on
both sides, so comparisons that break severity ties by ordinal agree. The vocabulary and both
codecs encode kinds by name.

## Why it is not fixed yet
The C trace records the kind ordinal as the payload of `ASX_TRACE_REGION_CANCELLED` and
`ASX_TRACE_CANCEL_REQUEST` (src/runtime/cancellation.c:54, :258, :464). Reordering the enum
therefore changes every recorded trace digest of a run that cancels with ParentCancelled,
ResourceUnavailable, Shutdown or LinkedExit. That includes most region cancels, because children
see ParentCancelled. Do it together with the owner's pending trace-digest decision, and refresh the
recorded digests in the same change. The ABI check pins only `ASX_CANCEL_USER = 0`.

## Done when
`asx-conformance constants schemas/rust_kernel_constants.json` reports these five keys as OK, and
their KNOWN entries are removed from tools/conformance/runner.c:
- `cancel_kind.variants`;
- the ParentCancelled, ResourceUnavailable, Shutdown and LinkedExit ordinals.
Recorded digests are refreshed in the same change.

title: Default obligation leak response: Rust panics (RuntimeConfig, LabConfig), C logs (asx_runtime_config_init) - owner decision
description:
## Drift
Rust 5e60b1c4c defaults to failing loudly on an obligation leak:
- `RuntimeConfig::default().obligation_leak_response` is `ObligationLeakResponse::Panic`
  (src/runtime/config.rs:2242);
- `LabConfig::default().panic_on_obligation_leak` is `true` (src/lab/config.rs:192).

C's `asx_runtime_config_init` defaults to `ASX_LEAK_LOG` (src/runtime/hooks.c:772). The C lab
(`asx_lab_init`) and every runtime built from the default config use it too, so in C a leaked
obligation is logged by default where Rust panics.

## Decision needed (owner)
Should C default to `ASX_LEAK_PANIC`? That changes what an ordinary C program does on a leak.
First check what `ASX_LEAK_PANIC` does in C (abort or a panicked task) and which tests and
examples leak on purpose; those would set LOG explicitly. The conformance interpreter sets its own
policy and is unaffected. The other choice is to keep LOG as an accepted C default and record the
reason.

## Done when
Either C's default matches Rust, or the difference is recorded as accepted with its reason. In both
cases `asx-conformance constants` reports the two keys accordingly:
`runtime.default.obligation_leak_response` and `lab.default.panic_on_obligation_leak`.

title: Canonical semantic vocabulary v2: event kinds, status map, cancel kinds by name, outcome+reason, snapshot schema, independence relation
description:
## Why
A Rust↔C comparison is only meaningful if both sides project into **one** canonical vocabulary,
and that vocabulary must be fine-grained enough that diverging engines can't look equal. The
current fixtures mostly assert generic `UserTrace` events, which proves nothing. The two sides
also use incompatible status numbers: the Rust fuzz target uses `ST_NOT_FOUND=-1`, while C has
`ASX_E_NOT_FOUND=102`. And the cancel-kind ordinals differ: Rust has `LinkedExit=10, Shutdown=9`,
C has `LinkedExit=7, Shutdown=10`.

## Deliverables
1. **`docs/CANONICAL_VOCABULARY_V2.md`** (normative) and `schemas/canonical_vocabulary_v2.json`.
2. **Event kinds**, each with fields and the Rust `TraceEvent` variant(s) it projects from
   (`/dp/asupersync/src/trace/event.rs`):
   - Task:
     - `task.spawned{task, region, budget}`;
     - `task.state{task, from, to}`;
     - `task.polled{task, step}` (optional detail level);
     - `task.completed{task, outcome}`.
   - Region: `region.state{region, from, to}`, `region.closed{region, close_outcome}`.
   - Cancel: `cancel.requested{target, reason}`, `cancel.acknowledged{task, reason}`,
     `cancel.strengthened{target, old, new}`.
   - Obligation: `obligation.reserved{id, kind, holder}`, `obligation.committed{id}`,
     `obligation.aborted{id, reason}`, `obligation.leaked{id}`.
   - Timer: `timer.armed{id, deadline}`, `timer.fired{id}`, `timer.cancelled{id}`.
   - Channel:
     - `chan.reserved{ch, permit}`;
     - `chan.sent{ch, permit}`;
     - `chan.aborted{ch, permit}`;
     - `chan.recv{ch}`;
     - `chan.closed{ch, side}`.
   - Sync: `sync.acquired{prim}`, `sync.released{prim}`, `sync.waited{prim}`.
   - Actor: `actor.msg{actor, kind}`, `supervisor.restart{child, n}`.
   - `wake{task, source}`.
3. **Encodings.**
   - Outcomes are `{"ok"} | {"err": <code>} | {"cancelled": <reason>} | {"panicked": <descriptor>}`.
   - A reason is `{kind: <NAME>, origin_region, origin_task, timestamp, message?, cause_chain_len,
     truncated}`.
   - Cancel kinds are encoded **by name** (`"PollQuota"`), never by ordinal.
4. **Status mapping table.** Rust `Error` / `ErrorKind` / `SendError` / `RecvError` /
   `AcquireError` etc. map to `asx_status`. Each mapping is either exact or lossy-with-rationale.
   Unmapped is not allowed.
5. **Snapshot schema.** The end-of-scenario canonical state dump:
   - per task: state, outcome with reason, cancel phase, cleanup polls used;
   - per region: state, close outcome;
   - per obligation: state, reason, holder;
   - per channel: len, reserved, closed flags;
   - pending timers.
6. **Independence relation** (for Foata canonicalization). Port the exact predicate from
   `/dp/asupersync/src/trace/independence.rs:303` (`pub fn independent(a, b)`), restated over
   vocabulary events with citations. It must be identical on both sides, and a unit test table
   checks it.
7. **Digest algorithm** over the canonical JSON (SHA-256 of canonical bytes: sorted keys, no
   whitespace, integers as decimal). Pinned; no ordinal dependence.
8. **`docs/VOCABULARY_EXCLUSIONS.md`.** Every Rust `TraceEvent` variant that is deliberately
   not projected, with its rationale.

## Success criteria
- The spec is complete, with no TBDs.
- The JSON schema validates the examples.
- The status table covers every `asx_status` (66 codes) and every Rust error kind reachable from
  the kernel APIs used by DSL v2.
- The independence predicate is cross-checked by a table test on both sides (C test under
  `tests/unit/runtime/`; Rust test in `tools/twin_run`).

"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.
4. **Tests are required.**
   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.
   - E2E scripts emit detailed structured JSONL logs: `ts`, `run_id`, `layer`, `suite`, `test`,
     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.
5. **Never delete a file or directory without explicit written owner permission**
   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.
6. **Don't run code-modifying scripts** (AGENTS.md). Make code changes manually.
7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.
8. **Close only with evidence.** The close reason must name test names, gate output and artifact
   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.
9. **Rust line numbers drift.** Treat cited `file:line` anchors as grep starting points and
   re-verify them at the pinned rev.

sufficient on its own.

title: Formal evidence tests: distinguish native enumeration from actual bounded checking and reject vacuous proofs
description:
Purpose: Gate the real bounded-proof requirement (PLAN 10.7.3), extending the existing Lean/TLA crosswalk task bd-9kll.2.14 without creating a duplicate implementation task. make formal-cbmc currently builds and runs six ordinary C executables. It does not invoke CBMC; compatible source and passing finite enumeration cannot satisfy solver/interleaving evidence.

Required implementation in the dependency: a pinned actual bounded-checker lane with explicit bounds, unwind completeness, assumptions and source/toolchain provenance for cancellation ordering, obligation double resolve and small scheduler interleavings; formal-check/native tests and actual proof status must be reported separately. Include conditional fairness assumptions for refinement progress rules #9,#21,#28 and make no unbounded-liveness claim from finite search.

Validator/negative controls: checker absent; timeout; insufficient unwind; disabled assertion; contradictory/vacuous assumptions; zero reachable executions; unexpected source SHA; one deliberately admitted illegal transition/double resolve; starvation trace under missing fairness. Each must produce an honest failure or explicit non-proof classification. A passing bounded run reports explored bound and obligations, not universal correctness. Run representative harnesses against actual C runtime functions, preserve minimized counterexamples and JSONL per property/bound/tool status. Assert CI does not print proof=pass solely because standalone harnesses run. Native fallback remains useful local diagnostics, never a silent certified result.

Context and completion policy: This is the 2026-10-11 reality-check extension of bd-9kll, audited at C commit 1df1808d51ae5ca90c2fdd0c6a351e77091b9c3c. Implement manually in existing files where possible; preserve other agents' work and never delete any file without written owner permission. Run strict build, pinned format/lint, unit/invariant tests and conformance; compare pass counts before/after. Closure must identify tests, commands, source SHA, toolchain, artifacts and remaining exclusions. title: Oracle: assert zero ghost-monitor violations on every conformance and fuzz-differential run
description: Found by the 2026-10-12 reality check (no bead covered it). tools/conformance/runner.c never calls asx_ghost_violation_count() (include/asx/core/ghost.h:112), and the runner library is not built with ASX_DEBUG_GHOST, so a protocol/linearity/borrow violation that happens inside a fixture which still matches Rust goes unnoticed. - [ ] Planted negative: a test-only mutant (ASX_MUTANT_* style) that performs an illegal transition inside an otherwise-matching scenario makes the ghost-checked run fail while the plain run passes
- [ ] CI conformance job runs the ghost-checked corpus; all 167 fixtures pass
- [ ] No-claim: green does not prove absence of memory errors (that is the sanitizer bead)

title: Scenario DSL v2: scripted task-body step programs covering every kernel/primitive unit (versioned JSON schema)
description:
## Why
The current fixture ops (`region_open`, `task_spawn`, `channel_create`, …) can't express task
bodies, so no Rust capture ever polls a task:
- the capture tool inserts bare `TaskRecord`s with no future;
- "1 tasks leaked" appears in the expected errors.

The new runtime features (park/wake, masking, task groups, budgets, channel waits, actors) are
unrepresentable. `docs/SCENARIO_DSL.md` lists opcodes nobody implements.

## Design (`schemas/scenario_dsl_v2.json` plus `docs/SCENARIO_DSL_V2.md`)
- **Top level.**
  - `{schema:"asx.scenario.v2", id, description, rules:[...], seed, lab:{auto_advance:false, worker_count:1}, profile_requirements, setup:[region ops], tasks:{name: program}, script:[global ops at virtual times], expect:{kind: "ok"|"must_fail", error?}}`.
  - `rules` names the v4 formal semantics rules exercised.
- **Task program.** A list of steps executed one per poll unless noted.
  - Control: `yield`, `park_until_woken`, `checkpoint`, `sleep_ns n`, `wait_until t`,
    `consume_cost n`.
  - Masking: `mask`, `unmask`.
  - Obligations: `reserve {kind, as:name}`, `commit name`, `abort name`.
  - Spawning: `spawn {program, region?, budget?, as:name}`, `join name`, `watch name`.
  - Channels: `chan_create {cap, as}`, `reserve_send ch {as permit}`, `send permit value`,
    `abort permit`, `recv ch {expect?}`, `close ch`, `drop_rx ch`.
  - Sync: `mutex_lock m`, `mutex_unlock m`, `sem_acquire s n`, `sem_release s n`,
    `barrier_wait b`, `notify_wait n`, `notify_one n`.
  - Task groups: `group {mode: race|join|first_ok|quorum k, members:[program], deadline?}`.
  - Actors: `actor_spawn`, `cast`, `call`, `stop`, `supervisor {strategy, children, intensity}`.
  - Termination: `complete ok|err code|panic`.
- **Region ops.** `open {as, budget?}`, `open_child {parent, as, budget?}`, `close r`,
  `cancel r kind`, `drain r kind?`.
- **Faults.** `fault {kind: clock_skew|alloc_fail_next, ...}`, applied as scripted events only.
  There is no random chaos in parity fixtures.
- **Budgets.** `{deadline_ns?, poll_quota?, cost_quota?, priority?}`; absence means
  unconstrained.
- **Semantics.** Each step's semantics are defined once in the spec, so both interpreters agree:
  - what a step does if cancellation is observed (acknowledge at a `checkpoint`; other steps are
    "cancel-oblivious" unless stated);
  - how `recv` blocks;
  - what `complete` returns when a cancel is pending.
- **Must-fail fixtures** declare an expected error (for example `{"error":"ASX_E_INVALID_TRANSITION","at_step":...}`)
  to cover the forbidden-behavior catalog.

## Success criteria
- The schema and spec are complete.
- At least 20 example scenarios validate, covering every unit listed in W1.7.
- The spec states, per step, which Rust API and which C API implements it, so W1.4 and W1.5 have
  no guesswork.
- The old `docs/SCENARIO_DSL.md` is marked superseded (with W0.5).


---

title: Twin-run harness (tools/twin_run): drive real asupersync LabRuntime from DSL v2, project to vocabulary, record schedule/RNG/certificate
description:
## Why
This replaces the fabricating `tools/fixture_capture`. The new tool must **execute asupersync**.
The old tool's problems:
- `insert_task` with no future (`main.rs:283`);
- hardcoded `CancelKind::User` (`:309`);
- `Budget::meet` is never called (`:262-277`);
- channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` (`:381-401`);
- timer events are self-written (`:403-424`);
- unknown ops are silently traced (`:446-452`).

## Design
- **Crate.** `tools/twin_run/` is a Rust crate (tooling may use dependencies, plan §2.1.2).
  - It depends on `asupersync` pinned by git rev `5e60b1c4c` (W1.1) with the needed features
    (`test-internals` / lab).
  - `serde_json`, `clap`, `uuid`, `sha2`.
- **Rust side.**
  - For each DSL v2 task program, spawn a real task into a real region via the `LabRuntime`
    public or lab API. Use `Cx`-based APIs: `cx.checkpoint()`, `cx.masked`, obligations,

title: C conformance interpreter asx_conformance_run(): execute DSL v2 through the C runtime, emit vocabulary events + snapshot, self-computed digest
description:
## Why
No C code interprets fixture `input.ops`; `rg '"scheduler_run"|input\.ops'` finds only test
labels. The C side of the oracle has to exist.

## Design
- **Library API.** `include/asx/conformance/conformance.h`, `src/conformance/interpreter.c`.
  This is genuinely new functionality, so new files are justified.
  - `asx_status asx_conformance_run(const char *scenario_json, size_t len, const asx_conformance_sink *sink, asx_conformance_result *out)`.
  - The sink receives canonical vocabulary-v2 JSON lines (events, then the snapshot).
  - `out` carries the self-computed digest, step count and engine identity: git SHA embedded at
    build time via `-DASX_GIT_SHA`, a library config fingerprint, profile and codec.
- **JSON parser.** Reuse the existing JSON codec parser in `src/runtime/hooks.c` or the codec
  module if it can parse arbitrary JSON. Otherwise write a small bounded JSON reader with no
  dynamic allocation: static arena sized by config, and errors on overflow.
- **Task programs** run as C poll functions over a per-task step cursor stored in a static table.
  This is the protothread pattern. Each DSL step maps to the C API named in the W1.3 spec.
- **Execution mode.** Lab mode: deterministic and seeded. Once S1 lands it uses the lab dispatch
  mode, and until then the current scheduler. The interpreter must not assume one or the other.
  It drives the scheduler and records events by hooking trace emission (or post-processing the
  trace ring through a projection table `asx_trace_event_kind → vocabulary`). It must not
  depend on the 1024-event prefix limit: coordinate with RB1, and use a streaming sink.
- **Snapshot** built from runtime query APIs.
- **CLI.** `build/bin/asx-conformance` (`tools/conformance/runner.c`) reads fixture files, runs
  them, and compares against the fixture's expected events and snapshot in all three modes where
  available (W1.6 implements the comparator library). It emits a JSONL report.
- **Negative controls built in.**
  - `--self-test` corrupts one expected event in memory and asserts a FAIL.
  - Runs refuse when the engine identity is missing.

## Success criteria
- The interpreter executes every W1.3 example scenario without unknown-op errors.
- The digest is computed from execution: changing one C runtime behaviour, for example a
  deliberately mutated build with `-DASX_TEST_MUTANT_BUDGET_MEET`, changes it.
- It works from both the twin_run (FFI) path and the standalone CLI.

## Tests
- Unit tests per DSL step (`tests/unit/conformance/test_interpreter.c`).
- A mutation self-test.
- An e2e script, `tests/e2e/conformance_interpreter.sh`, with JSONL logs.

title: Comparator with three strengths (snapshot, Foata trace class, exact schedule) + first-divergence report + ddmin minimizer; make conformance uses it
description:
## Design
- **Modes.**
  - (a) **snapshot/outcome**: compare the canonical end snapshots and per-task outcomes. This is
    schedule-independent.
  - (b) **Foata trace class**: compute the Foata normal form of both projected traces using the
    W1.2 independence relation, then compare layer by layer. C implements the canonicalizer in L1;
    in twin_run, Rust's `trace::canonicalize` provides the reference and the C port must agree.
  - (c) **exact**: event-by-event equality when both engines follow the same schedule. Either C's
    lab dispatcher replicates Rust's picker (S1, compare certificates), or Rust replays C's
    recorded schedule via `run_forced_schedule` (`lab/runtime.rs:2685`), or C replays Rust's (L3).
- **Report** per scenario (JSONL):
  - `scenario_id`, `rules`, `mode`, `parity` (pass/fail), `first_divergence` (JSON pointer plus
    both values), `mismatch_signature` (a stable hash of the minimal diff);
  - `engine_identity` for both sides;
  - the plan §9.3 provenance fields: `rust_baseline_commit`, `rust_toolchain_commit_hash`,
    `cargo_lock_sha256`, `fixture_schema_version`, `scenario_dsl_version`;
  - `delta_classification` (`none | intentional_upstream | c_regression | spec_defect |
    harness_defect`) and `classification_record_id` when not none.
- **Minimizer.** ddmin over DSL v2 steps and tasks, preserving schema validity, that reduces a
  divergent scenario to a minimal one. Output goes to `fixtures/fuzz_counterexamples/` (schema
  `asx.fuzz_counterexample.v2`).
- **`make conformance` uses it.** It runs offline C replay of the checked-in fixtures (all modes
  available offline: (a), (b), and (c) against the recorded schedule) and, when `cargo` is
  available, live twin_run compare. It fails closed when 0 records are compared (W0.3).
  Emit `build/conformance/parity_summary.json`, consumed by W0.10 and W1.14.

## Success criteria
- On the regenerated corpus (W1.7), every mode reports pass or a classified delta.
- A mutant C build (for example the old `min` priority meet) fails mode (a) on a budget fixture,
  with a first-divergence pointer to the task's effective priority.
- The minimizer reduces a 40-step divergent scenario to ≤ 5 steps.

## Tests
`tests/e2e/oracle_selftest.sh` covers:
- sabotage fixture → FAIL;
- corrupted event → FAIL;
- same-engine comparison (both sides C) → REJECTED by the EngineIdentity guard;
- mutant library → FAIL with the correct `first_divergence`.

It logs JSONL.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.
4. **Tests are required.**
   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.
   - E2E scripts emit detailed structured JSONL logs: `ts`, `run_id`, `layer`, `suite`, `test`,
     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.
5. **Never delete a file or directory without explicit written owner permission**
   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.
6. **Don't run code-modifying scripts** (AGENTS.md). Make code changes manually.
7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.
8. **Close only with evidence.** The close reason must name test names, gate output and artifact
   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.
9. **Rust line numbers drift.** Treat cited `file:line` anchors as grep starting points and
   re-verify them at the pinned rev.

Orientation-only living plan: `docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md`. This bead is meant to be
sufficient on its own.

title: Oracle self-test suite: negative controls, engine-identity guard, mutant libraries, projection completeness, with detailed JSONL logging
description:
## Why
Honesty must be encoded in the harness. The oracle must demonstrably fail when it should; a
passing oracle that can't fail is the original problem again.

## Plan
`tests/e2e/oracle_selftest.sh`, run in CI on every push once W1.6 lands. Cases:
1. **Sabotage fixture** (op `launch_missiles`, bogus events) → fixture-integrity FAIL.
2. **Single corrupted expected event** in an otherwise valid fixture → conformance FAIL, with
   `first_divergence` pointing at that event.
3. **Self-comparison.** Both engine identities set to the same C build → REJECTED with
   `ENGINE_IDENTITY_COLLISION`.
4. **Mutant C libraries** built with `-DASX_MUTANT_<X>`. Each must fail the expected fixture
   family:
   - `BUDGET_PRIORITY_MIN` → budget unit;
   - `CANCEL_NO_STRENGTHEN` → cancel unit;
   - `OBLIGATION_SKIP_ABORT_ON_CANCEL` → obligation unit;
   - `SCHED_REVERSE_ORDER` → scheduler unit (mode c).

   Mutant macros live in the source behind `#ifdef ASX_MUTANT_*`, compiled only in self-test
   builds. Document each.
5. **Projection completeness** (Rust side, in `tools/twin_run` tests). For every state-changing
   `TraceEvent` variant, perturb one field and assert the projected vocabulary event changes,
   unless the variant is listed in `docs/VOCABULARY_EXCLUSIONS.md`.
6. **Zero-record guard.** An empty fixture dir → `make conformance` FAILS.
7. **Determinism.** Running the full corpus twice produces identical reports (except timestamps
   and run IDs).

## Success criteria
- All cases behave as specified in CI.
- The JSONL log lines carry `case`, `expected`, `observed`, `pass` and artifact paths.

title: Regenerate the Rust-captured fixture corpus: >=6 scenarios per semantic unit incl. must-fail, rule-tagged, JSON+real BIN
description:
## Plan
Author DSL v2 scenarios and capture them with `twin_run capture`. Promote them via
`make fixtures-promote` (W1.1). Units, each needing ≥ 6 scenarios with ≥ 1 must-fail where the
unit has forbidden behaviour:

| Unit | What the scenarios cover |
|---|---|
| `budget` | meet: deadline, poll, cost, **priority**; exhaustion → cancel kinds |
| `cancel` | each of the 11 kinds; strengthen tie-breaks; attribution chain depth/truncation; masking; checkpoint-masked |
| `task_lifecycle` | spawn; complete ok/err/panic; cancel before first poll vs after; value-after-ack |
| `region_lifecycle` | close ok-body vs err-body; drain with reason; descendants PARENT; finalizer order; close outcome |
| `obligation` | reserve/commit/abort/leak; holder cancelled → abort CANCEL; leak policy and escalation |
| `quiescence` | Q1-Q4 failures and successes |
| `scheduler` | lane priority; cancel streak 16; EDF; rng tie-break; pending-without-wake |
| `timers` | same-tick order; timeout boundary; interval modes |
| `mpsc`, `oneshot`, `broadcast`, `watch` | per-channel semantics |
| `sync` | `mutex`, `semaphore`, `rwlock`, `barrier`, `notify`, `once` |
| `combinators` | poll-based race/join/select/timeout/retry/bracket |
| `task_groups` | race/join/first_ok/quorum, deadline, owner cancel |
| `actor`, `supervision` | actor and supervisor behaviour |
| `leak_policy` | each policy and its escalation |

Also:
- Every fixture's `rules` lists the v4 formal semantics rules it exercises.
- The coverage report (rule → fixture count) is emitted; every kernel rule must have ≥ 1 fixture.
- Store genuine BIN encodings as `.bin` files alongside the JSON (the current `*.codec_bin.json`
  files are JSON with a different label).
- Old fixtures stay where they are. Mark them `legacy_unverified` and exclude them from the
  parity lane. Don't delete them (RULE 1). A later owner-approved cleanup may remove them.

## Success criteria
- At least 150 rule-tagged fixtures.
- The rule-coverage report shows no uncovered kernel rule.
- `make conformance` runs all of them.
- Initial results show the **known drifts as failures** (K1 priority, etc.). That proves the
  oracle bites. The drift beads then turn them green.

Method. Closed (commit, scenarios):
- cancel (98d66ca, 5): the driver had only used User/Timeout/Deadline/Shutdown and two kinds (RaceLost, ResourceUnavailable) were observed nowhere: a matrix of all 11 kinds with each kind's cleanup budget; the strengthen ladder; weaker-after-stronger; equal severity keeps the earlier; same-instant message tie-break.

title: Real codec-equivalence and profile-parity: execute fixtures under every profile x codec build and compare runtime-produced digests
description:
## Problem
- **codec-equivalence** compares two `semantic_digest` strings stored in fixture files. Both come
  from one capture algorithm that ignores the codec, and both files are JSON.
- **profile-parity** does the same across profile labels. The capture tool ignores the profile,
  and the C runtime is built once for CORE.
- `tests/conformance/profile_parity_conformance_test.c` round-trips a synthetic fixture.

## Plan
1. **Build matrix.** Build the conformance interpreter for {CORE, POSIX, FREESTANDING,
   EMBEDDED_ROUTER, HFT, AUTOMOTIVE, PARALLEL, BROWSER} × {JSON, BIN} with `DETERMINISTIC=1`.
2. **Profile parity.** Run the shared fixture set on each build. Compare the runtime-produced
   canonical digests and snapshots. Any difference fails, unless the scenario exceeds a profile's
   resource class, which is reported as a class-limit outcome per R1 rather than as drift.
3. **Codec parity.** Encode the C-produced trace to BIN and back to JSON, and compare the digest
   of the produced events (this is real equivalence). Also decode the checked-in `.bin` fixtures
   and compare them to the JSON fixtures.
4. **Gates.** Replace the fake gates: `make profile-parity` and `make codec-equivalence` now run
   these. Keep the old record-comparison logic only as part of `fixture-integrity`.

## Success criteria
- A deliberately profile-dependent mutant (for example `#ifdef ASX_PROFILE_HFT` changing a tie
  rule) fails profile-parity.
- The matrix runs in CI via rch-friendly targets.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is

     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.

   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.

     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.

   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.

7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.

   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.

title: [K] Kernel semantic parity with asupersync 0.6.0 (budget, cancel, region, task, obligation, outcome, combinators)
description:
## Why
Kernel parity is the port's *primary* goal (plan §2.2). Since the Feb 2026 baseline, upstream has
made 1,077 commits to the kernel paths, and the C kernel diverges in observable ways:
- budget priority is reversed;
- the cleanup budget is a hard kill counted from the request;
- the value retained after a cancel is acknowledged is lost;
- region close ordering and outcomes differ;
- normal spawns are admitted while a region is Finalizing;
- leak policy default and escalation differ;
- there are no attribution chains, timestamps are 0, and ordinals differ;
- checkpoint and capability semantics differ;
- the poll-based race doesn't drain losers;
- task-group FIRST_OK, tie-break, owner reason and quorum validation differ;
- links and monitors are missing;
- outcomes carry no reason.

## Method
For each unit:
1. Extract the rule from the v4 formal semantics and the Rust source at the pinned rev.
2. Write or capture failing fixtures via the twin-run oracle.
3. Fix C.
4. Make it green on (a)+(b), and (c) where scheduler-relevant.
5. Update the C refinement map and the README.

## Done when
Every kernel rule in `docs/C_REFINEMENT_MAP.md` is `Implemented` with fixture evidence, and each
kernel unit's parity lower bound is ≥ 99.9% (95% credible) on ≥ 20k random differential
scenarios.

title: K1 Budget priority semiring is reversed vs Rust (min->max, INFINITE=0, ZERO=255, default 128) + explicit deadline presence
description:
## Drift (verified 2026-10-08)
| | C (`src/core/budget.c`) | Rust 0.6.0 (`/dp/asupersync/src/types/budget.rs`) |
|---|---|---|
| Meet | `result.priority = min_u8(a->priority, b->priority)` (`:46`) | `priority: self.priority.max(other.priority)` (`:569`, in `combine_untraced`) |
| Infinite | `asx_budget_infinite()` priority = 255 (`:15`) | `Budget::INFINITE` priority = 0 (`:222`), the identity for max |
| Zero | `asx_budget_zero()` priority = 0 (`:24`) | `Budget::ZERO` priority = 255 (`:230`), absorbing |
| Default | none | `Budget::new()` priority = 128 |

Upstream changed this in commits `a16f46c5a` / `8195e9a1c` (Mar 10-12) and `d9f3bda42`
(Jul 31: INFINITE priority is 0).

The C README documents the old rule (`README.md:731-735`, `meet(a,b).priority = min(...)`), and
the C algebraic suite (`tests/formal/algebraic/`) "proves" the wrong lattice. The old
self-referential fixtures never caught it, because the capture tool never called `Budget::meet`.

There is a second difference. C uses deadline `0` to mean "unconstrained", so a deadline at time
0 can't be expressed, and `zero()` uses deadline 1. Rust uses `Option<Time>`, with `ZERO.deadline
= Some(Time::ZERO)`.

## Fix
1. `asx_budget_meet`: take the max of priorities; keep min for deadline, poll and cost.
2. Set `asx_budget_infinite().priority = 0` and `asx_budget_zero().priority = 255`.
3. Add `asx_budget_new()` / `ASX_BUDGET_DEFAULT_PRIORITY 128`.
4. `asx_budget_from_polls` uses priority 128. Verify against Rust's `Budget::with_poll_quota` or
   the equivalent; if it starts from INFINITE, then 0.
5. Explicit deadline presence: add `has_deadline` or an `ASX_DEADLINE_NONE` sentinel
   (`UINT64_MAX`), so time 0 is expressible. Mirror `ZERO.deadline = 0` with presence. Update
   every consumer (scheduler deadline checks, timers, region inheritance).
6. Fix the algebraic/CBMC suites and the README (the budget algebra section and the cleanup text).
   Check every caller that compares priorities (the scheduler, after S5) for the direction of
   "higher = more urgent".

## Tests
- Unit tests for the identity, absorbing, commutativity, associativity and idempotence laws under
  the max semiring; meet with NULL; default 128.
- Algebraic suite updated.
- A Rust-captured budget fixture family (W1.7) covering priority inheritance through regions and
  tasks.
- Metamorphic M3 (spawn under `meet(a,b)` ≡ nested regions a then b).

## Success
The budget unit is green on W1 modes (a)/(b), `check-rust-constants` (W1.12) shows no budget
mismatch, and the README is correct.

title: K10 Cost-quota exhaustion semantics: cancel at checkpoint when cost reaches exactly 0 (Rust) vs C overcharge-cancel
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** (`/dp/asupersync/src/cx/cx.rs:3145`) cancels with CostBudget only at a checkpoint,
  when the remaining cost reaches exactly 0.
- **C** `asx_task_consume_cost` (`src/runtime/lifecycle.c:931`) cancels with COST_BUDGET
  immediately whenever a charge exceeds the remainder, and returns
  `ASX_E_COST_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`. README L745 documents the C behaviour.

## Fix
Re-verify Rust's exact consume and check semantics (saturating decrement? error on overcharge?),
then align. Document the API mapping (the C `consume_cost` maps to which Rust API). Update README
L739-746.

## Tests
Charges {below, exactly equal to, above} the remaining amount × checkpoint before or after.
Fixtures: budget/cost family.

title: K11 Verify inline-future drop semantics separately from task-group loser drain; close remaining combinator contracts
description:
Current contract correction (2026-10-11, C 1df1808d, Rust pinned 5e60b1c4c): Rust Cx::race explicitly drops losing futures without awaiting them (cx/cx.rs:4305-4338); Scope::race/race_all over spawned tasks drains. C core inline combinators now never poll a dropped loser again, and real task groups implement cancel+join. Requiring true asynchronous drain in every inline combinator would create a new parity divergence. The original K11 loser-drain premise is superseded by this API-family distinction, not by weakening structured concurrency.

Deliverables:
1. Reverify every inline combinator against its pinned corresponding Rust API, and maintain an API contract table separating inline futures, task groups and nonblocking admission counters.
2. Preserve pending-until-owner-cancel for empty race/select and first_ok stopping at cancellation. Verify their current code rather than duplicate already implemented fixes.
3. Specify and enforce exactly-once resource release for an inline branch that stops being polled: identify explicit C drop/cleanup callbacks or obligation/owner cleanup that substitute for Rust Future::drop, and test acquired resources. Never poll an inline loser after the drop decision.
4. Preserve real task-group cancel reason, loser join/drain and panic propagation. Multi-poll cleanup and owner cancellation belong to task-group coverage, not to inline futures.
5. Close the actual remaining retry/backoff and map_reduce first-failure gaps tracked by bd-2cvl; do not silently erase those features. Compare all 11 originally scoped combinators and the newer inline family without assuming their shared poll function means identical cancellation rules.
6. Update README/refinement evidence and capture expressive real Rust fixtures; direct C resource-lifetime tests must state unexpressible type-level misuse separately.

Tests: inline winner with a pending loser is dropped once and never polled again; owned-resource release once on winner/cancel/timeout/error; empty race waits then responds to owner cancel; first_ok stops at cancelled middle branch; task-group loser requiring at least five cleanup polls is awaited and its obligations resolved; owner reason and loser panic; retry backoff/time boundaries and map_reduce first error via bd-2cvl. Structured JSONL and first divergence required. Existing 131 fixture passes cannot regress. This is an evidence-based correction, not authorization to force inline asynchronous cleanup or alter pinned semantics.

title: K12 Task-group parity: sequential first_ok, Rust tie-breaks, owner reason pass-through, early quorum validation, sealed per-branch regions
description:
## Drift
Rust `/dp/asupersync/src/cx/scope.rs`: `:1306` race_all, `:1479` join_all, `:1811` quorum,
`:2023` first_ok, `:2130` timeout. C: `src/runtime/task_group.c:114-161`.

| Aspect | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| first_ok | runs attempts **one at a time**, starting the next only after an Err | runs all members concurrently |
| Tie-break | 2-way race alternates which branch is checked first; N-way picks among same-round finishers with the Cx RNG | always the lowest index |
| Cancelled owner | passes its own reason (or Timeout for a scope timeout); commits `7cb5e043c`, `62102979a` | sends PARENT |
| Invalid quorum | rejected before spawning | discovered at the first poll, after spawning |
| Race branches | each in its own sealed child region (`2755c421c`, Oct 6) | — |

## Fix
1. FIRST_OK becomes sequential. If concurrent first-ok is useful, keep it as `FIRST_OK_CONCURRENT`,
   C-only and documented.
2. Implement the tie-breaks. The RNG comes from the lab seed, via S1.
3. Pass the owner's reason through.
4. Validate quorum before spawning.
5. Give each race branch a sealed child region.
6. Update README L863-871.

## Tests
- Each mode × owner cancel × deadline × simultaneous completions.
- Fixtures: task_groups family.

title: K13 Links and monitors (LinkedExit/FailFast cancels, trap_exit, DOWN messages) + resolve C module name clash
description:
## Drift
Rust `/dp/asupersync/src/link.rs` (`:672`, LinkedExit) and `src/monitor.rs` implement
Erlang-style links and monitors: a linked exit cancels the peer with LinkedExit, `trap_exit`
turns that into a message, and a monitor delivers DOWN. C has only `asx_task_watch`. It never
issues FAIL_FAST or LINKED_EXIT cancels; POISON containment uses RESOURCE (`lifecycle.c:744`).

The C modules `include/asx/monitor/` and `include/asx/link/` are **unrelated** concepts with
clashing names: runtime health monitoring and coordination links.

## Fix
1. Rename the unrelated C modules to accurate names, for example `health_monitor` and
   `coord_link`. AGENTS.md: no compatibility shims; update all users.
2. Implement Rust-semantics links and monitors in the runtime: link/unlink, `trap_exit`,
   monitor/demonitor, DOWN delivery through an actor mailbox or a oneshot.
3. Issue FailFast for fail-fast scopes as Rust does. Cite where Rust emits FailFast (for example
   join_all fail-fast variants) and match it.

## Tests
- Linked pair exits: Err → peer cancelled LinkedExit; with `trap_exit` → message.
- Monitor DOWN with the reason.
- Fixtures: actor/link family.

title: K16 Enforce obligation holder authorization at application commit and handoff boundaries
description:
Problem and user value: C_REFINEMENT_MAP rule.obligation.commit #14 explicitly has no open bead. asx_obligation_commit accepts only an obligation handle; possession of that ID can resolve another task's obligation. This loses Rust's token-bound holder guarantee even though valid same-holder DSL fixtures pass. The reserve-outside-poll problem is already K4 (bd-9kll.3.4); this task owns commit authorization, not that duplicate.

Deliverable: Inventory reserve/commit/handoff and channel/sync callers in lifecycle.c, runtime.h, cx and scope. Extract the pinned Rust token and any administrative abort-by-id contracts. Make the application resolution boundary carry and validate the current holder/context, region, generation and Reserved phase before changing the ledger. A handoff must atomically update authority; the old holder must lose commit authority. State clearly which narrowly scoped runtime cleanup actions may act administratively; a public raw-ID bypass must not undermine the guarantee. Avoid compatibility wrappers: fix affected callers directly. Preserve exactly-once/failure atomicity and public status taxonomy.

Implementation checks: valid holder commits once; non-holder and stale contexts do not mutate state, counts, trace or ownership; handoff transfers authority once. Update the refinement row and public preconditions. The companion test bead must prove the forbidden path fails before this correction and succeeds as an expected rejection after it. DSL cannot currently transfer a token to a different caller, so direct public-API tests are required alongside real Rust captures where its API is expressive.

Context and completion policy: This is the 2026-10-11 reality-check extension of bd-9kll, audited at C commit 1df1808d51ae5ca90c2fdd0c6a351e77091b9c3c. The real oracle currently compares 131 fixtures successfully; that proves its projected lab scenarios, not every public API or formal rule. Rust authority for parity is git revision 5e60b1c4c53d62aaddae68de3ee7de4732f1755b, accessed with git show rather than an unpinned working tree. Semantic delta budget is zero. Implement manually in existing files where possible; preserve other agents' work and never delete any file without written owner permission. Run strict build, pinned format/lint, unit/invariant tests and conformance; compare pass counts before/after. Closure must identify tests, commands, source SHA, toolchain, artifacts and remaining exclusions. E2E JSONL must include run_id, suite, test, status, seed, profile, codec, rust_rev, c_git_sha, configuration fingerprint and first divergence. Keep hardware-unavailable, missing tools, timeout and skipped lanes visible; they cannot count as proof.
notes:

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-10-11 prototype finding (reverted, nothing committed): a strict check in asx_obligation_commit / abort_with_reason (an obligation with a holder resolvable only from that holder's poll, asx_task_current() == holder; holderless ones by anyone) broke 16 of 131 conformance fixtures (all actor-* GenServer fixtures, mpsc-two-phase-send-recv, oneshot-*, obligation-reserve-commit-001, obligation-limit-permit-admitted-at-poll-end-001, supervision-child-holds-obligation-001) and 5 unit suites. Cause: Rust resolves tokens from other tasks legitimately: a moved ObligationToken (e.g. a GenServer call's reply token, committed by the server) keeps its holder's liability but can be committed by whoever owns it now (obligation_mailbox.rs ObligationToken::commit has no caller check; only try_transfer moves liability), and C's channel/actor internals resolve permits on another task's behalf. So the fix needs (a) an internal resolution path for the runtime's own administrative resolutions (actor reply, channel permit delivery/abort, interpreter), (b) a public transfer API (Rust try_transfer: destination live, not cancel-requested, different holder; same-region quota reuse) used where C code moves a token to another task, and only then (c) the public holder check. Rust allows a moved token to be committed by its new owner without a transfer, so (c) is stricter than Rust and needs an explicit ruling against the pinned semantics before it lands.

title: K2 Cleanup budget must start at acknowledgement and be advisory (Rust) - C hard-kills from request (CANCEL_FORCED)
description:
## Drift
- **Rust.** The cleanup budget is applied only when the task acknowledges cancellation
  (`/dp/asupersync/src/record/task.rs:1341`). In production it is advisory
  (`runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:1280`): the task is never force-completed. In the lab runtime,
  exhaustion only *strengthens* the reason to PollQuota.
- **C.** It counts cleanup polls from the request, including polls before acknowledgement, and
  force-completes the task (CANCEL_FORCED) when the budget is exhausted
  (`src/runtime/scheduler.c:689-705, 791`). README L718 describes this: "Force-completes tasks
  whose cleanup budget is exhausted."

A long, well-behaved cleanup therefore gets killed in C but completes in Rust, and the outcomes
and traces differ.

## Fix
1. Start the cleanup counter at the Cancelling transition (acknowledgement).
2. Lab and deterministic builds: on exhaustion, strengthen the reason (PollQuota) exactly as Rust
   does. Re-verify the exact behaviour at the pinned rev and cite file:line in the commit.
3. Production: advisory, with no force-complete.
4. Keep a hard bound only as an explicit, opt-in **resource-plane** option
   (`asx_runtime_config.cleanup_hard_bound`, default off). Document that enabling it is a semantic
   deviation excluded from parity, and give it a dedicated test.
5. Update README L718 and L747-772.

## Tests
- A task that acknowledges cancellation and then needs 300 polls of cleanup under a TIMEOUT
  cancel (quota 500): C must complete it normally.
- The same with 600 polls: the lab strengthens to PollQuota, there is no force-complete, and the
  outcome matches Rust.
- Opt-in hard-bound test.
- Fixtures: cancel unit, "cleanup over quota" family (W1.7).


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.
4. **Tests are required.**
   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.
   - E2E scripts emit detailed structured JSONL logs: `ts`, `run_id`, `layer`, `suite`, `test`,
     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.
5. **Never delete a file or directory without explicit written owner permission**
   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.
6. **Don't run code-modifying scripts** (AGENTS.md). Make code changes manually.
7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.
8. **Close only with evidence.** The close reason must name test names, gate output and artifact
   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.
9. **Rust line numbers drift.** Treat cited `file:line` anchors as grep starting points and
   re-verify them at the pinned rev.

Orientation-only living plan: `docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md`. This bead is meant to be
sufficient on its own.

title: K18 Replace implicit global runtime authority with explicit owned state and failure-atomic lifecycle
description:
Uncovered architecture contract: PLAN section 7.3 says zero ambient globals and explicit runtime/context flow; PROPOSED_ANSI_C_ARCHITECTURE says no implicit global runtime. lifecycle.c owns process-global g_regions/g_tasks/g_obligations, hooks.c owns g_hooks, and rt.c initializes any new runtime by calling asx_runtime_reset. The generation guard correctly prevents a stale runtime object from shutting down the new one, but this is a singleton bootstrap token, not independently owned runtime state. Existing K8 capability narrowing does not repair state ownership.

Deliverable: Inventory every mutable process-global runtime subsystem and its allocation/lifetime requirement, distinguishing immutable authority tables and platform process-wide signal plumbing. Define explicit runtime-owned storage usable from caller-supplied static arenas in freestanding/R1 and normal host configurations; tie handles, Cx, hooks, clocks, traces, waiters and configuration to the owning runtime. Update affected public/internal callers directly without legacy wrappers. Preserve deterministic ordering and failure atomicity. A second initialization must never silently destroy another live runtime; reject a conflicting init atomically until independent storage is implemented. Stale or cross-runtime handles must not resolve through coincident slot indices/generations.

Phase the implementation in the same task's checked inventory: lifecycle/scheduler/obligations, channels/sync/timers/trace, then live adapters. Avoid solving it with an ambient mutable current-runtime selector. Clarify documented single-thread versus cross-thread rules and platform sharing. This is required architecture work, not permission to add native multicore workers. Completion requires the companion isolation tests plus updated footprint evidence under R1/R3.
