comments.text:
IcyStream: K18 CHECKED INVENTORY of mutable process-global state (basis: main at f769814 + the shared tree; code-first, nothing built).

METHOD. Four independent read-only passes (ast-grep + rg for column-0 static/extern/volatile/static locals/multi-line decls, every hit read in context, const tables excluded). 388 file-scope mutable objects in about 65 files. CLASS: KERNEL = must be per runtime; HANDLE = keyed by a tagged handle, a kernel lookup suffices; PROCESS = process-wide by design; TOOL = diagnostics/harness, no semantic effect; CACHE = derived/write-once. Totals: KERNEL 160 (73 of them lab/parallel, 1 = the kernel block), HANDLE 19, PROCESS 38, TOOL 129, CACHE 42. Per-object rows (file:line, size, reset path, keyed-by, fix) are in four tables, 1,451 lines; they are not in the repo (scratch: /data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-asupersync-ansi-c/3b9a9c33-3b9d-4f83-abda-cde854b52071/scratchpad/inv-g{1-runtime,2-core-sync-channel,3-adapters,4-lab-parallel}.md). Say the word and I commit them as one doc.

DONE (phase 1 so far): region/task/obligation arenas + lifecycle scalars (f769814, 6daadf4, 08e9eba).

== A. HAZARDS THAT DECIDE THE ORDER (each verified at the cited line) ==
A1. asx_runtime_clear_internal(k) is not per kernel. After the arenas it calls ~30 argument-less resets (cancel chain limits, ghost, scheduler event log/scheduler/lab dispatch, wait pool, parallel, channel/oneshot/watch/broadcast/session, timer wheel, waker, io driver, blocking pool, trace, telemetry, hindsight, adapters, fault, hooks, event log, error ledger, notify/semaphore/rwlock/barrier/once/actor/supervisor, reset hooks net/fs/process/signal, diagnostic), and its first line, asx_runtime_object_reset_internal (rt.c:499), zeroes rt_generation of EVERY registered kernel. Clearing, resetting or shutting down runtime B wipes runtime A's channels, timers, wakers, waiters, sync primitives, actors, links, monitors, lab and parallel state and drops A's hold. Unreachable today only because rt.c:195 refuses a second init (asx_kernel_any_held) and asx_kernel_bind_internal always binds slot 0 / tag 0 (resource.c:63-72; asx_kernel_hold takes g_kernels[0]->tag).
A2. Tag-blind identity and keys (latent while ASX_MAX_RUNTIMES == 1): wait_queue.c:40 asx_wait_same_task, link.c:50 and monitor.c:44 same_task, actor.c:1441 asx_actor_task_finished, ghost.c:199 leak scan compare handles with the tag dropped; keyed by bare slot: status.c:74 error ledger, link.c:290 g_cause[slot], and the scheduler wake-timer token (slot<<1)|kind in the process-wide runtime wheel (scheduler.c:114, decoded :274; timers_fire(k) indexes k->tasks[slot], so a shared wheel hands runtime 2's due timers to whichever kernel fires).
A3. Handles minted with tag 0 or carrying no tag at all: channel ids use asx_handle_pack(ASX_TYPE_CHANNEL, 0, idx) (mpsc.c:156) and channel_slot_lookup (mpsc.c:133) never asks asx_kernel_of; sync, actor, supervisor, waker, epoch, timer, asx_io_token and asx_blocking_handle are bare {slot, generation}; link/monitor refs are plain counters; witness ids a u32 sequence.
A4. Bounded shared capacity is semantic: wait-node pool 256, wakers 64, cancel witnesses 64, timers 128 per wheel, channels 16, ... A second runtime consumes the first one's budget, so RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED depends on the other runtime. That is why these are KERNEL, not HANDLE.
A5. Not reached by clear at all (a reset exists, only tests call it): pipe, quic, tls, websocket tables, g_dns_jobs, the posix reactor ctx (epoll fd + wake pipe), logical counters (posix/win32), g_app_shutdown_watch, pool.c, contended_mutex.c (after a clear its 16 slots stay alive on a stale inner semaphore: every lock returns STALE_HANDLE), epoch, symbol, affinity, adaptive, gen_server, deadline monitor, io/blocking g_initialized flags.
A6. Wrong-kernel although they take rt: init binds/clears g_kernels[0]; asx_runtime_is_quiescent(rt) calls handle-less asx_lab_admissions_pending / region_commands_pending / handle_cancels_pending; asx_runtime_io_registration_count(rt) and asx_runtime_blocking_active_count(rt) ignore rt. asx_blocking_pool_reset() runs the hooks' shutdown_fn, which joins the shared worker pool: another runtime's reset would stall on it.
A7. Scheduler g_current_task: sched_poll_slot sets INVALID after a poll instead of restoring the outer value (scheduler.c:1098-1102); two runtimes polled from one thread nest.

== B. INVENTORY BY SUBSYSTEM (objects; class mix; fix; phase) ==
Phase codes: P1 = before test (d); P2 = channels/sync/timers/trace per-runtime; P3 = live adapters; D = by design process-wide (accept only if equal / single owner).

Kernel registry (resource.c g_kernel_static, g_kernels; 2): KERNEL/PROCESS. Fix: bind picks a free registry slot and returns the tag; asx_kernel_hold takes it. P1.
Hooks (hooks.c; 9): g_hooks, g_hooks_installed = PROCESS/D (second init accepted only if byte-equal with allocator_sealed masked, else INVALID_STATE); g_virtual_now, g_seeded_entropy = KERNEL (k->virtual_now, k->seeded_entropy; readers scheduler.c:477, cancellation.c:33, replay.c:31, lab.c:155,179; writers scheduler.c:982,1338, parallel.c:1085, lab.c:83,156,171, replay.c:58, interpreter.c:4956,5948; asx_runtime_virtual_now/advance/set_internal take k). P1: the scheduler advances it.
Fault injection (hooks.c g_faults, g_fault_*): TOOL.
Trace (trace.c; 15): ring, counters, digest, observer, lock = KERNEL (k->trace; internal (k, ...); public emit derives k from the entity handle; getters gain rt: callers journal.c:144,145,250, journal_replay.c:279, hindsight.c:113, diagnostic.c:136,138, lab.c:32,235, regression_localize.c:94-109, browser_diagnostic.c:217); replay reference = TOOL. P1 (digest identity is per runtime).
Scheduler (scheduler.c; 13): g_current_task (restore outer, A7), sweep/scope scratch (per call; per kernel), event log = TOOL, wake timers live in the process wheel (A2). P1.
Lifecycle/cancellation scratch (g_subtree_*, g_propagate_*, g_member_order; 7): per call, no callback in the loop except the trace observer; guard nested use with asx_task_current() != INVALID. No change needed.
Reset-hook table (lifecycle.c g_reset_hooks; 1): PROCESS, idempotent, run only from the process-clear half.
Replay snapshots (replay.c g_snapshots; 2): KERNEL-by-id: tag in asx_snapshot_id; take/restore use the lab's kernel clock. P2.
Journal/replay (journal.c, journal_replay.c; 3): PROCESS, one stream (D).
Event log, hindsight, telemetry, diagnostic stack, deadline monitor, automotive/hft instruments, router adapter (event_log 8, hindsight 6, telemetry 5, diagnostic 2, deadline_monitor 4, automotive 5, hft 3, vertical_adapter 1): TOOL; shared diagnostics accepted, no per-runtime fix unless a runtime wants its own ring (emit would derive k from entity_id). The first three are written from the trace/hook paths with entity 0, so a per-runtime ring needs the hook ctx.
rt.c (g_active_io_backend, g_rt_generation; 2): PROCESS/D; second init must request the same backend; generation monotonic.
Cancel witnesses (cancel.c; 5): KERNEL, one global 64-slot table (bd-f5bs adds asx_cancel_reset_internal(tag) in the working tree: releases only that tag's witnesses; table still global); chain limits g_chain_max_depth/memory = PROCESS/D (second init must have equal limits). P2.
Timers (timer_wheel.c; 8): runtime wheel + app wheel = KERNEL (wheel per kernel, or tag in the token). P1 because the scheduler uses it.
Waker (waker.c; 6): KERNEL, 64-entry table, asx_waker carries no tag. P2 (needed by io/blocking in P3).
Wait queue (wait_queue.c; 5): KERNEL, 256-node pool, node index global, same-task compare tag-blind (A2). P2.
Sync primitives (barrier 2, contended_mutex 2, notify 2, once 2, pool 2, rwlock 2, semaphore 2): KERNEL, tables of 16-ish slots, handles untagged. P2.
Channels (mpsc 3, oneshot 2, watch 2, broadcast 5, session 2): KERNEL; mpsc mints tag 0; g_channel_count is write-only (dead); g_permit_serial deliberately never reset (monotonic). P2.
Actors/supervisor/gen_server/link/monitor/cx (3+2+2+3+2+1): KERNEL (gen_server and cx PROCESS: arena of {slot, generation}, uniqueness stamp). P2.
Core diagnostics (adaptive 7, affinity 3, ghost 13, status 6, symbol 2, epoch 2): PROCESS/TOOL, none needed, except status (slot-only key, A2: add the tag).
Lab dispatch (lab_dispatch.c; 50): KERNEL. Design: one lab_ctx (11.5 KB at R1, 44.4 KB unclassed; lanes + handle aborts + region commands = ~87%), static instance g_lab_ctx0 for kernel 0 behind asx_kernel.lab (+8 B per kernel, no .bss change; lab_dispatch.o is already linked because clear names its reset); a second lab brings its own ctx (a member of asx_lab or runtime_config.lab_storage), not embedded in asx_kernel (+11.5 KB per storage block at R1). Signatures: lab_kernel() becomes a k argument; 24 handle-less hooks and 13 public calls gain k/rt/lab; refusal tickets gain the tag. P2-late.
Parallel (parallel.c; 23): KERNEL. One par_ctx (6.0 KB at R1 with 64 workers, 3.6 KB with 4), g_par_ctx0 behind asx_kernel.par; the 8 per-slot arrays stay per ctx (moving them into asx_task_slot would cost ~25 B per slot for everyone); 18 handle-less calls gain rt. A parallel run still reaches kernel-0 globals outside this file (scheduler fire_due_timers/next_timer :482, waker, io driver, blocking pool, trace ring). P2-late.
io driver / blocking pool (io_driver 6, blocking 6): KERNEL/D (one reactor and one worker pool per process by nature). asx_io_token, asx_waker, asx_blocking_handle untagged (A3); counts ignore rt (A6). P3.
Net (net.c 15, pipe 1, quic 3, tls 1, websocket 1): socket/listener/udp/dns tables = KERNEL for the memory backend, D for native. Native sockets hold OS fds. P3.
Fs (6), process (2 + posix 5), signal (3 + posix 8): memory backend = KERNEL, native = D (a signal handler and its self-pipe are process-wide; first signal_pump drains the shared pipe, so a second runtime would never see the signal). Logical clocks (posix hooks.c:74, win32 hooks.c:71): no cheap predicate; move into the hooks ctx. P3.
App/cli/console/report (app 1, report 2, cli 2, console 1): TOOL, except g_app_shutdown_watch (move into asx_app).
Conformance harness (interpreter.c 49, canon.c 8): TOOL, one scenario at a time through the kernel-0 bridge; interpreter g_budget points at a stack local of conformance_run (:5887) and dangles after it returns (H5; harmless, noted).
Handle-keyed only (HANDLE 19): g_cause (link.c), one object in src/runtime (g1 table), and 17 adapter slot tables whose lookups already go through a tagged handle once A3 is fixed.

== C. HANDLE-LESS ENTRY POINTS (no handle, rt or kernel) AND THEIR FIX ==
- asx_region_open(out) -> (rt, out) [D2, last in phase 1].
- asx_runtime_reset(void) -> asx_runtime_reset(rt): clears only kernel_for_tag(rt->tag). 951 call sites in tests/src/examples; D2 as approved does not cover it, needs its own decision (see mail).
- asx_resource_used/remaining/snapshot_get/admit(kind...) (resource.c:97,108,115,130), asx_obligation_leak_count(void), asx_runtime_snapshot_capture(snap), asx_oracle_check_named(name) -> take const asx_runtime *rt.
- asx_runtime_virtual_now/advance/set_internal, asx_cancel_now_internal -> take k.
- asx_cancel_reason_default(kind, msg) (public core/cancel.h:50), asx_region_close_reason_internal(void): origin_region read from kernel 0 slot 0. Internal callers holding a handle use asx_kernel_of: lifecycle.c:1163,1186,1461,1462, scheduler.c:803, task_group.c:61,169,173,600, lifecycle.c:1043, lab_dispatch.c:1165; callers needing rt: supervisor.c (10 sites), link.c:288, interpreter.c:2450,2532, doctor.c:640.
- asx_scheduler_fire_due_timers_internal(void), asx_scheduler_next_timer_internal(out), asx_scheduler_reset_internal(void) -> take k.
- asx_trace_* getters, asx_trace_set_observer, asx_replay_* reference API, asx_trace_export/import_binary, asx_trace_continuity_check, asx_snapshot_capture -> take rt (emit variants take k; asx_trace_user(task) already has a handle).
- asx_task_current(void): keep (PROCESS), restore outer in sched_poll_slot.
- asx_scheduler_stuck_tasks(region...) and asx_lab_run_forced_schedule: take a region but resolve lab_kernel() = kernel 0 by slot index (lab_dispatch.c:66) -> derive from the region handle.
- The remaining handle-less calls of lab (24 hooks, 13 public) and parallel (18) are listed in the g4 table (a).

== D. GUARD DESIGN (what I will implement; AmberSummit's 5098 condition, named refusal) ==
Init-time "unthreaded subsystem not in use" predicates alone are UNSOUND: a second runtime could start using an unthreaded subsystem after a clean init and collide with the first. Sound rule, two parts:
 R1 (init). A second runtime is accepted only if every still-unthreaded subsystem reports nothing live (predicates below). Otherwise ASX_E_INVALID_STATE and asx_runtime_last_refusal_reason() returns "handle-less subsystem <X> still process-wide (<predicate>)".
 R2 (use). While two or more runtimes are live, every unthreaded subsystem's entry that creates or acquires state (channel create, timer arm, waker register, sync init, actor spawn, link/monitor create, lab/parallel enable, native adapter open, ...) returns ASX_E_INVALID_STATE with the same named reason. Existing handles of that subsystem cannot exist (R1) and none are created (R2).
Predicates (all verified readable; each needs a small *_in_use_internal() accessor because the variables are static): trace asx_trace_emitted_total() != 0 or observer set; hooks asx_runtime_get_hooks() != NULL && !byte_equal; fault asx_fault_injection_count() != 0; event log/hindsight/telemetry counts (or accept shared diagnostics); journal asx_journal_active(); replay asx_replay_active(); snapshots any asx_snapshot_is_valid; diagnostic asx_diagnostic_current() != NULL; io backend differs; scheduler asx_task_current() != INVALID at init and at asx_scheduler_run entry; cancel witnesses any active from another tag; chain limits differ; timers asx_timer_active_count(runtime wheel) != 0 || app wheel; wait pool asx_wait_nodes_in_use() != 0; sync g_slot_count != 0 per file (pool.c:45, contended_mutex.c:25, notify.c:52, once.c:41, rwlock.c:89, semaphore.c:90, barrier.c:46); mpsc g_channel_hwm != 0; oneshot/watch/session g_slot_count != 0; broadcast g_slot_count != 0 || g_credit_live != 0; waker asx_waker_active_count() != 0; actor g_live_servers != 0 || g_actor_hwm != 0; supervisor g_sup_hwm != 0; link asx_link_count() != 0; monitor asx_monitor_count() != 0; lab asx_lab_dispatch_active() (tested BEFORE bind/clear: clear itself runs the lab reset, rt.c:195 vs :199-200); parallel asx_parallel_is_initialized() || g_run_active; io driver asx_io_driver_is_initialized() || asx_io_active_count() != 0; blocking pool asx_blocking_pool_is_initialized() || active_count != 0; net backend != MEMORY or any listener/stream/udp/unix hwm, socket, dns job; fs backend != MEMORY, entries/open files; process backend != MEMORY, any alive/in_use/detached; signal backend == NATIVE, subscriptions, shutdown_requested, refcount/installed; posix reactor g_reactor_ctx.count != 0; app g_app_shutdown_watch.main_task != INVALID; reset-hook slots registered.
No predicate possible (must move first): posix/win32 logical clock.

== E. PROPOSED PHASE 1 SCOPE FOR TEST (d), needs AmberSummit's decision ==
Test (d) as specified (two runtimes, interleaved region/task/obligation ops, independent quiesce, ASan) cannot be honest unless these are per kernel first, because the scheduler touches all of them: (1) split clear (A1) and per-kernel object reset; (2) virtual clock + seeded entropy (k->virtual_now); (3) timer wheel per kernel (or tag in the token); (4) trace ring/digest per kernel; (5) g_current_task restore (A7); (6) status ledger key with tag; (7) asx_cancel_reset_internal is already tag-aware (bd-f5bs). Everything else stays unthreaded under guard R1+R2 with a named reason. Then D2, then the guard flip, then test (d).

Not closed; AmberSummit closes.

IcyStream: footprint evidence for K18 (compile-only probe of sizeof(asx_kernel) at f769814 + 36b627a, gcc -std=c99, LP64; nothing linked or run):
- default class (8 regions / 64 tasks / 128 obligations / 128 timers / 1024 trace): sizeof(asx_kernel) = 213,856 B
- R1 (4 / 16 / 16, 32 timers, 64 trace): 84,464 B
- R2 (16 / 64 / 64, 128 timers, 256 trace): 337,472 B

title: Async finalizers: port Scope::defer_async (masked, serialized barrier, poll/time budget, escalation) and wire finalizer_* config
description: Found by the 2026-10-12 reality check. C has only synchronous region finalizers (asx_region_register_finalizer / asx_region_defer_sync) plus cleanup-task spawns. Rust's Scope::defer_async runs async finalizers in a masked, serialized barrier during region Finalizing, bounded by a 100-poll / 5 s budget with BoundedLog escalation (pinned rev 5e60b1c4c). The runtime config fields finalizer_poll_budget, finalizer_time_budget_ns and finalizer_escalation are validated and stored but nothing reads them (README Hot Config Reload says so). In Rust, Finalizing admission is reachable only through defer_async, so K5's must-fail admission fixture also needs this. Work: C API for async finalizers (poll function + user data) run one at a time, masked, during Finalizing, with the config budgets and escalation; DSL v2 op in both interpreters; snapshot projection; Rust fixtures for order, budget exhaustion/escalation and Finalizing admission.

- [ ] C async-finalizer API; finalizers run serially, masked, in LIFO registration order during Finalizing
- [ ] finalizer_poll_budget / finalizer_time_budget_ns / finalizer_escalation are honoured (unit tests for each escalation mode)
- [ ] DSL v2 op + twin_run projection; >= 4 Rust fixtures (order, poll-budget exhaustion, time-budget escalation, Finalizing admission refusal) pass in make conformance

title: K3 Spawn completion policy: keep Ok/Err value when cancel acknowledged after first poll (Rust Aug-2026 semantics)
description:
## Drift
Since `16c065d8a` / `6b24c8f30` (Aug 12), an ordinary Rust spawn keeps an Ok or Err value
returned by user code that acknowledged a cancel arriving *after* the first poll
(`/dp/asupersync/src/runtime/task_handle.rs:156`). Structured combinators and JoinSet still report
Cancelled.

C maps any completion with a pending cancel to CANCELLED (`src/runtime/scheduler.c:752-762`).

## Fix
1. Track, per task, whether the cancel was requested before the first poll and whether user code
   acknowledged it.
2. Add a per-spawn completion policy: `ASX_COMPLETION_RETAIN_VALUE` (default for ordinary spawn,
   per Rust) and `ASX_COMPLETION_CANCELLED` (used by combinators, task groups and join_set).
3. Apply Rust's classification in `asx_task_join_poll`, task-group status and outcome
   aggregation. Cite the exact Rust predicate at the pinned rev.

## Tests
A 2×2×2 matrix:
- cancel before or after the first poll;
- acknowledged or not;
- ordinary spawn or combinator member.

Each cell's expected result is taken from Rust. Fixtures: task_lifecycle "value-after-ack"
family. Metamorphic M10.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);

title: K4 Region close semantics: body-outcome-driven close, drain reason propagation, finalizers->leak audit->close ordering, close_outcome
description:
## Drift
Rust anchors: `/dp/asupersync/src/cx/scope.rs:880-900`; `src/record/region.rs:1658, 1786`;
`src/runtime/state.rs:10118`. Relevant upstream commit: `87124a690` (May 7), "a cancelled region
with no live work closes Cancelled, not Ok".

| Aspect | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| Region body returned Ok | waits for child tasks without cancelling them | — |
| Body Cancelled/Err/Panicked | cancels children with that reason (or FailFast) | — |
| Descendants | get ParentCancelled | — |
| `asx_region_drain` | — | cancels the root region's own tasks with PARENT, not the requested kind |
| Close ordering | run finalizers, then leak-audit leftover obligations under the leak policy, then close | checks obligations first and stops with `ASX_E_OBLIGATIONS_UNRESOLVED` (`src/runtime/quiescence.c:243`) |
| Finalizers | run | skipped |
| Close outcome | recorded; Cancelled when the region was cancelled | never recorded |
| Obligations without a holder | not allowed | allowed |

## Fix
1. Drain takes a cancel reason: the root region's tasks get that kind, descendants get PARENT.
2. Add a close that waits without cancelling (the Ok-body path).
3. Record a region `cancel_reason` and a `close_outcome`, computed by joining with a Cancelled
   default when the region was cancelled.
4. Ordering: run cleanup and finalizers (the cleanup stack, LIFO), then leak-audit any leftover
   obligations under the configured leak policy (K6), then close.
5. Obligations must have a holder. Reject unowned reserves (`asx_obligation_reserve` outside a
   task, without `_ex`) with a documented status, or audit them at close as Rust does. Pick the
   Rust behaviour and cite it.
6. Map each step to the v4 rules CLOSE-BEGIN, CLOSE-CANCEL-CHILDREN, CLOSE-CHILDREN-DONE,
   CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER and CLOSE-COMPLETE, and update `docs/C_REFINEMENT_MAP.md`.
7. README: quiescence section (L1063-1078) and region drain text (L770).

## Tests
- Unit and invariant tests for each close path (Ok body, Err body, cancelled, drain with each
  reason, nested 3 levels, finalizer LIFO order, leftover obligation under each leak policy).
- Fixtures: region_lifecycle family.
- The e2e `nested_regions.sh` updated.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.
4. **Tests are required.**
   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.
   - E2E scripts emit detailed structured JSONL logs: `ts`, `run_id`, `layer`, `suite`, `test`,
     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.
5. **Never delete a file or directory without explicit written owner permission**
   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.
6. **Don't run code-modifying scripts** (AGENTS.md). Make code changes manually.
7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.
8. **Close only with evidence.** The close reason must name test names, gate output and artifact
   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.
9. **Rust line numbers drift.** Treat cited `file:line` anchors as grep starting points and
   re-verify them at the pinned rev.

## Real-work worksheet

Inventory examined: git log --stat, current complete production/test/gate diffs, reflog, recent closed Beads ordered by updated_at, and original open task descriptions. Original K4, K5 and K18 remain in_progress. The older closes precede this implementation window. Exactly one class per work unit:

2. USER: K4 public synchronous finalizers, callback-before-ledger ordering, exactly-once reentrancy, actual cleanup completion, nested cancellation and recycled-region drain fixes.

Three agents made small doc/citation and fixture setup changes; none shipped an independently closed feature or tracker close. Root implemented and reviewed runtime behavior, then reran their tests as part of the whole suite.

title: K5 Finalizing admission: reject normal spawns while region Finalizing; add cleanup-only spawn entry (Rust 59bdc2baa)
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** (`/dp/asupersync/src/record/region.rs:140`) admits normal work only while Open
  (`:150` is the cleanup-work predicate). Commit `59bdc2baa` (Apr 30) split Finalizing admission
  into normal work (rejected) and cleanup-only work (allowed). Commit `f4bcaba9c` (Oct 1): work
  started during cleanup does not inherit the cleanup quota.
- **C.** `asx_region_can_accept_work` returns true for Finalizing (transition tables), and
  `asx_task_spawn` uses it (`src/runtime/lifecycle.c:783`).

## Fix
1. Make `can_accept_work` true only for Open.
2. Add `asx_region_can_accept_cleanup_work` and `asx_task_spawn_cleanup` (or a spawn flag).
3. Cleanup tasks get a fresh budget, not the inherited cleanup quota (per `f4bcaba9c`). Verify
   against the Rust source.
4. Update the transition-table docs and the refinement map.

## Tests
- Spawn in each region state × {normal, cleanup}; the expected statuses come from Rust.
- Fixtures: region_lifecycle admission family, including a must-fail fixture.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**

title: K7 Cancel attribution parity: timestamps, bounded cause chains, immediate-parent origin, epoch-once, message tie-break, kind ordinals
description:
## Drift
Rust anchors: `/dp/asupersync/src/types/cancel.rs:198` (chain depth 16, 4096 bytes),
`:956` (strengthen), `:264, 473, 1027`; `state.rs:7691-7750`.

| Aspect | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| Cause chain | set | never set; the `max_cancel_chain_*` config knobs (`asx_config.h`) do nothing |
| Timestamps | stamped | always 0 |
| Origin for descendants | the immediate parent | the root region |
| Strengthen | full rule | only the kind changes, and there is no message tie-break; Rust orders by severity, then earlier timestamp, then smaller message (`cancel.c:52`, `cancellation.c:44-51`) |
| `cancel_epoch` | bumped on the first request only | bumped on every repeated request |
| Witness | — | no region or epoch; rejects a repeated phase |
| Ordinals | `LinkedExit=10, Shutdown=9` | `LinkedExit=7, Shutdown=10` |
| Display strings | — | differ |

The ordinal and display differences break binary codec and digest parity whenever kinds are
ordinal-encoded.

## Owner decision D1
Align the ordinals with Rust now. This is an ABI break, but AGENTS.md says no backward
compatibility is needed. Recommendation: align, **and** encode kinds by name in the canonical
vocabulary (W1.2).

## Fix
1. Stamp the current logical time on every cancel request.
2. Build bounded cause chains: depth 16, 4096 bytes, with truncation metadata.
3. Origin is the immediate parent.
4. Bump the epoch on the first request only.
5. Strengthen copies the whole reason, including the message tie-break.
6. Outcome carries the reason (with K14).
7. Align ordinals and display names.
8. Make the config knobs effective.

## Tests
- Unit tests for the strengthen ordering (severity, then timestamp, then message), chain
  truncation at both bounds, epoch-once.
- Fixtures: cancel family, attribution subfamily.
- `check-rust-constants` (W1.12) for the ordinals.

title: [S] Scheduler parity: Rust lab scheduling-model contract, lanes, seeded picker, dispatch certificates
description:
## Why
The C scheduler polls every runnable task each round in ascending arena index. It has no lanes,
no priority and no seed, and it re-polls Pending tasks that were not woken. Rust's lab runtime
does something different each step:
- draws from a recorded xorshift64 RNG;
- picks a lane: cancel (streak limit 16), then due timed tasks (EDF), then ready;
- picks among tied highest-priority tasks with `rng % len`;
- polls exactly one task.

As a result, trace parity is impossible for any scenario with two or more runnable tasks, and
budget priority has no effect in C.

## Scope
- A scheduling-model contract extracted from Rust.
- A C lab dispatch mode implementing it exactly, with dispatch certificates equal to Rust's
  `ScheduleCertificate`.
- Pending-without-wake semantics.
- Cancel-lane promotion.
- Lab clock semantics.
- Lanes and priority in the production scheduler.
- Lane order in `asx_parallel_run`.

## Done when
Dispatch-certificate equality with Rust holds on all scheduler fixtures and on random scenarios
(N ≥ 20k).

title: S0 Scheduling-model contract: extract Rust LabRuntime step semantics exactly (RNG, lanes, wake order, spawn enqueue, time) with file:line
description:
## Why
Exact trace parity (W1 mode c) and dispatch-certificate equality need a precise, written contract
for how Rust's lab runtime picks the next task. "Add three lanes" is nowhere near specific enough.

## Extract, citing file:line at the pinned rev (`/dp/asupersync`)
Sources: `src/lab/runtime.rs` (step around `:4499-4515` and `:6324-6399`),
`src/runtime/scheduler/priority.rs` (`:417-421`, `:547-610`, `:759-790`, `:861`),
`src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs` (`:166`, `:1280`), `src/util/det_rng.rs`,
`src/lab/config.rs` (`:199`, `auto_advance` defaults to false), and the formal semantics
§1.11 and §3.0 (rules ENQUEUE and SCHEDULE-STEP, plus "Scheduler fairness").

1. **Step definition.** In order:
   - timer firing (and whether it is gated by `auto_advance`);
   - wake draining;
   - lane choice;
   - task choice;
   - one poll;
   - handling of wakes produced during the poll (enqueue position);
   - the "yield" semantics.
2. **RNG.**
   - xorshift64 (`det_rng.rs`).
   - Seed derivation from `LabConfig.seed`, including degenerate-seed remapping
     (`det_rng.rs:126-167`).
   - Draw points: every step, only on ties, or also for worker choice.
   - Index mapping (`rng % len`).
   - Whether draws are recorded in the certificate.
3. **Lanes.**
   - Membership rules: when a task enters the cancel lane (on request or on acknowledgement).
   - Priority sources: cleanup priority (200/210/215/220/255 per cancel kind) vs budget priority.
   - The cancel-streak limit of 16, widened to 2× during DrainObligations/DrainRegions, and the
     fallback when the cancel lane is the only work.
   - The timed lane: EDF by (deadline, seq), and when a timed task counts as "due".
4. **Ties.** Group size cap (256?) and order within the group (wake order).
5. **Wake order.** Tail enqueue or a LIFO slot (the October perf change added a LIFO slot for a
   task woken by the running task; does the lab mirror it?), and wake deduplication.
6. **Spawn enqueue.** Runnable at once or after the parent's poll returns, and the position.
7. **Time.** `advance_to_next_timer` / `run_with_auto_advance` semantics, the 1 ms wheel tick and
   coalescing.
8. **Optional: multi-worker lab.** How the virtual worker is chosen per step, if
   `worker_count > 1`.
9. **The ScheduleCertificate** (`lab/runtime.rs:2576`): its exact contents and hashing.

## Deliverable
`docs/SCHEDULING_MODEL_CONTRACT.md`:
- normative pseudo-code;
- citations for every statement;
- a section of worked examples (3-task scenarios with expected step sequences) that become W1.7
  scheduler fixtures.

## Success criteria
A reviewer can implement S1 from the doc alone. Each worked example matches a real Rust run
captured by twin_run, attached as an artifact.

title: sweep scheduler: a task spawned into a region opened this round is skipped until the next round (yield gives it no turn)
description:
Found by bd-9kll.4.9 (compare-sweep over the 186 v2 fixtures at 811ac3f).

**Defect.** `sched_run` computes the round's scope once (`sched_compute_scope`) before the walk. A region a task opens *during* the round is not in that scope, so `sweep_walk`'s tail visits a task spawned into it, finds `sched_scope_region(t) == NULL` and skips it. The task waits for the next round. A `yield` in the opener therefore does not give the new task a turn: in round 2 the opener (lower arena index) runs again first.

Scenario shape (3 fixtures): `t.parent` opens `r.c`, spawns `t.worker` into `r.c`, yields, then `cancel_region r.c`. Under the sweep the cancel lands before the worker's first poll, the worker's `server_spawn` is refused (REGION_CLOSED), and its next op fails with "unknown or stopped server". Under Rust's ready queue the spawned worker is queued before the parent's yield re-queue, so it runs first.

Fixtures (sweep_known_divergences.txt, reason `drift bd-...`):
- actor-cancel-after-batch-drains-call-001
- actor-cancel-caller-and-server-001
- actor-cancel-idle-server-001

**Fix sketch** (src/runtime/scheduler.c only): in `sched_run`, where `rslot = sched_scope_region(t); if (rslot == NULL) continue;`, when `i >= g_sweep_listed` (spawned this round) recompute the scope once and look again. One recompute marks the new region for the rest of the round; tasks the snapshot never listed that stay out of scope are skipped as now.

**Test.** test_scheduler.c: a task opens a child region, spawns into it, yields; assert the child's task is polled before the opener resumes. Then the 3 fixtures turn into STALE entries, which the runner fails on, so the list must shrink with the fix.

Not verified by a run (no builds this window): diagnosis is from the log + scheduler.c:1555-1575 and the scenario programs.

title: sweep scheduler: poll-quota exhaustion is stamped with (region, task, now) instead of CancelReason::poll_quota() defaults (Rust lab and production both use the defaults)
description:
Found by bd-9kll.4.9 (compare-sweep, 811ac3f).

**Defect.** `sched_enforce_budget` (scheduler.c:774-790) stamps an exhausted poll quota with Rust's `CancelReason::poll_quota()` testing defaults only under lab dispatch. The non-lab branch calls `asx_task_cancel_budget_internal(tid, POLL_QUOTA, now)`, which stamps (task's region, task, now).

Rust's **production** scheduler does the same as its lab: `three_lane.rs::consume_budget_poll` (5e60b1c4c, L1280-1305) sets the Cx cancel with `CancelReason::poll_quota()` ("as the lab does") and a later `Cx::checkpoint` re-attributes it with `(region, now, task)`, the earlier timestamp winning (cx.rs:3112-3160). So the sweep's exhaustion-time stamp diverges from both Rust schedulers; the checkpoint then keeps the earlier (exhaustion-time) stamp instead of its own.

Fixtures with PollQuota provenance/outcome differences under the sweep:
- budget-quota-cx-reason-at-completion-001 (origin root/null/1e9 vs r.main/t.1/250)
- budget-quota-cx-reason-reconciled-001 (ts 200 vs 150: re-attribution at the checkpoint lost to the earlier exhaustion stamp)
- cancel-cleanup-budget-advisory-001
- lab-dispatch-cancel-waker-once-001
- cancel-request-event-reason-001 (Rust's task ends PollQuota; sweep keeps User)
- region-lifecycle-closed-child-spawn-001 (Rust t.1 cancelled PollQuota, sweep completes ok)

The last two may have a second cause once the stamp is fixed; re-run compare-sweep after the change and list what remains.

**Fix sketch** (scheduler.c): drop the `asx_lab_dispatch_active()` gate on the poll-quota branch so the sweep calls `asx_task_cancel_reason_internal(tid, &asx_cancel_reason_default(POLL_QUOTA, NULL), ASX_CANCEL_SRC_BUDGET)` too. cancellation.c's SRC_BUDGET path is already mode independent (it wakes the slot in non-lab). Existing unit assertions (test_cancellation.c:2045-2049 origin == rid/tid) keep holding because the checkpoint re-attributes with an earlier timestamp.

Not verified by a run.

title: sweep scheduler: pre-poll deadline enforcement cancels cleanup tasks / region finalizers that Rust arms no deadline timer for
description:
Found by bd-9kll.4.9 (compare-sweep, 811ac3f).

**Defect.** Under the sweep, `sched_enforce_budget` (scheduler.c:760-773) cancels any task whose budget deadline has passed *before polling it*, with no exemption for cleanup tasks / region finalizers. Rust arms no deadline timer for a cleanup task (create_task_infrastructure_in, state.rs:4401; the lab path here skips `asx_lab_arm_budget_deadline_internal` for finalizers), so the finalizer's FINALIZER_TIME_BUDGET_NANOS (5 s) deadline stays advisory until a masked checkpoint evaluates it (cx.rs:3112-3160).

Fixture: region-finalizer-time-budget-advisory-001: Rust `is_cancel_requested` at step 2 is false, the sweep reports true (the pre-poll enforcement cancelled the sleeping finalizer's task at its wake-up).

**Fix sketch**: in the non-lab deadline branch of `sched_enforce_budget` skip tasks with `t->cleanup_only` (finalizers are spawned cleanup_only by `asx_task_spawn_finalizer_internal`). The parked-deadline wake arm below it (`timer_arm`, the SWEEP_PARKED_DEADLINE_NO_WAKE mutant site) needs the same exemption.

Not verified by a run.

title: checkpoint outside lab dispatch does not strengthen a pending cancel with a passed budget deadline (Rust checkpoint_budget_exhaustion does)
description:
Found by bd-9kll.4.9 (compare-sweep, 811ac3f).

**Defect.** `asx_checkpoint` (cancellation.c:633-645) evaluates a passed budget deadline only `(asx_lab_dispatch_active() || !t->cancel_pending)` and stamps the *deadline itself* instead of `now` outside lab dispatch. Rust's `checkpoint_budget_exhaustion` (cx.rs:3112-3160) is the same code in the lab and the production runtime: a passed deadline is a DEADLINE candidate stamped now that strengthens a cancel already pending. The non-lab gate means a task already cancel-pending with a weaker kind (User) never gets the stronger Deadline its Cx holds.

Fixture: cancel-region-request-lane-priority-001 (now_ns 150 vs 100). Rust's child keeps the Cx's Deadline, so its sleep does not end on the supervisor's User cancel and the run reaches 150 (a Timeout/Deadline-kind sleep keeps waiting, sleep.rs:788-794; asx_sleep_poll mirrors that). The sweep's child record stays User, its sleep ends at the cancel and the run stops at 100.

**Fix sketch**: drop the `asx_lab_dispatch_active() ||` / `!cancel_pending` split and the `stamp` special case (stamp `now`, strengthen a pending cancel) in the checkpoint; keep the pre-poll deadline path in `sched_enforce_budget` stamping the deadline for a task that has no timer. Check test_cancellation.c / test_budget_obligation.c deadline tests that pin the non-lab stamp (they were written against the old behaviour).

Cause is read from the code and the fixture description; not verified by a run.

title: S1 C lab dispatch mode implementing the scheduling-model contract exactly (one task/step, lanes, wake seq, xorshift64 replica, dispatch certificate)
description:
## Drift
`src/runtime/scheduler.c:615-790` sweeps all runnable tasks each round in ascending arena index:
- no lanes;
- no priority;
- no seed;
- re-polls Pending tasks that weren't woken (`:768-770`).

Rust's lab polls one task per step, choosing by lane, then priority, then wake order, then a
seeded RNG tie-break. So C trace digests can't match Rust's whenever two or more tasks are
runnable at once.

## Implementation (allocation-free, deterministic, static arenas)
1. `asx_scheduler_mode` in `asx_runtime_config`: `ASX_SCHED_LAB_STEP`, the default when
   `ASX_DETERMINISTIC=1` (decide and document), or `ASX_SCHED_SWEEP` (legacy; remove once
   parity is reached; AGENTS says no tech debt).
2. Data structures:
   - per-lane priority structures over task indices: a binary heap keyed by
     (priority desc, wake_seq asc) for cancel and ready, and (deadline, seq) for timed;
   - a per-task `wake_seq` counter;
   - a tie-group gather of ≤ 256 entries.
3. RNG: an exact replica of Rust's xorshift64, including seed derivation and degenerate-seed
   remapping. Unit-test it against a Rust-generated sequence (the first 1000 values for 5 seeds,
   captured by twin_run).
4. Each draw is recorded into a dispatch log, from which the C dispatch certificate is computed
   per S0 §9. The certificate must equal Rust's for the same scenario.
5. Pending-without-wake is not runnable (S2), and cancel-lane promotion (S3) is included where
   the contract places it.

## Success criteria
- The certificate equals Rust's on every scheduler fixture and on ≥ 20k random DSL v2 scenarios
  via twin_run fuzz.
- W1 mode (c) passes.
- Performance: no heap allocation on the hot path. A bench (P1) confirms the per-step overhead.

## Tests
- Unit tests: RNG replica, lane selection, streak limit, tie-group gather.
- CBMC harness for lane selection (bounded queues).
- e2e `tests/e2e/scheduler_certificate_parity.sh` logs per-scenario certificate hashes on both
  sides.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Authority.**
- The semantic authority is Rust asupersync at `/dp/asupersync`, commit `5e60b1c4c` (Cargo
  `0.6.0`, not on crates.io).
- Pin it by git rev: `git = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync", rev = "5e60b1c4c..."`.
- The normative spec is `/dp/asupersync/asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md`. Its Canonical Rule
  Index supplies the rule names used as spec tags, for example SPAWN, SCHEDULE-STEP,
  CANCEL-REQUEST, strengthen, CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGE, CHECKPOINT-MASKED, CLOSE-RUN-FINALIZER,
  RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK.
- Rust maps its own code to those rules in `/dp/asupersync/formal/impl_refinement_map.md`.

**Rules for every bridge bead.**
1. **Semantic delta budget is 0.** Resource-plane differences (arena sizes, worker counts, profile
   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:
   - land C unit and invariant tests that pin the Rust behaviour, citing the Rust file:line;
   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.
3. **Gates fail closed.** A missing tool, zero comparisons or an unknown op is a FAILURE, never
   SKIP-as-pass. Before closing, run:
   - `make build test format-check lint` with `STRICT_GATES=1` (or the equivalent pinned
     clang-format: `uvx --from clang-format==18.1.8 clang-format`);
   - plus `make conformance` once the real oracle exists.
4. **Tests are required.**
   - Unit tests cover the happy path, edge cases (empty, max, boundary) and error paths.
   - E2E scripts emit detailed structured JSONL logs: `ts`, `run_id`, `layer`, `suite`, `test`,
     `status`, `seed`, `profile`, `codec`, `rust_rev`, `c_git_sha`, and the first divergence on
     failure.
5. **Never delete a file or directory without explicit written owner permission**
   (AGENTS.md RULE 1). This includes files you created. Ask first.
6. **Don't run code-modifying scripts** (AGENTS.md). Make code changes manually.
7. **Offload heavy builds and tests** with `rch exec -- <cmd>`.
8. **Close only with evidence.** The close reason must name test names, gate output and artifact
   paths. Update the README and docs in the same change whenever a claim changes.
9. **Rust line numbers drift.** Treat cited `file:line` anchors as grep starting points and
   re-verify them at the pinned rev.

Orientation-only living plan: `docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md`. This bead is meant to be
sufficient on its own.
notes: Refinement r1: also update the README claims that describe the old sweep (README L711 'ascending arena index within each round', L713 implicit yield, L715-720 round description) to describe the lab step dispatcher. That was plan item S7, folded in here.

title: S2 Pending-without-wake must not be re-polled; yield becomes an explicit self-wake
description:
## Drift
- **C.** A task returning `ASX_E_PENDING` without parking is treated as a yield and polled again
  next round (`src/runtime/scheduler.c:768-770`; README L713: "A task that returns ASX_E_PENDING
  without parking simply yields").
- **Rust.** A Pending future is polled again only when woken. A yield wakes itself explicitly
  (`yield_now`).

## Fix
1. Pending without a registered wake means parked until woken. Detecting "nothing can wake it"
   becomes a futurelock/deadlock diagnostic: the lab reports it (Rust has futurelock detection),
   and the scheduler returns `ASX_E_WOULD_BLOCK` at idle.
2. Add `asx_task_yield(self)`, which self-wakes and returns PENDING, and migrate every internal
   and example poll function that relied on implicit yield. Audit with `rg 'return ASX_E_PENDING'`
   in poll functions.
3. README update.

## Tests
- A poll fn returning PENDING without a wake → never re-polled; the run ends `WOULD_BLOCK` with a
  futurelock diagnostic naming the task.
- With `asx_task_yield` → re-polled.
- Fixtures: scheduler family.


---
### Program context (shared footer: every bridge bead carries this so it is self-contained)

This bead belongs to the **2026-10-08 reality-check bridge program**. The umbrella epic is
"Reality-check bridge: make asx a proven, Rust-faithful port of asupersync 0.6.0".

**Background.** The 2026-10-08 audit of `asx` at commit `c808a6e` found four problems:
1. **The Rust-parity gates were self-referential.**
   - `make conformance` printed `parity_records=0 comparable_parity_records=0 ... pass=true`.
   - No C code executes a fixture's `input.ops`; `tools/ci/run_conformance.sh` only round-trips
     fixtures through the codec.
   - Most "Rust" fixtures were synthesized by `tools/fixture_capture/src/main.rs` rather than
     recorded from asupersync running. Channel ops are recorded as `user_trace` strings, the
     cancel kind is hardcoded to `User`, and `Budget::meet` is never called.
   - The Rust fuzz differential is skipped by default and informational even when enabled.
2. **Real semantic drift exists against the current Rust reference.** For example, the budget
   priority semiring is reversed (C `min` vs Rust `max`).
3. **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has never passed.** The first job fails at `format-check`,
   so the other seven jobs have never run.
4. **Many README claims are wrong** (counts, code samples, contradictions).

**Rules for every bridge bead.**

   instrumentation) must never change canonical semantics.
2. **A semantic fix ships with fixtures.** It lands together with Rust-captured fixtures (from the
   twin-run oracle, workstream W1) that fail before the fix and pass after it. Until the oracle
   exists:

   - create or point to a follow-up "capture fixtures" task.

title: S3 Cancelled tasks are promoted to the cancel lane with their cleanup priority (Rust priority.rs:861)
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** (`/dp/asupersync/src/runtime/scheduler/priority.rs:861`) moves a cancelled task into
  the cancel lane at its cleanup priority, per kind: 200/210/215/220/255. Verify the mapping.
- **C** (`src/runtime/cancellation.c:89-91`) only unparks the task; it then waits its arena-order
  turn.

## Fix
As part of the S1 lane machinery, cancellation (request or acknowledgement, per the S0 contract)
moves the task to the cancel lane with the cleanup priority from the cancel table. That table is
extracted by W1.12; don't hand-copy it.

## Tests
- A low-priority task cancelled with SHUTDOWN runs before ready tasks; streak-limit fairness
  still holds.
- Fixtures: scheduler/cancel-lane family.

title: S4 Lab clock semantics: frozen virtual clock, auto_advance flag (default off), clock_is_virtual() true for lab
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** `LabConfig.auto_advance` defaults to false (`/dp/asupersync/src/lab/config.rs:199`).
  Time is frozen unless advanced explicitly or by auto-advance.
- **C** always jumps to the next timer when idle (`src/runtime/scheduler.c:577-583`). Under
  `asx_lab` (`src/runtime/lab.c:75`), the clock gains a tick on every read (`tick_ns`), and
  `asx_runtime_clock_is_virtual()` returns 0 for it (`src/runtime/hooks.c:593-600`), so the idle
  jump never happens there.
- Also: `asx_vtime_install`/`uninstall` (`src/runtime/virtual_time.c:164-180`) are no-ops that
  return OK.

## Fix
1. Freeze the lab clock (`tick_ns = 0` by default).
2. `clock_is_virtual()` returns true for the lab and vtime clocks.
3. Idle jump-to-next-timer happens only if `auto_advance` is set (default off, matching Rust);
   explicit advance APIs mirror Rust (`advance_time`, `advance_to_next_timer`).
4. Implement or remove the no-op vtime install/uninstall. Removal needs care; no compatibility
   shims.
5. Update README L1080-1099 and L1412-1436.

## Tests
- A lab scenario with sleeps and no advance → `WOULD_BLOCK`. With `auto_advance` → completes;
  virtual time equals the max deadline.
- Fixtures: timers family.

title: S5 Production (non-lab) scheduler honours lanes and budget priority (priority currently has no effect anywhere in C)
description:
## Why
Even outside the lab, Rust's scheduler uses priority lanes: the cancel lane gets cleanup priority,
EDF applies for timed tasks, and the ready lane uses priority. C ignores budget priority entirely,
so K1's fix would be invisible at runtime.

## Plan
Make the production (live, non-deterministic) path use the same lane structures as S1. Instead of
the seeded RNG, use deterministic FIFO within a priority group, or the same RNG seeded from
entropy (document which, citing Rust's production behaviour in `three_lane.rs`). Keep the hot
path allocation-free and O(log n).

## Tests
- Live-mode test: a high-priority task scheduled ahead of a low one under contention.
- Bench (P1): no regression beyond an agreed threshold. Record before/after numbers.

title: S6 asx_parallel_run lane order (cancel>timed>ready), deadline-ordered timed lane, honour parked tasks
description:
## Drift
`src/runtime/parallel.c:64, 714-718`:
- lane order is CANCEL > READY > TIMED, but Rust's three-lane order is cancel, then timed (EDF
  when due), then ready (`three_lane.rs:166`);
- the timed lane isn't deadline-ordered;
- `parallel_run` ignores `parked`.

The PARALLEL profile's `parallel-parity` gate compares only C against C, so this was never
caught.

## Fix
Unify `parallel_run`'s lane logic with S1/S5's lane structures, so the logical-worker scheduler
selects exactly like Rust's multi-worker scheduler for the same seed. That is the optional
multi-worker lab-parity tier in the S0 contract. Honour parked tasks.

## Tests
- `parallel-parity` remains green.
- New fixtures with `worker_count` 2 and 4 compare against Rust's lab (if the S0 contract covers
  multi-worker), else C-vs-C plus a unit test of the lane order.

title: [C] Channel parity: cancel-safety, permits as obligations, close/drop, watch/broadcast semantics, unbounded waiters
description:
## Why
The C channels differ from Rust in several ways:
- they never observe cancellation; withdrawal needs a manual `wait_cancel`, and forgetting it
  stalls producers;
- permits are not obligations, so a leaked permit eats capacity forever, undetected;
- receiver close always discards the queue;
- there is no sender reference counting;
- watch versions start at 1, so new receivers see phantom changes;
- broadcast returns OK with no receivers and has no lag count;
- waiter queues are capped at 32, beyond which tasks busy-poll and lose FIFO order.

## Done when
Every channel unit is green under the oracle with LB ≥ 99.9%, waiter caps are gone, and the
cancel-storm and waiter-flood e2e tests pass.

title: C6 Shared intrusive unbounded FIFO waiter queues linked through task slots (remove all waiter caps and eviction paths)
description:
## Drift
Rust waiter queues are unbounded (`/dp/asupersync/src/sync/semaphore.rs:149`,
`sync/waiter.rs:49`, VecDeque/Slab). C uses fixed per-primitive waiter arrays:

| Primitive | Cap | When full |
|---|---|---|
| MPSC (per direction) | 32 | busy-polls every round; `wq_evict_woken` (`src/sync/wait_queue.c:118-155`) can cost a woken waiter its FIFO place |
| semaphore/mutex, rwlock, notify | 16 (`semaphore.h:33`, `rwlock.h:34`, `notify.h:36`) | `ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (`semaphore.c:226`, `rwlock.c:316`, `notify.c:217`) |
| barrier | 32 | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (`barrier.c:162`); a barrier with more than 32 parties can never trip |
| once, pool | 8 | busy-polls |

So the 17th task to wait on a mutex gets an error that Rust never produces, and FIFO fairness
breaks under load.

## Design
- Each task slot (`asx_task_slot`) gets a small fixed array of intrusive wait links. Size it with
  `ASX_TASK_MAX_WAIT_LINKS`, default 2-4, enough for select-style waits on a few primitives.
- Each primitive has a FIFO list head/tail of (task index, link index), so waiters are bounded
  only by `ASX_MAX_TASKS`.
- Links are cleared automatically when the task completes or is cancelled, with no manual
  `wait_cancel` (pairs with C1).
- Generation-checked handles throughout.
- No dynamic allocation.

## Plan
1. Implement it in `src/sync/wait_queue.c` (revise in place).
2. Migrate MPSC, oneshot, broadcast, watch, mutex, semaphore, rwlock, barrier, notify, once and
   pool.
3. Remove the eviction path and the cap constants. Keep a compile-time assertion that link count
   ≥ 1.

## Tests
- Waiter-flood test: 1000 tasks (with `ASX_MAX_TASKS` raised via RB4) contend on one mutex;
  acquisition order is exactly FIFO by arrival.
- Same for MPSC reserve.
- Cancel a middle waiter: the hand-off skips it correctly.
- Task completion clears its links (no dangling entries).
- Stress e2e `tests/e2e/waiter_flood.sh` with JSONL logs.

notes: Refinement r2: the per-task wait-link count (ASX_TASK_MAX_WAIT_LINKS) is a resource-plane limit. title: Channel/sync stress e2e: cancel storms, waiter floods (>1000 tasks), barrier rounds, notify-before-wait, permit leaks - with JSONL logs
description:
## Plan
`tests/e2e/primitives_stress.sh`, built with raised `ASX_MAX_TASKS` (RB4):
1. 1000 producers on a capacity-8 MPSC channel, with a random 30% cancelled. Assert FIFO among
   survivors, no stall, all permits resolved, no leaks.
2. 1000 waiters on a mutex: exact FIFO.
3. Barrier with 50 parties × 20 rounds: exactly one trip and one leader per round.
4. Notify-before-wait ×1000: no lost wakeups.
5. Leaked permits under each leak policy.
6. Watch subscribe storm: no phantom changes.
7. Everything runs under ASan/UBSan (E5) and in the deterministic lab with fixed seeds; rolling
   digests (RB1) are logged.

## Success
Green in CI at milestone M-δ.

title: MPSC sender handles: one producer closing twice must not drop another producer's sender
description: Found by the 2026-10-12 reality check. MPSC senders are counted on the channel id (asx_channel_sender_clone / asx_channel_close_sender), not represented as handles: if one producer calls asx_channel_close_sender twice (a double drop), the count drops by two and silently removes another producer's sender, possibly closing the channel under a live producer. Rust's Sender is an owned value; a double drop is impossible. Broadcast already refuses a dropped handle; MPSC cannot. Work: give each sender clone an identity (generation-safe sender handle or token) so close_sender of an already-dropped sender is refused (ASX_E_INVALID_STATE or STALE_HANDLE) without changing the count; update callers, tests, README Channel Families. No compatibility shim.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each clone yields a distinct sender identity; closing an already-closed sender is refused and leaves the count unchanged
- [ ] Unit test: producers A and B; A closes twice; the second close is refused; B can still send; the channel closes only when B also closes
- [ ] All existing mpsc fixtures still pass in make conformance (interpreter updated to the handle API)

title: Channels: release messages that are discarded unreceived (receiver drop, seal-then-drop, eviction), as Rust drops them
description: Found by CalmTrout on 2026-10-12 while closing bd-9kll.5.7. C channel payloads are uint64_t tokens (often pointers to application memory). When a message is discarded without being received (asx_channel_close_receiver drops the queue, a seal followed by the receiver's drop, send_evict_oldest / send_evict_oldest_where, broadcast overwrite of an unread slot), the application gets no notification, so whatever the token refers to leaks. Rust's channels own T and run its Drop for every discarded message. Work: an optional per-channel discard callback (fn + ctx) invoked exactly once for each message dropped without being received, on every discard path and both MPSC backends (identical semantics), plus oneshot/broadcast/watch equivalents where Rust drops values; tests for each path including exactly-once and no call for received messages.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Optional discard callback per channel (MPSC; equivalents for oneshot/broadcast/watch where Rust drops values)
- [ ] Called exactly once per unreceived discarded message on receiver drop, seal-then-drop, eviction and overwrite; never for received messages (unit tests per path, both MPSC backends)
- [ ] No behaviour change when no callback is installed

title: C1 Channel waits are cancel-safe: observe cancellation, return ASX_E_CANCELLED, withdraw, pass the wake on (no manual wait_cancel)
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** checks for cancellation first in reserve and recv: it returns `Cancelled`, removes the
  waiter, and passes the wake on when the Reserve future is dropped
  (`/dp/asupersync/src/channel/mpsc.rs:1003-1012, 1061, 1077-1085, 1225, 1786-1797`).
- **C** channels never check cancellation, and there is no `ASX_E_CANCELLED` anywhere in
  `src/channel/` (`mpsc.c:536-611, 706-751`). Abandoning a wait requires a manual
  `asx_channel_wait_cancel` (`mpsc.c:757`). If it is forgotten, a woken task holds the hand-off
  and other producers stall.

title: C2 Send permits are tracked obligations (commit on send, abort on abort/drop/holder end); leaked permits detected
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** registers each SendPermit as an obligation (`/dp/asupersync/src/channel/mpsc.rs:1176-1180`).
  Drop aborts it (`:1663-1673`).
- **C** `asx_send_permit` (`include/asx/core/channel.h:59-63`) is a plain struct with no ledger
  entry and no auto-abort. A leaked permit consumes capacity forever, and nothing detects it.

## Fix
1. Reserving a permit creates an obligation of kind SendPermit held by the reserving task. Send
   commits it; abort aborts it.
2. When the holder task completes or its region closes, outstanding permits are resolved through
   the obligation machinery:
   - abort with reason CANCEL if the holder was cancelled;
   - otherwise a leak under the leak policy (K6).

   Capacity is released.
3. The same applies to oneshot permits (C8) and semaphore permits (Y4) where Rust tracks them.

## Tests
- A task reserves and returns without sending: the permit leaks (policy-dependent) and capacity
  is restored.
- Cancelled holder → aborted with CANCEL.
- Fixtures: mpsc obligation family.

title: C3 Channel close semantics: receiver close keeps queue drainable vs drop discards; sender refcount; DISCONNECTED on closed reserve
description:
## Drift
- **Receiver close vs drop.** Rust `close()` keeps queued messages readable
  (`/dp/asupersync/src/channel/mpsc.rs:1694-1712`); drop discards them (`:2122-2148`). C
  `close_receiver` always discards (`src/channel/mpsc.c:446-477`).
- **Sender lifetime.** Rust uses sender reference counting (`:1237-1254`). C uses an explicit
  `close_sender` (`mpsc.c:423-444, 545-547`).
- **Reserve on a closed channel.** Rust returns `Disconnected`; C returns `ASX_E_INVALID_STATE`.

## Fix
1. Add `asx_channel_close` (drainable) and `asx_channel_receiver_drop` (discard).
2. Add sender handle clone/drop with a reference count. The channel becomes sender-closed when the
   count reaches 0.
3. Make the reserve status match Rust via the vocabulary status map.
4. Remove `close_sender` and update callers (no shims).

## Tests
- close, then recv → drains, then disconnected.
- drop → immediate disconnected.
- Clone 3 senders, drop 2 → still open; drop the 3rd → closed.
- Fixtures: mpsc close family.

title: C4 Watch channel phantom change: versions must start at 0 and subscribe marks current version seen (u64 versions)
description:
## Bug (verified)
- **Rust** (`/dp/asupersync/src/channel/watch.rs:190-192, 408-418, 598-620`) starts at version 0
  with receivers at seen = 0. A new subscriber starts at the current version.
- **C** (`src/channel/watch.c:103, 111, 130`) starts the version at 1 with receivers at seen = 0.
  Every new receiver and subscriber reports `has_changed()` immediately for a change that never
  happened. Versions are `uint32`.

This breaks the standard config-propagation pattern the README advertises (L1013-1015): every
subscriber does a spurious first reload.

## Fix
Start at version 0, set receiver seen = current on create and subscribe, and use u64 versions.
Keep the changed/closed ordering, which matches Rust (`watch.rs:731-760` vs `watch.c:208-230`).

## Tests
- New receiver → `has_changed` false; after a send → true; after a read → false.
- Subscribe after 3 sends → false.
- Version wrap test is no longer relevant (u64).
- Fixture: watch family. (It can land before the oracle with C unit tests citing the Rust lines.)

title: C5 Broadcast semantics: Closed when no receivers, send returns receiver count, Lagged(n) count, u64 seq, multi-sender, reserve
description:
## Drift
`/dp/asupersync/src/channel/broadcast.rs:415-423, 843-860` vs `src/channel/broadcast.c:31, 164-226`:

| Aspect | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| No receivers | reserve/send returns Closed | returns OK and buffers the message |
| Send return value | live receiver count | nothing |
| Lag | `Lagged(missed)` | `ASX_E_LAGGED` with no count |
| Sequence | u64 | u32, wraps |
| Senders | multi-sender with reserve | single sender, no permit/reserve |

The C header also claims sends fail with `CHANNEL_FULL` when full (`broadcast.h:10`), but the
code overwrites.

## Fix
Align each row. Fix the header doc. Expose the lag count through an out parameter.

## Tests
- No receivers → closed.
- Receiver lag of 5 → lagged(5), cursor advanced.
- Multi-sender ordering.
- Fixtures: broadcast family.

title: C7 MPSC surface parity: send_evict_oldest, recv_many, closed(), weak sender (+ unbounded per owner decision D3)
description:
## Missing in C
`/dp/asupersync/src/channel/mpsc.rs`:
- `unbounded` (`:599`);
- `send_evict_oldest` (`:872`);
- `WeakSender` (`:941`, `:1259`);
- `recv_many` (`:1754`);
- `closed()` future (`mpsc_closed.rs:39`).

Also, C payloads are `uint64_t` only.

## Decision D3
Unbounded queues in a bounded-memory C runtime. Recommendation: provide them, but forbid them in
profiles that declare `ASX_FORBID_UNBOUNDED_QUEUE` (ROUTER, AUTOMOTIVE, BROWSER). Creation then
returns `ASX_E_PERMISSION_DENIED`, which is a documented profile capability rather than a semantic
fork. "Unbounded" in C means bounded by the arena; exhaustion follows the failure-atomic policy.
Record the decision.

## Plan
Implement the evict-oldest, recv_many, closed-wait and weak-sender equivalents, and unbounded per
D3. Payloads: keep `uint64_t` plus an optional user pointer, and document that it is not typed.

## Tests
Per API, plus fixtures.

title: [Y] Sync primitive parity: barrier reuse, notify permits, rwlock fairness, semaphore surface, poisoning
description:
## Why
Confirmed bugs:
- the barrier is not reusable, because `arrived` is never reset (`src/sync/barrier.c:137,145`);
- `notify_one` with no waiter is lost (`src/sync/notify.c:179`).

Drift:
- rwlock readers can starve forever;
- the semaphore lacks `acquire_many`/`add_permits`/`forget` and allows a double release;
- waiter caps of 16 or 32 return RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED where Rust's queues are unbounded;
- mutex has no poisoning.

## Done when
The bugs are fixed with regression tests, every sync unit is green under the oracle, and the caps
are removed via the shared intrusive waiter queue.

title: Y1 Barrier is not reusable: arrived never reset after trip (every later arrival trips alone)
description:
## Bug (verified)
In `src/sync/barrier.c`, `asx_barrier_wait_begin` increments `s->arrived` (`:137`) and trips
when `arrived >= threshold` (`:145`). On trip, `arrived` is never reset; the only decrement is in
`barrier_waiter_withdraw` (`:55`). When a released waiter completes `poll_wait`, only
`waiter_count` drops.

So after round 1, `arrived` stays at the threshold, and each subsequent single arrival trips the
barrier alone as leader. Rust's barrier is cyclic (`/dp/asupersync/src/sync/barrier.rs:325-326`:
generation/round reset).

A second problem: a waiter that is cancelled *after* release goes through the checkpoint path and
calls `barrier_waiter_withdraw`, which decrements `arrived` for an already-tripped round.

## Fix
1. Add a round (generation) counter.
2. On trip, set `arrived = 0` and increment the round. Stamp each waiter with its round.
3. Withdraw only decrements `arrived` if the waiter's round is the current, untripped round.
4. A released-then-cancelled waiter returns OK with `is_leader = 0`. Check Rust's exact behaviour
   (`barrier.rs`) and match it.
5. Leader election: the last arrival is leader, per round.

## Tests
- 3 rounds × 4 parties: each round trips exactly once, with exactly one leader per round.
- Cancel before trip: the round still needs N arrivals.
- Cancel after release: returns OK, round counts are unaffected.
- CBMC harness for the round counter (with W1.13).
- Fixture: sync/barrier family.

title: Y2 Notify loses notify_one when no waiter is present (lost wakeup): add stored permit like Rust
description:
## Bug (verified)
`src/sync/notify.c:172-181`: `asx_notify_one` delivers to the oldest waiter if there is one,
otherwise does nothing, with the comment `/* no waiters, that's fine */`. Rust
(`/dp/asupersync/src/sync/notify.rs:446`) **stores** a notification permit when nobody is
waiting, and the next `notified()` consumes it immediately.

C therefore has a classic lost-wakeup race: notify-before-wait is dropped, and the waiter parks
forever.

## Fix
1. Add a `stored` permit counter: `notify_one` with no waiter (or with a hand-off nobody takes)
   increments it.
2. `poll_wait` consumes a stored permit before parking.
3. Match Rust exactly: is it a single stored permit (boolean) or a count? Verify in `notify.rs`.
   tokio's Notify stores at most one permit; asupersync may differ.
4. `notify_all` semantics per Rust (does it store anything?).
5. Have `notify_one` report whether a waiter was woken, if Rust exposes that.

## Tests
- notify then wait → returns immediately.
- notify ×2 then wait ×2 → Rust-defined result.
- `notify_all` with no waiters.
- Fixture: sync/notify family.

comments.text: d145f42 tightens 'reject double release' to permit identity where C can see it. A mutex guard carries the serial of its hold and the mutex records the holder's serial, so a stale guard copy can no longer unlock (or poison) a later holder's lock (before: accepted whenever the later hold kept outstanding at 1, breaking mutual exclusion). title: [T] Time parity: same-tick ordering, timeout boundary, interval modes, limits
description:
## Why
- **Same-tick order.** Rust's 4×256 wheel (1 ms tick) fires timers in the same tick in insertion
  order; C sorts by exact deadline.
- **Timeout boundary.** At `now == deadline`, Rust polls the inner future first; C returns
  TIMED_OUT immediately.
- **Interval.** Rust's first tick fires immediately, with Burst/Delay/Skip modes (default Burst);
  C waits a full period and supports only Delay.
- **Limits.** C caps at 24 h and 128 timers; Rust is unbounded with a 7-day clamp.

## Done when
Time units are green under the oracle with LB ≥ 99.9%.

title: T1 Timers in the same 1ms wheel tick fire in insertion order (Rust 4x256 wheel) - C sorts by exact deadline
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** (`/dp/asupersync/src/time/wheel.rs:43-55, 710-740`): a 4-level × 256-slot hierarchical
  wheel with a 1 ms tick. Timers landing in the same tick fire in insertion order.
- **C**: the scheduler's timer heap is keyed by (exact deadline, insertion seq)
  (`src/runtime/scheduler.c:94-99`).

Example: register A at 5.7 ms, then B at 5.2 ms. Rust fires A then B; C fires B then A.
Separately, `src/time/timer_wheel.c` is a flat 128-slot table that the scheduler doesn't use.

## Fix
1. Quantize timer deadlines to Rust's tick for *ordering* purposes, using Rust's exact rounding
   (up or down, extracted from source).
2. Order by (tick, insertion seq).
3. Keep exact deadlines for wake-time accounting, per Rust.
4. Decide the fate of `timer_wheel.c` in T4.

## Tests
- The A/B example.
- 1000 random timers: firing order equals Rust's (fixture via twin_run).
- Metamorphic M8 (time scaling) must account for tick quantization; document it.

title: T4 Timer limits (7-day clamp, no fixed timer count) and one authoritative timer structure (timer_wheel.c vs scheduler heap)
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** (`/dp/asupersync/src/time/wheel.rs:98-103`): no timer count limit; durations clamp at
  7 days.
- **C** (`src/time/timer_wheel.c:125-147`): at most 128 timers, and durations over 24 h are
  rejected with `ASX_E_TIMER_DURATION_EXCEEDED`.
- C also has two timer structures:
  - `timer_wheel.c` (a flat table, README "Timer Wheel" section);
  - the scheduler's deadline heap, which is what the scheduler uses.

## Plan
1. Clamp at 7 days, as Rust does (verify).
2. The timer count is bounded by a configurable arena (`ASX_MAX_TIMERS` with an `#ifndef` guard,
   RB4). Exhaustion is failure-atomic per R1.
3. Make one structure authoritative. If `timer_wheel.c` is redundant, **ask the owner before
   deleting it** (RULE 1). Otherwise make the scheduler use it.
4. Update README L800-806.

## Tests
- Durations of 6 days, 7 days and 8 days (clamped).
- Arena exhaustion.

title: T5 asx_timer_update must reject stale (generation-mismatched) handles
description:
## Drift
Generation-safe handles are a core C guarantee (README "Generation-Safe Handles"), but
`asx_timer_update` does not refuse a stale handle (audit finding).

Generation-check in update, returning `ASX_E_STALE_HANDLE`.

Cancel, re-arm the slot, then update with the old handle → `STALE_HANDLE`, and the new timer is
unaffected.

title: Time + actor/supervision e2e: same-tick ordering, timeout boundary, interval modes, restart window/backoff, GenServer call/cast under load - JSONL logs
description:
## Plan
`tests/e2e/time_actor_parity.sh`, running in the deterministic lab and comparing against
Rust-captured fixtures via the interpreter:
1. **Timers.** 10k random timers with heavy same-tick collisions; firing order matches the fixture
   (T1). Timeout exactly at the deadline (T2). Interval Burst/Delay/Skip under a 5-period stall
   (T3). 7-day clamp (T4).
2. **Supervision.** Crash children 4 times within 60 s of virtual time → escalation; spread over
   2 minutes → restarts continue. The backoff sequence matches 100/200/400… ms capped at 10 s
   (A4). Transient cancelled → no restart.
3. **GenServer.** 1000 interleaved call/cast ops; a dropped reply triggers the leak policy; the
   overflow policies behave; system messages are prioritized (A3).
4. **Actors.** Reply-then-exit delivers the reply (A1). Stop on a full mailbox succeeds (A2). A
   65th send parks and wakes FIFO (A5).
5. JSONL per scenario, with rolling digests (RB1).

Green at milestone M-δ. Each case cites the bead it verifies.

title: [A] Actor/GenServer/supervision parity (Erlang/OTP layer) incl. reply-loss bug
description:
## Why
- **Bug:** a reply is lost if the actor exits right after replying (`src/actor/actor.c:404`
  checks `alive` before `replied`).
- **Stop** is queued as an ordinary message and can fail when the mailbox is full.
- **GenServer** runs its handler synchronously in the caller. There is no reply obligation, no
  system messages and no cast-overflow policy.
- **Supervision** counts restarts over its whole lifetime, with no 3-per-60 s window and no
  100 ms to 10 s backoff, and it restarts Transient children that exited Cancelled.
- **Mailbox** is 16 instead of 64, and send does not wait for space.
- **Monitors and links** are missing; the C `monitor/` and `link/` modules are unrelated.

## Done when
These units are green under the oracle, and the reply-loss bug has a regression test.
