title: A1 Actor call reply lost when actor exits right after replying (actor.c:404 checks alive before replied)
description:
## Bug (verified by audit)
`src/actor/actor.c:404`: polling a call token checks whether the actor is `alive` *before*
checking whether the reply was set (`replied`). If the actor replies and then exits in the same
poll or round, the caller sees "actor gone" and loses a reply that was actually delivered. Rust
delivers a reply sent before exit (`/dp/asupersync/src/actor.rs:1056-1089`).

## Fix
Check `replied` first. Only if there is no reply and the actor is gone, return the
dropped/disconnected status.

## Tests
- An actor handler replies, then stops itself → the caller receives the reply.
- An actor stops without replying → disconnected.
- Fixture: actor family.

title: A2 Actor stop seals the mailbox (flag) instead of queueing a STOP message that can fail on a full mailbox
description:

- **Rust** `actor.rs:328-331`: `stop()` seals the mailbox. Later sends fail, and queued messages

  full, and later sends are still accepted.

title: A3 GenServer parity: runs on its own actor task, call returns token with reply obligation, system messages, cast overflow policy, name registry
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** `gen_server.rs` (314 KB): a GenServer runs as its own task. `Reply` is an obligation,
  and dropping it unreplied is a leak. There are system messages and a cast-overflow policy
  (`gen_server.rs:617-745, 1045-1057`).
- **C** `src/actor/gen_server.c:104-108, 125-129` runs the handler **synchronously in the
  caller**. It has no reply obligation, no system messages and no overflow policy.

## Plan
1. Re-implement GenServer on the actor task model (A2/A5).
2. `call` enqueues a request and returns a token backed by a reply obligation (via the K6
   machinery).
3. A system-message queue, polled first.
4. Cast overflow: REJECT by default, DROP_OLDEST optional, per Rust's enum.
5. A name registry (bounded).
6. Update `examples/ex_gen_server.c`.

## Tests
- Call/cast ordering.
- Handler drops the reply → leak policy.
- System message priority.
- Overflow policies.
- Fixtures.

title: A4 Supervision parity: sliding restart window (3/60s), exponential backoff 100ms->10s x2, escalation, Transient-cancelled = normal, reverse-order stop
description:
## Drift
Rust `supervision.rs:262-273` (intensity 3 per 60 s), `:364-374` (backoff 100 ms to 10 s,
factor 2), `:382-402` (strategies), `:1823-1843` (Transient). C `src/actor/supervisor.c:120-134,
261, 124-128`:

| Aspect | Rust | C |
|---|---|---|
| Restart limit | sliding window, 3 per 60 s | lifetime count, no window |
| Backoff | exponential, 100 ms to 10 s, ×2 | none |
| Transient child that exited Cancelled | normal exit, not restarted | restarted |
| Escalation | Stop / Escalate / ResetCounter | — |
| Stopping children | reverse start order on every path | — |

Strategies (one_for_one, one_for_all, rest_for_one) match.

## Fix
1. Implement each row, with defaults extracted by W1.12.
2. Use virtual time for the window and backoff (`asx_task_wait_until`).
3. Fix the UBSan finding in the same file (RB6: `memcpy` with NULL, 0 at `:367`).

## Tests
- 4 failures in 60 s → escalate.
- 4 failures over 2 minutes → restarts continue.
- Backoff sequence 100/200/400/... capped at 10 s.
- Transient cancelled → not restarted.
- Reverse stop order.
- Fixtures.

title: A5 Actor mailbox capacity 64 and send waits for space (Rust) vs C 16 + WOULD_BLOCK
description:
## Drift
- **Rust** `actor.rs:275-286, 876`: the default mailbox is 64, and `send` waits for space
  (cancel-safe).
- **C** `include/asx/actor/actor.h:39`, `src/actor/actor.c:97`: the mailbox is 16, and send
  returns `WOULD_BLOCK`.

## Fix
- Make the capacity configurable with a default of 64.
- Make send a wait (park on a C6 link; cancel-safe via C1 semantics), with `try_send` returning
  WOULD_BLOCK.

Fill to 64, the 65th send parks, a receive wakes it in FIFO order.

title: Supervision: Rust surfaces not yet ported (registries, shared restart domains, restart storms, per-child shutdown budgets, cleanup outcomes)
description:
## What
03a0497 ported Rust's managed supervisor (asupersync 5e60b1c4c, src/supervision.rs:1795-3506) to
src/actor/supervisor.c. These Rust surfaces of the same module are still missing in C, as stated
in include/asx/actor/supervisor.h ("Not in the C model"):

- **Name registration.** `bind_managed_with_registry` (supervision.rs:2117) registers each
  generation in a name registry. Its `Registration` error never occurs in C.
- **Dynamic supervisors with a shared restart domain.** The `SharedRestartLimit` error never
  occurs in C.
- **Restart storm detection.** `RestartStormMonitor` and `StormMonitorConfig` (:5582, :5769).
- **Per-child shutdown budgets.** A drained generation in C has its cancel kind's cleanup budget,
  which is Rust's default `Budget::INFINITE` ceiling. Rust's `ChildSpec` shutdown budget is not
  ported.
- **Region cleanup outcomes.** C regions have no finalizers whose cleanup can fail, so the
  `Cleanup` and `SupervisorCleanup` errors never occur.
- **The legacy `Supervisor` / `ChildStart` path** (non-managed). It may not be worth porting;
  decide first.

## Why
These are the remaining supervision gaps the README and FEATURE_PARITY now list as not ported.
Each one that is ported must come with a DSL v2 step or field and twin_run fixtures, as the managed
controller did (DSL §3.8; vocabulary §2/§6).

## Done when
Each item is either ported, with fixtures that pass `make conformance`, or recorded as excluded
with a reason in FEATURE_PARITY and the header. The README "Not ported" lists are updated to match.

comments.text: 2026-10-11 finding (restart storm detection): in Rust it is observability only. title: Supervision DSL/C model: a body cannot return a Cancelled outcome; supervised child programs cannot use naming steps (per-generation name scoping)
description:
## What
The managed supervision port (03a0497) has two expressiveness gaps in its C API and in DSL v2.
Both are gaps of the model, not divergences between the engines: both oracles agree on everything
DSL v2 can express.

1. **A body cannot return a Cancelled outcome.**
   - Rust's factory future returns `Outcome<(), E>`, which can be `Outcome::Cancelled(reason)`.
     `ManagedRestartMode::eligible` treats that as not eligible for a Transient child.
   - The C start function's body maps `ASX_OK` to ok and any other status to `Err(status)`, so a
     body returning `ASX_E_CANCELLED` is an error, and a Transient child is restarted.
   - DSL v2 `return` has only the tags ok, err and panicked, and twin_run maps a program's err to
     `Outcome::Err`, so the engines agree today.
   - Fix: decide how a C body reports a Cancelled outcome. For example, `ASX_E_CANCELLED` could
     mean `Outcome::Cancelled` with the task's cancel reason, or there could be an explicit
     out-parameter. Add `return {"tag": "cancelled"}` to the DSL, map it in both interpreters,
     and capture a fixture that shows the Transient non-restart.
2. **A supervised child's program may not use naming steps.**
   - The banned steps are `spawn`, `open_region`, `server_spawn` and `supervise` (DSL §3.8). Every
     generation reruns the same program, so their `as` names would repeat across generations.
     Both interpreters reject such scenarios.
   - Fix: scope the names a generation creates under the generation's name, for example
     `<supervisor>/<child>#<n>/<as>`. This needs a vocabulary §2 rule, naming in both
     harnesses, and generator support for nested supervision trees.

## Done when
Both are expressible, each is covered by twin_run fixtures that pass, and the generator emits them.

title: [L] Lab/trace parity: Foata canonical trace class, oracle catalog, schedule record/replay, bounded DPOR
description:
## Why
The C trace fingerprint is an order-sensitive FNV over the raw event stream, while Rust's is a
Foata-normal-form fingerprint that ignores how independent events interleave
(`trace/canonicalize.rs`, independence relation in `trace/independence.rs:303`). C also has 3
oracles where Rust has 24, no forced-schedule replay and no DPOR. Without these, the oracle can't
compare by trace class, and C can't prove that outcomes are independent of the schedule.

## Done when
C Foata fingerprints equal Rust's for the same projected traces, the oracle catalog mapping is
complete, forced-schedule replay works both ways, and bounded-DPOR reachable-outcome sets match
Rust's for small scenarios.

title: L1 Foata canonical trace class in C: port Rust independence relation + canonicalizer; fingerprints must equal Rust's
description:
## Why
- **C** (`src/runtime/trace.c:162-179`): an FNV hash over the raw ordered event stream, so it is
  interleaving-sensitive.
- **Rust**: `trace/canonicalize.rs` (Foata normal form of the Mazurkiewicz trace, fingerprint
  around `:381-386`) over `trace/independence.rs:303` `independent(a,b)`.

Mode (b) of the oracle compares trace classes: legal interleavings of independent events must not
count as drift. The C side needs the same canonicalizer.

## Plan
1. Implement `asx_trace_canonicalize` over vocabulary-v2 events, using the W1.2 independence
   predicate (ported exactly from Rust, with citations):
   - O(n²) Foata layering;
   - deterministic within-layer sort key, identical to Rust's comparison key;
   - fingerprint hashed exactly as Rust does, or over the canonical JSON if the oracle defines
     the fingerprint that way. Decide in W1.2 and make the two sides agree.
2. Use bounded static storage. The trace length cap must be configurable, and RB1 makes the
   streaming digest independent of storage.
3. Differential test via twin_run: random vocabulary traces are canonicalized on both sides and
   the fingerprints must be equal. The canonicalizer itself is fuzzed.

## Success criteria
- 100k random traces: fingerprints equal.
- Swapping two independent events doesn't change the C fingerprint; swapping two dependent ones
  does.

title: L3 Schedule recording and forced-schedule replay in C (counterpart of Rust run_forced_schedule), both directions
description:
## Why
Exact-parity mode (c) can work two ways:
1. C replicates Rust's picker (S1); or
2. one engine replays the other's recorded schedule.

Rust has `start_forced_schedule_recording`, `finish_forced_schedule_recording` and
`run_forced_schedule` (`/dp/asupersync/src/lab/runtime.rs:2618-2784`), with a canonical byte format
(`to_canonical_bytes` around `:364`). C needs the counterpart. It is also invaluable for debugging:
replay Rust's schedule in C and find the first divergent step.

## Plan
1. C dispatch log → canonical bytes in the same format as Rust's `ForcedScheduleArtifact`
   (verify the format in the source).
2. `asx_lab_run_forced_schedule(artifact)` forces dispatch choices. It errors if a forced task
   isn't runnable, with the step index.
3. twin_run supports C→Rust and Rust→C forced replay in compare mode (c).

## Success criteria
- A Rust-recorded schedule replayed in C gives identical vocabulary events on scheduler fixtures,
  and the reverse also holds.
- A mismatch reports the first divergent step.

title: L4 Bounded DPOR in C + cross-engine reachable-outcome-set equality for small scenarios
description:
## Why
A single schedule per seed misses drift that only some interleavings expose. Rust has DPOR-style
exploration (`src/trace/dpor.rs`, `src/lab/explorer.rs`) over the same independence relation.
Comparing the **sets of reachable outcomes** under all schedules is the strongest
schedule-independent parity check available.

## Plan
1. C bounded explorer: for scenarios with ≤ 4 tasks and ≤ 12 steps, enumerate one schedule per
   Mazurkiewicz class via persistent/sleep sets over the W1.2 independence relation, using forced
   schedules (L3). Collect the set of end snapshots and outcomes.
2. In twin_run, compute the same set using Rust's explorer, or Rust forced schedules over the
   C-enumerated class representatives.
3. Assert the sets are equal. Report C-only reachable outcomes (for example a leak or a
   Panicked) and Rust-only ones.
4. Run as a nightly lane over a curated set of small scenarios.

## Success criteria
Set equality on ≥ 200 small scenarios. A planted mutant reachable only under a specific
interleaving (e.g. a missing wake under race) is detected.

title: Child regions: Comprehensive unit tests
description:
Add thorough unit tests for the parent-child region lifecycle.

## Test cases (in tests/unit/runtime/test_quiescence.c):
1. open_child_in_open_parent: open parent, open child, verify child_count=1
2. open_multiple_children: open 3 children, verify child_count=3
3. open_child_in_closed_parent_rejected: close parent, attempt open_child → ASX_E_REGION_NOT_OPEN
4. open_child_in_poisoned_parent_rejected: poison parent → ASX_E_REGION_POISONED
5. child_close_decrements_parent: close child, verify parent.child_count decremented
6. all_children_closed_q2_passes: close all children, run quiescence check, verify q2_children_closed=1
7. open_children_q2_fails: leave one child open, verify q2_children_closed=0
8. parent_drain_blocked_by_children: close parent with open child, verify stays in CLOSING
9. parent_drain_proceeds_after_children_close: close child, then parent drain succeeds
10. max_children_exhaustion: open ASX_MAX_REGION_CHILDREN children, next → ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
11. nested_grandchild: parent → child → grandchild, verify 3-level close order
12. child_of_root_vs_child_of_child: verify parent_id tracking at each level

## Logging
Each test logs: parent_id, child_count before/after, region states. Use fprintf(stderr, ...) with descriptive prefixes.

## Files
- tests/unit/runtime/test_quiescence.c (extend)
close_reason: Added comprehensive child-region lifecycle unit coverage

title: EPIC: Embedded Target Matrix Gate (GATE-EMBEDDED)
description:
## Goal
Implement GATE-EMBEDDED: cross-compilation for ARM and RISC-V targets with QEMU-based smoke
tests, validating that the C port builds and runs correctly on constrained embedded platforms.

## Why This Matters
The C port's raison d'être is portability to embedded targets that Rust's async runtime cannot
reach (bare-metal MCUs, router-class devices, automotive ECUs). Without actually building and
testing on these targets, the "portable ANSI C" claim is aspirational rather than proven.

GATE-EMBEDDED is one of the 9 non-negotiable quality gates from AGENTS.md:
"Embedded target matrix gate (cross-build + QEMU + device smoke)."

The three resource classes (R1=tight, R2=balanced, R3=roomy) defined in asx_config.h are
specifically designed for embedded deployment. The FREESTANDING and EMBEDDED_ROUTER profiles
compile with no libc dependency. This gate proves those profiles work end-to-end.

## What "Done" Looks Like
- Cross-compilation succeeds for: arm-none-eabi (Cortex-M), aarch64-linux-gnu, riscv32-unknown-elf
- QEMU user-mode runs the C test suite for aarch64 and riscv32 targets
- Bare-metal builds (arm-none-eabi) link successfully with FREESTANDING profile
- Resource class R1 builds fit within 64KB RAM budget
- make embedded-matrix passes in CI

## Architectural Context
The Makefile already has profile-parity targets that build with ASX_PROFILE_FREESTANDING and
ASX_PROFILE_EMBEDDED_ROUTER. The freestanding hooks (src/platform/freestanding/hooks.c) provide
stub implementations for platforms without libc. What's missing is the actual cross-compiler
toolchains, QEMU setup, and the CI integration to exercise them.

## Risk
- Cross-compiler toolchain installation varies by host OS
- QEMU user-mode may not perfectly emulate all target quirks
- Bare-metal linking requires a linker script and startup code
- R1 memory budget (64KB) may require tuning ASX_MAX_* constants
notes:
## CRITICAL: EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE AUDIT (2026-03-12)

The following ALREADY EXISTS and must NOT be recreated or modified:
- tools/ci/run_embedded_matrix.sh: Linux-musl cross-build matrix (armv7, aarch64, mipsel)
- tools/ci/run_qemu_smoke.sh: QEMU testing for Linux-musl targets
- make ci-embedded-matrix: Makefile target for Linux-musl embedded builds
- tools/ci/generate_layout_budget_report.sh: Binary size/layout reporting
- tools/ci/compute_layout_budget_delta.sh: Cross-run regression detection

## What This Epic ACTUALLY Adds (COMPLEMENTARY, NOT REPLACEMENT)
Bare-metal cross-compilation for FREESTANDING/EMBEDDED_ROUTER profiles on:
- ARM Cortex-M (arm-none-eabi-gcc) — new toolchain
- RISC-V (riscv-elf-gcc) — new toolchain
- QEMU semihosting for bare-metal binaries — new execution mode
- R1 memory budgets for .text/.bss sections — new measurements

## Subtask Inventory (8 total)
.1 Install bare-metal ARM toolchain (60m) — Linux-musl ARM already exists
.2 Install RISC-V toolchain (60m) — genuinely new
.3 QEMU semihosting setup (90m) — Linux user-mode QEMU already exists
.4 Bare-metal Makefile targets (120m) — Linux-musl targets already exist
.5 Bare-metal link validation (120m) — genuinely new
.6 R1 memory budgets (90m) — layout reporting exists for musl
.7 CI gate for bare-metal (120m) — embedded CI exists for musl
.8 QEMU e2e tests for bare-metal (180m) — QEMU smoke exists for musl

title: Install ARM cross-compiler toolchain (arm-none-eabi-gcc)
description:
## STATUS: LINUX-MUSL TOOLCHAINS EXIST — BARE-METAL TOOLCHAIN IS NEW

## Context
The project already has cross-compilation for Linux-musl ARM targets:
- armv7-openwrt-linux-muslgnueabi-gcc (OpenWrt SDK)
- aarch64-openwrt-linux-musl-gcc (OpenWrt SDK)
These are LINUX embedded targets (musl libc, runs under Linux kernel).

This bead is about BARE-METAL ARM targets (arm-none-eabi-gcc) which are a
DIFFERENT, COMPLEMENTARY class of embedded deployment:
- No OS, no libc (or only newlib-nano)
- Targets Cortex-M0/M3/M4/M7 (microcontrollers, not application processors)
- Validates the FREESTANDING profile (no POSIX, no malloc, no printf)

## Why Both Are Needed
- Linux-musl embedded (existing): Proves the library works on resource-constrained
  Linux systems like routers (OpenWrt). Uses EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile.
- Bare-metal (this bead): Proves the library works on microcontrollers with NO OS.
  Uses FREESTANDING profile. This is a stronger portability claim.

## Task
1. Install arm-none-eabi-gcc (GNU ARM Embedded Toolchain)
2. Verify targets: cortex-m0, cortex-m3, cortex-m4, cortex-m7
3. Verify newlib-nano is available
4. Create smoke test compiling a trivial .c file
5. Document in tools/ci/TOOLCHAINS.md (alongside existing musl entries)

## Acceptance Criteria
- arm-none-eabi-gcc --version succeeds
- Can compile targeting -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb
- newlib-nano headers findable
- Clearly documented as complementary to existing musl toolchains

title: Install RISC-V cross-compiler toolchain (riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc)
description:
## Context
The GATE-EMBEDDED quality gate also requires RISC-V target validation. RISC-V is
increasingly important for embedded systems and the asupersync library should be
verified on this architecture.

## Background
RISC-V (specifically RV32IMAC and RV64IMAC) is a primary embedded target alongside
ARM. The C port's portability claims must be validated on both architectures to be
credible. Key concerns:
- Endianness handling (RISC-V is little-endian, same as ARM, but the codec must
  handle big-endian fields correctly regardless)
- Alignment requirements differ from ARM
- Atomic operation availability varies by extension set (A extension)

## Task
1. Install riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc (or riscv-none-elf-gcc from SiFive/xPack)
2. Verify targets: rv32imac, rv64imac
3. Verify that picolibc or newlib headers are available
4. Create a small smoke test compiling a trivial .c file
5. Document in tools/ci/TOOLCHAINS.md alongside ARM entry

## Acceptance Criteria
- `riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc --version` succeeds
- Can compile targeting -march=rv32imac -mabi=ilp32
- Can compile targeting -march=rv64imac -mabi=lp64

## Why This Matters
Validates portability claims on a non-ARM embedded architecture. Together with ARM,
provides confidence that the FREESTANDING profile is genuinely cross-platform.

title: Set up QEMU semihosting for bare-metal ARM and RISC-V targets
description:
## STATUS: QEMU HARNESS EXISTS — SEMIHOSTING MODE IS NEW

## Context
A comprehensive QEMU smoke harness ALREADY EXISTS:
- tools/ci/run_qemu_smoke.sh (395 lines)
- Supports mipsel, armv7, aarch64 targets
- JSONL logging, timeout handling, artifact collection
- --build-first, --dry-run, --strict modes

HOWEVER, this harness is for LINUX user-mode emulation (qemu-arm-static running
Linux ELF binaries linked against musl). For bare-metal binaries (from arm-none-eabi),
we need QEMU SEMIHOSTING mode, which is a different execution model.

## Difference: Linux User-Mode vs Semihosting
- Linux user-mode: qemu-arm-static runs Linux ELF, translates syscalls
- Semihosting: qemu-arm -semihosting runs bare-metal ELF, I/O via SVC instructions

## Task
1. Install qemu-system-arm and qemu-system-riscv32 (or verify user-mode works)
2. Create tools/ci/run_qemu_baremetal.sh that:
   a. Extends the EXISTING run_qemu_smoke.sh pattern (same JSONL format, same flags)
   b. Adds semihosting support for bare-metal binaries
   c. Supports arm-m4, arm-m0, riscv32, riscv64 targets
3. Create minimal semihosting startup code (tests/embedded/startup_semihosting.s)
4. Verify trivial bare-metal binaries run under QEMU semihosting

## Acceptance Criteria
- Trivial ARM bare-metal binary runs under qemu-system-arm -semihosting
- Trivial RISC-V bare-metal binary runs under qemu-system-riscv32
- run_qemu_baremetal.sh follows same conventions as run_qemu_smoke.sh
- Both scripts can coexist (Linux-musl + bare-metal)

title: Add Makefile cross-compilation targets for ARM and RISC-V
description:
## STATUS: LINUX-MUSL TARGETS EXIST — BARE-METAL TARGETS ARE NEW

## Context
The Makefile ALREADY HAS embedded cross-compilation:
- make build TARGET=armv7-openwrt-linux-muslgnueabi PROFILE=EMBEDDED_ROUTER
- make build TARGET=aarch64-openwrt-linux-musl PROFILE=EMBEDDED_ROUTER
- make ci-embedded-matrix runs all Linux-musl targets

These use OpenWrt musl toolchains targeting LINUX embedded systems.

This bead adds BARE-METAL Makefile targets using arm-none-eabi/riscv-elf toolchains
targeting microcontrollers with NO OS, using the FREESTANDING profile.

## Task
1. **Create linker scripts** for each target architecture:
   - tools/embedded/cortex-m4.ld: Flash 256KB + SRAM 64KB memory map
   - tools/embedded/cortex-m0.ld: Flash 128KB + SRAM 16KB memory map
   - tools/embedded/riscv32.ld: Generic SRAM-only layout for QEMU
   - tools/embedded/riscv64.ld: Generic SRAM-only layout for QEMU
   - Each defines .text, .rodata, .data, .bss, .stack sections
   - Stack size configurable via symbol (default 4KB)

2. Add BARE-METAL Makefile targets (complementary to existing musl targets):
   - cross-baremetal-arm-m4-free: Cortex-M4, FREESTANDING
   - cross-baremetal-arm-m0-free: Cortex-M0, FREESTANDING
   - cross-baremetal-riscv32-free: RV32IMAC, FREESTANDING
   - cross-baremetal-riscv64-free: RV64IMAC, FREESTANDING
   - cross-baremetal-arm-m4-router: Cortex-M4, EMBEDDED_ROUTER
   - cross-baremetal-arm-m0-router: Cortex-M0, EMBEDDED_ROUTER
   - cross-baremetal-riscv32-router: RV32IMAC, EMBEDDED_ROUTER
   - cross-baremetal-riscv64-router: RV64IMAC, EMBEDDED_ROUTER
   - cross-baremetal-all: all 8 targets
   Each target: separate build dir, static .a, size report

3. DO NOT modify existing musl targets — these are additive

## Linker Script Details
Bare-metal ARM/RISC-V linking requires explicit memory layout. Without linker scripts,
the linker uses a default layout that places everything at address 0, which won't work
on real hardware and may confuse QEMU semihosting. The .ld files define:
- MEMORY regions (FLASH, SRAM with origin and length)
- SECTIONS layout (.text → FLASH, .data/.bss → SRAM)
- _stack_top symbol for startup code
- ENTRY(_Reset) referencing the startup code from bd-aw69.3

## What Already Works (DO NOT TOUCH)
- make build TARGET=... for Linux-musl cross-compilation
- make ci-embedded-matrix for Linux-musl matrix
- tools/ci/run_embedded_matrix.sh

## Acceptance Criteria
- make cross-baremetal-all builds all 8 targets (static .a files)
- Linker scripts exist for all 4 architectures
- Each .a contains only thumb/riscv code (verified via file/readelf)
- Existing musl targets unaffected
- EMBEDDED_ROUTER .a files larger than FREESTANDING (includes channels)

## Testing
- Run: make cross-baremetal-arm-m4-free && readelf -h build/cross/arm-m4-free/lib/libasx.a
- Run: make cross-baremetal-all (all 8 must succeed)
- Verify: nm on each .a shows only expected symbols
- Verify: existing make ci-embedded-matrix still passes unchanged

title: Validate bare-metal linkage: no unresolved symbols in FREESTANDING and EMBEDDED_ROUTER profiles
description:
## Context
Cross-compilation may succeed at the object-file level but fail at link time if
the FREESTANDING or EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile accidentally references libc functions,
POSIX APIs, or other host-only symbols.

## Background
Both embedded profiles are designed to have zero runtime dependencies beyond what
the user provides via asx_runtime_hooks:
- No malloc/free (user provides allocator hooks)
- No printf/fprintf (user provides log_sink hook)
- No time() / clock_gettime() (user provides wall_clock / logical_clock hooks)
- No pthread_* (single-threaded or user-managed concurrency)
- No errno, no signal(), no setjmp/longjmp

EMBEDDED_ROUTER adds channels and adaptive scheduling on top of FREESTANDING. These
additional modules may introduce new symbol dependencies that FREESTANDING doesn't
have. Both must be validated independently.

Subtle dependencies that can creep in:
- memcpy/memset/memmove may be implicitly generated by the compiler
- Division helpers (__aeabi_uidiv on ARM) may be needed
- Static initializers may reference __libc_init
- Channel ring buffer operations may pull in modular arithmetic helpers

## Task
1. Create tools/ci/validate_baremetal_linkage.sh that for each of the 8 .a files
   (4 targets x 2 profiles):
   a. Extracts undefined symbols: nm --undefined-only libasx.a
   b. Categorizes each: compiler intrinsic / libc / POSIX / code bug
   c. Attempts link with: startup.o + libasx.a + libgcc.a + --no-undefined
   d. Reports per-binary results with JSONL logging
2. If unresolved symbols are found:
   a. For compiler intrinsics (memcpy, __aeabi_*): provide libgcc or compiler-rt
   b. For libc functions: fix the profile to remove the dependency
   c. Document required runtime support in docs/EMBEDDED.md
3. Generate symbol table diff between FREESTANDING and EMBEDDED_ROUTER

## JSONL Output Format
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","step":"extract_undefined","symbols":["memcpy","memset"],"count":2}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","step":"categorize","compiler_intrinsic":2,"libc":0,"posix":0,"unknown":0}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","step":"link_test","status":"pass","binary_size":34816}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"EMBEDDED_ROUTER","step":"link_test","status":"pass","binary_size":48128}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","step":"profile_diff","freestanding_only":[],"router_only":["asx_channel_create","asx_adaptive_set"],"count_diff":12}

## Testing
1. Create tests/ci/test_validate_baremetal_linkage.sh:
   a. Build a minimal .a with a known undefined symbol (e.g., calls printf)
   b. Run validate_baremetal_linkage.sh against it
   c. Verify: script correctly identifies printf as "libc" category
   d. Verify: link step fails with clear error
   e. Verify: JSONL reports the failure

2. Positive test: build libasx.a for FREESTANDING profile, run linkage validation
   a. Verify: all symbols resolve with only startup.o + libgcc.a
   b. Verify: JSONL shows "pass" for link_test step

3. Profile boundary test: verify EMBEDDED_ROUTER adds ONLY channel/adaptive symbols
   a. Compute nm diff between FREESTANDING and EMBEDDED_ROUTER .a files
   b. Verify: all additional symbols match expected channel/adaptive API surface
   c. Verify: no unexpected libc symbols appear in EMBEDDED_ROUTER

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 4 FREESTANDING binaries link with only: startup.o + libasx.a + libgcc.a
- All 4 EMBEDDED_ROUTER binaries link with only: startup.o + libasx.a + libgcc.a
- Zero unresolved symbols from libc/POSIX in any binary
- JSONL output per target/profile with categorized symbol report
- Symbol diff between profiles documented and reviewed
- Any required compiler intrinsics documented in docs/EMBEDDED.md
- Companion test validates the script's categorization logic

title: Validate R1 memory budget: static RAM/ROM footprint for Cortex-M4
description:
## STATUS: LAYOUT BUDGET REPORTING EXISTS — BARE-METAL R1 BUDGETS ARE NEW

## Context
The project ALREADY HAS layout/budget reporting for Linux-musl targets:
- tools/ci/generate_layout_budget_report.sh — generates per-target budget reports
- tools/ci/compute_layout_budget_delta.sh — computes deltas between runs
- run_embedded_matrix.sh invokes both automatically

This bead adds BARE-METAL memory budget validation, which is different:
- Linux-musl: measures shared library size and startup metrics
- Bare-metal: measures .text/.rodata/.data/.bss sections directly from linker map
- Bare-metal budgets are MUCH tighter (KB, not MB)

## Task
1. Create tools/ci/measure_baremetal_footprint.sh that:
   a. Accepts --profile, --target, --map-file, --run-id flags
   b. Parses .map file for .text/.rodata/.data/.bss sizes using awk/grep
   c. Computes total ROM (.text + .rodata) and total RAM (.data + .bss)
   d. Compares against R1 budget thresholds
   e. Reports in JSONL compatible with existing layout delta tooling
2. Set R1 budgets for both profiles on Cortex-M4:
   - FREESTANDING: ROM < 64KB, RAM < 8KB
   - EMBEDDED_ROUTER: ROM < 96KB, RAM < 16KB
3. Integrate with existing compute_layout_budget_delta.sh for regression detection
4. Document budget rationale in docs/EMBEDDED.md with per-section breakdown

## JSONL Output Format
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","section":".text","size_bytes":28672,"budget_bytes":65536,"status":"pass"}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","section":".rodata","size_bytes":4096,"budget_bytes":65536,"status":"pass"}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","section":".data","size_bytes":512,"budget_bytes":8192,"status":"pass"}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","section":".bss","size_bytes":2048,"budget_bytes":8192,"status":"pass"}
{"ts":"...","target":"arm-m4","profile":"FREESTANDING","rom_total":32768,"rom_budget":65536,"ram_total":2560,"ram_budget":8192,"status":"pass"}

## Testing
1. Create tests/ci/test_measure_baremetal_footprint.sh:
   a. Generate a synthetic .map file with known section sizes
   b. Run measure_baremetal_footprint.sh against it
   c. Verify: reported sizes match expected values exactly
   d. Verify: budget pass/fail is correct for known sizes
   e. Test over-budget scenario: create .map with .text > 64KB, verify "fail" status
   f. Test edge case: exactly-at-budget (should pass)
   g. Verify: JSONL output is parseable by jq
   h. Verify: exit code is non-zero when any section exceeds budget

2. Integration test: after building a real bare-metal target (requires bd-aw69.5),
   run the footprint script and verify output matches readelf section sizes.

3. Regression test: run twice, feed both outputs to compute_layout_budget_delta.sh,
   verify delta is zero (deterministic builds).

## What Already Works (EXTEND, DON'T REPLACE)
- generate_layout_budget_report.sh (for musl targets)
- compute_layout_budget_delta.sh (for cross-run comparison)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Bare-metal footprint measured reproducibly for both profiles on all 4 targets
- JSONL output per-section with summary line per target/profile
- Budget thresholds documented with rationale in docs/EMBEDDED.md
- Companion test script validates measurement logic with synthetic .map files
- Over-budget failures produce non-zero exit code and clear JSONL error detail
- JSON output compatible with existing compute_layout_budget_delta.sh

title: QEMU e2e tests: run asupersync unit test subset on ARM and RISC-V targets
description:
## Context
The current QEMU setup (bd-aw69.3) only validates that trivial "return 0" binaries
run. This is necessary but insufficient — it proves QEMU works, not that asupersync
works on embedded targets. We need to run actual asupersync operations under
emulation to prove functional correctness on ARM and RISC-V.

## IMPORTANT: Existing Linux-musl QEMU Infrastructure
tools/ci/run_qemu_smoke.sh (395 lines) already provides a COMPLETE QEMU user-mode
test harness for Linux-musl targets (mipsel/armv7/aarch64). It includes:
- qemu-*-static binary detection and execution
- JSONL logging, timeout handling, artifact collection, trace digest
- CLI: --build-first, --dry-run, --strict, --timeout, --target

This bead creates COMPLEMENTARY bare-metal QEMU semihosting tests (ARM Cortex-M,
RISC-V), NOT a replacement for run_qemu_smoke.sh. The existing harness tests
Linux-musl targets; this bead tests bare-metal targets with semihosting.

## Background
Running the full 64-suite test battery under bare-metal QEMU is impractical: the tests
use host-specific features (printf for test output, malloc for CORE profile tests, etc.).
Instead, we need a curated subset of tests that:
- Use only FREESTANDING or EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile APIs
- Don't require host stdio (use semihosting for minimal output)
- Don't depend on real timers or threading
- Exercise the critical path: region lifecycle, task scheduling, obligation tracking

## Task
1. Create tests/embedded/embedded_smoke.c — a self-contained test program that:
   a. Provides custom asx_runtime_hooks (static buffer allocator, no-op log_sink,
      monotonic counter as logical_clock)
   b. Opens a region, spawns tasks, runs scheduler, drains region
   c. Verifies task states, obligation states, quiescence
   d. Tests channel operations (EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile only, ifdef-guarded)
   e. Reports pass/fail via semihosting exit code (0 = pass, non-zero = fail count)
   f. Optionally emits minimal test log via semihosting SYS_WRITE0

2. Create tests/embedded/embedded_channel_smoke.c — channel-specific tests for
   EMBEDDED_ROUTER profile:
   a. Channel create, reserve, send, recv, close
   b. Backpressure (full channel returns correct error)
   c. Fairness (round-robin recv across multiple senders)

3. Create tools/ci/run_qemu_e2e.sh that:
   a. Cross-compiles embedded_smoke.c + libasx.a for each bare-metal target
   b. Runs under QEMU with semihosting (qemu-system-arm -semihosting, etc.)
   c. Captures exit code and semihosting output
   d. Reports per-target results with JSONL logging
   e. Runs EMBEDDED_ROUTER tests on targets that support it
   f. Uses same JSONL format conventions as existing run_qemu_smoke.sh for consistency

4. JSONL Log Format (consistent with run_qemu_smoke.sh):
   {"ts":"...","test":"embedded_smoke","target":"arm-m4-free","status":"pass","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":1200}
   {"ts":"...","test":"embedded_channel_smoke","target":"arm-m4-router","status":"pass","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":1800}

5. Test the test: create tests/embedded/test_hooks_minimal.c that unit-tests the
   custom hooks implementation (static allocator, counter clock) to ensure the test
   infrastructure itself is correct.

## Integration with Existing Infrastructure
- run_qemu_e2e.sh should REUSE tools/ci/run_qemu_baremetal.sh (from bd-aw69.3) for
  the actual QEMU semihosting invocation — do NOT duplicate QEMU launch logic
- run_qemu_e2e.sh handles: cross-compilation, test selection, result aggregation
- run_qemu_baremetal.sh handles: QEMU binary selection, semihosting flags, timeout, exit code capture
- Both scripts follow the same CLI conventions as run_qemu_smoke.sh
  (--dry-run, --strict, --timeout, --target)
- JSONL output should be compatible with the same log aggregation tooling
- The CI gate (bd-aw69.7) should run BOTH run_qemu_smoke.sh (Linux-musl) AND
  run_qemu_e2e.sh (bare-metal) for comprehensive coverage

## Static Allocator Design
The FREESTANDING profile needs a static buffer allocator for hooks:
- Pre-allocated uint8_t buffer[8192] (configurable)
- Bump allocator with alignment support
- realloc via copy-to-new-offset (no real realloc needed)
- free is a no-op (bump allocator doesn't reclaim)
- This is intentionally simple — good enough for test scenarios

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Global timer wheel time is never advanced: asx_deadline_arm refuses deadlines more than 24h past time 0 (live builds with uptime > 1 day)
description: Found by code reading in the bd-9kll.2.12 doc pass, confirmed 2026-10-10. src/time/deadline.c asx_deadline_arm registers dl->target_ns (an absolute asx_runtime_now_ns()-based time) on asx_timer_wheel_global(). title: twin_run: a spawned child whose handle never resolves fails capture (gen-275-53)
description: Found by fuzz campaign 2 (seeds 260-299, 2026-10-11): twin_run capture of generated scenario gen-275-53 (seed 275, index 53) fails with 'spawned task "t.3.c1" was never admitted (scenario or harness defect)' (project_denied_spawns, tools/twin_run/src/run.rs:3449-3487). Shape: region_limits max_tasks=3/max_children=2 on r.main at 0, cancel_region r.main (Deadline) at 50; t.3 locks a contended mutex, sleeps 200, then spawns t.3.c1 (a closing region by then). The handle's outcome was never harvested (raw_outcomes has no entry), so the projection cannot classify the refusal (ASX_E_REGION_CLOSED vs ASX_E_ADMISSION_LIMIT). The fuzz target tolerates refused captures (Makefile fuzz-differential: >=90% captured), so the seed still reports clean and the scenario is silently not compared. Reproduce: twin_run generate --seed 275 --count 200, then twin_run capture on gen-275-53.json. Done when: twin_run resolves such a spawn (harvesting its handle at the end of the run, or classifying it from the admission error) and the scenario captures and compares; one of 8000 generated scenarios hit it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Diagnosis: the end-of-run harvest (tools/twin_run/src/run.rs:2750-2770) calls handle.try_join() on every unjoined handle; a child whose cx.spawn is still in the spawn mailbox when the run ends (never admitted, never refused) yields Ok(None), so raw_outcomes has no entry and project_denied_spawns fails closed. Needed: a vocabulary rule for a spawn still pending admission at the end of the run (likely: the spawn step keeps its ASX_OK observation, the child has no snapshot entry and no trace events), the same projection in twin_run, and C's interpreter reporting a lab_admission_pending child that way; then capture gen-275-53 (seed 275 index 53) as a fixture.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-10-12, twin_run at 925294d (upstream e03ec46/841946a included): gen-275-53 (/var/tmp/asx-probe/fzg2/seed-275/scenarios on 212.90.121.76) still fails capture. Trigger confirmed: the same scenario with t.3's two abort_task steps on t.3.c1 removed captures and passes, Rust then refusing the spawn ASX_E_REGION_CLOSED (r.main was cancelled at 50), which is what C observes on the spawn step in both versions (C refuses at spawn time; asx-conformance run shows spawn ASX_E_REGION_CLOSED, aborts ASX_OK, quiescent). So: a JoinHandle::abort of a cx.spawn child whose admission the lab has not yet processed (likely the same poll: t.3's quorum members are refused at once, so the aborts run before t.3 yields) leaves Rust's handle unresolved for good (try_join Ok(None) at the end-of-run harvest, run.rs abort_task captures a refusal only if the handle is already finished). Fix options: (a) DSL rule: abort_task of a child still pending admission is outside the DSL, and the generator avoids it (abort only after a yielding step); (b) projection rule: twin_run records the target's admission outcome when the lab finally processes it, if it does, and otherwise reports the spawn as the admission would have (closing region -> ASX_E_REGION_CLOSED), which needs a check of what Rust's lab does with an aborted pending spawn (lab/runtime.rs admission path). (a) is cheap and honest; (b) needs the Rust admission code read. Not done yet.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Pointer for option (b): Rust TaskHandle::abort_with_reason (runtime/task_handle.rs:1005) calls apply_or_defer_cancel_reason with the admitted slot, deferring the reason until admission; and the handle's result sits behind a RetirementBarrier (try_join does not see a terminal until the scheduler opens it post-retirement). One of these likely keeps the refused child's result invisible to try_join at the end-of-run harvest; check both before choosing a projection rule.

title: [Epic] POSIX Platform Adapter
description:
Replace the empty src/platform/posix/hooks.c stub with a real POSIX platform adapter that populates asx_runtime_hooks for live-mode POSIX targets.

## Background
The asx runtime uses a composed hook family architecture (asx_runtime_hooks in include/asx/asx_config.h) with 5 categories: allocator, clock, entropy, reactor, log. Default implementations in src/runtime/hooks.c provide safe fallbacks (malloc, return-0 clock, counter PRNG, 0-event reactor, stderr log). Platform adapters override these defaults with real OS primitives.

Currently src/platform/posix/hooks.c is completely empty inside its #ifdef ASX_PROFILE_POSIX guard. This means anyone building with -DASX_PROFILE_POSIX gets zero platform integration — no real clock, no real entropy, no real reactor, no real threading.

## Scope
Wave B/C. The CORE profile (Wave A) works without this, but POSIX profile users need real hooks for live-mode operation.

## Deliverables
1. Clock hooks: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) for wall time, passthrough for logical time
2. Entropy hook: getrandom(2) with /dev/urandom fallback for seeded PRNG initialization
3. Reactor hook: epoll_create1/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait wrapper for the reactor.wait_fn
4. Blocking pool worker: pthread_create + condvar replacing inline execution
5. Export function: asx_posix_hooks_install(asx_runtime_hooks *h) as single entry point
6. Public header: include/asx/platform/posix.h declaring the install function
7. Unit tests: clock monotonicity, entropy distribution, reactor basic poll
8. Makefile: build-posix target with conditional PLATFORM_SRC and -lpthread linking
9. E2E smoke: tests/e2e/posix_adapter_smoke.sh exercising clock+entropy+reactor in a live scenario

## Hook signatures (from asx_config.h)
- allocator: malloc_fn(ctx, size), realloc_fn(ctx, ptr, size), free_fn(ctx, ptr)
- clock: now_ns_fn(ctx) -> asx_time, logical_now_ns_fn(ctx) -> asx_time
- entropy: random_u64_fn(ctx) -> uint64_t
- reactor: wait_fn(ctx, timeout_ms, ready_count), ghost_wait_fn(ctx, logical_step, ready_count)
- log: write_fn(ctx, level, message)

## Files
- src/platform/posix/hooks.c (modify: replace empty stub)
- include/asx/platform/posix.h (new: public declaration)
- Makefile (modify: add build-posix target)
- tests/unit/platform/test_posix_hooks.c (new: unit tests)
- tests/e2e/posix_adapter_smoke.sh (new: e2e smoke)
close_reason: All 9 deliverables complete: clock hooks, entropy hook, reactor (epoll+poll), blocking pool (pthread), install function, public header, unit tests (12 passing), Makefile build-posix target, E2E smoke test (7/7 scenarios). Header comment updated.

title: CLI: implement main.c with doctor, info, and version subcommands
description:
## Deliverable
Create src/cli/main.c — a standalone CLI entry point that links against libasx.a and provides:

### Relationship to existing cli.c
src/cli/cli.c (158 lines) already exists and provides LIBRARY UTILITY functions (output format parsing, flag helpers, etc). These are part of libasx.a.

The NEW main.c is a SEPARATE standalone entry point that USES the existing cli.c utilities. It is NOT compiled into libasx.a — it only links against it. This separation means:
- cli.c stays in the library as utility functions
- main.c is a standalone program that links libasx.a

### `asx version`
Print: asx <version> (profile=<PROFILE> codec=<CODEC> det=<0|1>)
Use asx_version_string() if available, or construct from compile-time macros.

### `asx info`
Print:
- Active profile name and ID (via asx_profile_active() / asx_profile_name())
- Resource class (R1/R2/R3) with limits table (via asx_profile_resource_config())
- Number of ASX_API declarations (compile-time constant)
- Compile-time flags (ASX_PROFILE_*, ASX_CODEC_*, ASX_DETERMINISTIC)
- Available surfaces (via asx_surface_gate() for each surface)

### `asx doctor`
Run diagnostic checks using existing app/doctor.c APIs:
- Verify hooks are installed and validate (asx_runtime_hooks_validate)
- Check clock monotonicity (call now_ns twice, verify non-decreasing)
- Check entropy (generate 10 samples, verify variance)
- Check allocator (malloc/free a small buffer)
- Report pass/fail for each check with descriptive names
- Support --format json for structured output (use asx_cli_parse_output_format from cli.c)
- Return exit code 0 if all pass, 1 otherwise

### Argument parsing
Simple hand-rolled parsing (no getopt dependency for freestanding compat):
- `asx` with no args → print usage summary
- `asx version` → version info
- `asx info` → profile/capability info
- `asx doctor [--format text|json]` → run diagnostics
- `asx help` / `asx --help` / `asx -h` → full usage
- Unknown subcommand → error message + usage, exit 1

### Makefile integration
Add to Makefile:
```make
CLI_BIN := build/bin/asx

cli: $(LIB_A) src/cli/main.c | build/bin
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $(CLI_BIN) src/cli/main.c $(LIB_A) $(LDFLAGS)

build/bin:
	mkdir -p build/bin
```
Also add `cli` to the .PHONY list and optionally to `make install` (install the binary alongside the library).

### Error handling
All subcommands must handle initialization failures gracefully:
- If asx_runtime_hooks_init fails, print error and exit 1
- If profile detection fails, print 'unknown profile' rather than crashing

## Files
- src/cli/main.c (new: ~200-300 lines)
- Makefile (modify: add cli target, build/bin directory)
close_reason: Created src/cli/main.c with 3 subcommands: version (prints version/profile/codec/det), info (prints profile descriptor with resource limits), doctor (runs asx_doctor_run with text and --format=json output). title: Child regions: Enforce parent-waits-for-children in drain
description:
Modify the drain/finalize path so that a parent region cannot advance past CLOSING while it has live (non-CLOSED) children.

## Current behavior
The drain path in quiescence.c (around line 215) advances regions through CLOSING → DRAINING → FINALIZING → CLOSED. Currently it skips DRAINING ("no children (walking skeleton) — fast path").

## New behavior
Before advancing past CLOSING:
1. Check r->child_count > 0
2. If yes: stay in CLOSING, return ASX_E_PENDING (children must close first)
3. If no: proceed to DRAINING as before

This ensures the parent region lifecycle respects the child region hierarchy. Children must be explicitly closed before parent can finalize.

## Files
- src/runtime/quiescence.c (modify: drain advancement logic)
close_reason: Implemented parent-waits-for-children drain semantics

title: Child regions: Track child close and decrement parent child_count
description:
When a child region transitions to CLOSED state, decrement the parent's child_count and remove the child from the parent's children[] array.

## Changes
In src/runtime/lifecycle.c, find where region state becomes CLOSED (likely in the drain/finalize path in quiescence.c or lifecycle.c). Add:
1. If region->parent_id != ASX_INVALID_ID: look up parent slot
2. Scan parent->children[] for this region's id
3. Remove it (shift remaining entries or swap with last)
4. Decrement parent->child_count
5. Handle edge case: parent already closed/freed — log warning but don't crash

## Idempotency
Must be safe if called multiple times (e.g., if close path runs twice due to error recovery). Check child is actually in parent's list before decrementing.

## Files
- src/runtime/lifecycle.c or src/runtime/quiescence.c (modify)

title: EPIC: Hardcoded Constants, Stale Comments, and Code Quality Remediation
description:
Master epic for systematically addressing all hardcoded magic numbers that should be configurable,
stale/misleading comments indicating unfinished code, and related code quality issues discovered
during a comprehensive fresh-eyes audit of the entire asupersync ANSI C codebase.

## Background

A full-project audit was conducted scanning every .c and .h file for:
1. Hardcoded numeric constants in function bodies that should be named #define macros
2. Comments containing "will", "would", "TODO", "FIXME" indicating unfinished or deferred work
3. Stale documentation that no longer matches the actual implementation state

## Scope

This epic covers:
- Converting 4 hardcoded magic numbers to named, #ifndef-guarded compile-time constants
- Updating 2 stale header comments that incorrectly describe code as stubs/future work
- Identifying and documenting items verified as correct (not needing changes)
- Ensuring all changes compile cleanly with -Werror and pass existing test suites

## Architectural Principle

The asx project uses a "resource contracts instead of silent degradation" philosophy (README).
Every operational parameter should be:
1. Named (self-documenting in code)
2. Overridable at compile time (#ifndef guard)
3. Documented with its default value and unit
4. Consistent with the profile/resource-class system

This ensures embedded deployers (R1/R2/R3 resource classes) and specialized profiles
(HFT, AUTOMOTIVE) can tune thresholds without modifying source code.

## Verification

All changes MUST:
- Build cleanly with `make build` (strict -Werror)
- Pass all existing unit tests
- Not change any runtime behavior when using default values
- Be backward-compatible (existing code that doesn't override the macros gets identical behavior)
close_reason: All tasks completed: 4 constants extracted, 2 comments fixed, audit trail documented

title: SUB-EPIC: Hardcoded Magic Numbers → Named Compile-Time Constants
description:
Convert all hardcoded magic numbers in function bodies to named #define macros with
#ifndef guards, enabling compile-time override by deployers.

## Why This Matters

The asx project targets 9 deployment profiles (CORE through BROWSER) and 3 resource
classes (R1/R2/R3). Each profile has different operational envelopes. Hardcoded constants
prevent deployers from tuning behavior without source modification, violating the
"resource contracts instead of silent degradation" principle.

## Pattern

For each constant:
1. Add `#ifndef ASX_<MODULE>_<NAME>` / `#define` / `#endif` in the relevant public header
2. Replace the literal in the .c file with the macro name
3. Update any doc comments referencing the old literal value
4. Verify the default value matches the original literal exactly (zero behavior change)

## Constants Identified

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | New Macro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Process wait poll guard | process.c:235 | 10000 | polls | ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS |
| App default poll budget | app.c:125 | 10000 | polls | ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET |
| HFT p99 gate threshold | hft_instrument.c:281 | 10000 | nanoseconds | ASX_HFT_DEFAULT_P99_NS |
| Automotive watchdog period | automotive_instrument.c:250,258 | 10000000 | nanoseconds | ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS |

## Items Audited and Verified as Correct (No Change Needed)

These were examined and confirmed to be intentionally placed:
- hooks.c:62 `return 0` — Intentional platform hook stub; overridden at runtime init
- lab.c:57,93 `1000000ULL` tick_ns — Default in config struct; already user-configurable via asx_lab_config
- console.c:84 "would check isatty()" — Design note explaining platform-specific behavior
- plan.c:413 "this would set up a deadline" — Explaining deterministic simulation vs real async
- Profile overload thresholds (90/85/80/75%) in overload_catalog.c — Intentional per-profile policy
- Seqlock spike retry limits (100, 1000) — Experimental research code, not production path
close_reason: All 4 hardcoded constants extracted to named #ifndef-guarded macros

title: Extract ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS from process.c:235
description:
## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000u` poll guard in asx_process_wait_with_output() with a named
compile-time constant ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/process/process.h (add #ifndef/#define/#endif block)
- Source: src/process/process.c line 235 (replace literal with macro)

## Why

asx_process_wait_with_output() polls in a bounded loop to prevent infinite hangs when
waiting for a child process to exit. The 10,000 iteration limit was chosen as a reasonable
default, but embedded deployers on slow hardware may need more iterations, while
latency-sensitive HFT profiles may want fewer.

Without a named constant, the only way to change this is to edit source code directly,
which violates the profile/resource-class customization model.

## Implementation

```c
// In process.h, after ASX_PROCESS_PROGRAM_MAX:
#ifndef ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS
#define ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS 10000u
#endif

// In process.c:235:
uint32_t max_polls = ASX_PROCESS_WAIT_MAX_POLLS;
```

## Verification

- `make build` passes with -Werror
- All process-related tests pass
- Default behavior unchanged (10000 iterations when macro not overridden)

## Status: COMPLETED

This task has been implemented and verified.

title: Extract ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET from app.c:125
description:
## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000` default poll budget in asx_app_init() with a named
compile-time constant ASX_APP_DEFAULT_POLL_BUDGET.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/app/app.h (add #ifndef/#define/#endif before asx_app_config typedef)
- Source: src/app/app.c line 125 (replace literal with macro)

When a user creates an asx_app_config with poll_budget=0, the app framework defaults to

## What

Replace the hardcoded `10000000u` (10ms) watchdog period in automotive_instrument.c
with a named compile-time constant ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS. This literal
appeared in TWO locations: ensure_auto_init() and asx_auto_instrument_reset().

- Header: include/asx/runtime/automotive_instrument.h (add before Watchdog monitor section)
- Source: src/runtime/automotive_instrument.c lines 250 and 258 (both replaced)

The automotive watchdog monitors checkpoint intervals for safety-critical systems.
If a monitored entity goes longer than the watchdog period without checkpointing,
a violation is recorded. The 10ms default is appropriate for typical automotive ECUs,
but:
- Fast-cycle control loops (engine management) may need 1ms (1000000ns)
- Slow-cycle monitoring (climate control) may use 100ms (100000000ns)
- Functional safety standards (ISO 26262) may mandate specific intervals

The automotive profile exists specifically for this kind of safety-tuning.
Hardcoding the watchdog period undermines the profile's purpose.

The literal appeared in both ensure_auto_init() and asx_auto_instrument_reset().
Both MUST use the same macro to ensure reset restores the same default as initial
construction. Using different values would create a subtle behavior difference
between first-init and post-reset states.

## Implementation

```c
// In automotive_instrument.h:
#ifndef ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS
#define ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS 10000000u
#endif

// In automotive_instrument.c (both sites):
asx_auto_watchdog_init(&g_watchdog, ASX_AUTO_DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_PERIOD_NS);
```

/* asx/raptorq/raptorq.h — RaptorQ erasure coding surface (fail-closed stub)

 *
 * Provides XOR-based erasure coding for symbol recovery. Encodes

title: Fix stale parallel.h header: remove future-tense 'will be added' promise
description:
## What

Update the parallel.h header comment from "Real multi-threaded dispatch will be added
when platform threading hooks are implemented" to a factual present-tense description.

## Where

- Header: include/asx/runtime/parallel.h lines 8-10

## Before (Stale)

```c
 * Walking skeleton: single-threaded simulation of lane scheduling.
 * Real multi-threaded dispatch will be added when platform threading
 * hooks are implemented.
```

## After (Factual)

```c
 * Currently provides single-threaded lane scheduling simulation.
 * Multi-threaded dispatch requires platform threading hooks.
```

## Why

The original comment made a promise about future work ("will be added when...").
This is problematic because:
1. It implies someone is actively working on threading (they may not be)
2. It doesn't say WHAT the current code actually does (walking skeleton simulation)
3. Future-tense promises in code comments become stale the moment the developer moves on

The fix changes to present-tense factual description: here's what it does now,
here's what's needed to go further. No promises about when or if.

## General Principle

Comments should describe WHAT IS, not WHAT WILL BE. If something is planned,
track it in beads (the issue tracker), not in code comments. Comments that say
"will" or "TODO" are essentially invisible issue tickets with no assignee,
no priority, and no dependency tracking.

title: [Epic] Child Region Tracking and Q2 Quiescence Fix
description:
Fix the only semantic contract violation in the walking skeleton: the Q2 quiescence conjunct (child regions closed) is hardcoded to 1 at src/runtime/quiescence.c:150 without actually checking.

## Background
The quiescence contract (docs/QUIESCENCE_FINALIZATION_INVARIANTS.md) requires four conjuncts:
- Q1: all tasks complete (implemented: checks r->task_count)
- Q2: all child regions closed (HARDCODED TO 1 — THIS IS THE BUG)
- Q3: all obligations resolved (implemented: checks obligations_reserved)
- Q4: cleanup stack drained (implemented: checks cleanup_drained)

The current code at quiescence.c line 150:
    /* Q2: all child regions closed (walking skeleton: always true) */
    out->q2_children_closed = 1;

This means any parent region with open child regions will incorrectly report as quiescent. The fix requires implementing a parent-child region model.

## Architecture
asx_region_slot (src/runtime/runtime_internal.h) currently has: state, task_count, task_total, generation, alive, poisoned, cleanup, capture_arena, capture_used. We need to add: parent_id, child_count, children[N].

The existing asx_region_open() creates root regions. We add asx_region_open_child(parent, &child) for hierarchical regions.

## Scope
Wave A — Critical. This is the only false assertion in the quiescence contract.

## Deliverables
1. Extended region slot struct with parent/child tracking
2. New asx_region_open_child() public API
3. Child close tracking (decrement parent's child_count on child CLOSED)
4. Real Q2 check: (r->child_count == 0) replaces hardcoded 1
5. Parent-waits-for-children drain enforcement
6. Comprehensive unit tests (parent/child lifecycle, Q2 verification, drain blocking)
7. CBMC harness for parent-child transition safety
8. E2E scenario exercising nested region lifecycle

## Risk
Touching runtime_internal.h affects sizeof(asx_region_slot) which affects static arena sizing. Must verify ASX_MAX_REGIONS * sizeof(new_slot) stays within acceptable BSS limits. children[8] adds 8*4=32 bytes + parent_id(4) + child_count(4) = 40 bytes per slot. With ASX_MAX_REGIONS=32, that's 1.25KB additional BSS.

## Files
- src/runtime/runtime_internal.h (modify: extend asx_region_slot)
- include/asx/asx_config.h (modify: add ASX_MAX_REGION_CHILDREN)
- include/asx/runtime/runtime.h (modify: add asx_region_open_child decl)
- src/runtime/lifecycle.c (modify: child open/close tracking)
- src/runtime/quiescence.c (modify: Q2 check, drain enforcement)
- tests/unit/runtime/test_quiescence.c (modify: add child region tests)
- tests/formal/cbmc/child_region_harness.c (new: CBMC harness)
- tests/e2e/e2e_nested_regions.c (new: e2e scenario)

title: [Epic] RaptorQ Erasure Decode with Symbol Recovery
description:
Implement actual erasure recovery in asx_raptorq_decode(). Currently, the decode function at src/raptorq/raptorq.c:120-127 just memcpy's all received symbols without any recovery from lost symbols:

    /* Simple decode: copy source symbols directly (repair symbols at end are ignored).
     * Full recovery from symbol loss would require the repair XOR equations. */
    memcpy(dst, syms, copy_len);

The encode side (lines 82-94) already generates real XOR repair symbols using the pattern: repair[j] = XOR of source symbols where (i + j) % r == 0. The decoder must invert these equations.

## Background
The RaptorQ module (src/raptorq/raptorq.c) implements a simplified XOR-based erasure code (not RFC 6330 compliant). It provides encode/decode for the asx codec surface. The encoder works correctly — it generates k source symbols + r repair symbols. But the decoder ignores repair symbols entirely, meaning any symbol loss results in data corruption.

## Algorithm
The XOR peeling decoder:
1. Build an equation matrix: each repair symbol covers a known set of source symbols
2. Iterative peeling: find any equation with exactly 1 unknown source symbol, solve it (XOR repair with known sources)
3. Repeat until all source symbols are recovered or no single-unknown equations remain
4. If stuck: declare unrecoverable (ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED)

## Scope
Wave A. The encode is real; the decode must match.

## Deliverables
1. New asx_raptorq_decode_with_erasures() API taking symbol_present bitmap
2. XOR peeling solver implementation
3. Decodability rank check (fail early if too many losses)
4. Updated existing decode to fast-path when all symbols present
5. Unit tests: no-loss, single-loss, max-recoverable, unrecoverable
6. E2E erasure recovery test with detailed logging
7. Conformance test vectors with known erasure patterns

## Files
- include/asx/raptorq/raptorq.h (modify: add new decode API)
- src/raptorq/raptorq.c (modify: implement recovery)
- tests/unit/raptorq/test_raptorq.c (modify: add erasure tests)
- tests/e2e/e2e_raptorq_erasure.c (new: e2e erasure scenario)
close_reason: All RaptorQ tasks complete: API (bd-yf9u), XOR peeling solver (bd-1fsi), rank check (bd-3nny), unit tests (bd-zt9e), E2E scenario (bd-rwax). The simplified XOR erasure decoder recovers from single-symbol losses; multi-symbol recovery is limited by the peeling-only approach (documented in E2E test). Evidence: tests/unit/raptorq/test_raptorq.c, tests/e2e/e2e_raptorq_erasure.c. Artifact evidence: build/e2e/

title: EPIC: Build System, Portability Matrix, and Repository Scaffold
description:
Background:
The runtime must compile and behave predictably across host and constrained targets. Build portability is a first-class requirement, not cleanup work.

Goal:
Establish build/repo infrastructure for GCC/Clang/MSVC plus embedded cross-target matrix, including QEMU validation harness.

Must preserve:
- dependency-free core assumptions
- profile-aware compile paths
- reproducible, diagnosable failures

Why this serves users:
- HFT teams need deterministic reproducible builds
- embedded teams need cross-target confidence before deployment
- maintainers need fast feedback loops with clear failure surfaces.

Cross-cutting quality contract:
- Child tasks must define and link unit tests, e2e script coverage (when behavioral), and structured log/manifest artifacts or explicit rationale for non-applicability.
- Completion evidence must remain compatible with bd-66l.9 enforcement and traceability index expectations.

title: Race outcome reason drift: a region Timeout cancel vs the task's budget deadline 0 (fuzz gen-622-100)
description:
Found 2026-10-11 by the Rust-vs-C differential campaign (twin_run at d9043b5 generator, C at 5c7dd2e; seed 622 scenario 100), minimized by twin_run minimize to 6 elements.

Minimized scenario (asx.scenario.v2): region r.main; task t.3 in r.main with budget {deadline_ns: 0}; program [sleep 150, race with one empty member [[]]]; script: at 0 cancel_region r.main kind Timeout.

Divergence (observations[1], the race step's outcome):
- Rust: cancelled, reason kind Deadline, origin_region r.main, origin_task t.3, timestamp 0.
- C:    cancelled, reason kind Timeout, origin_region r.main, origin_task null, timestamp 0.

So in Rust the race's member outcome carries the task's own budget-deadline reason (origin the task), while C carries the region's Timeout cancel. Likely the strengthen/tie rule between the Cx's budget-deadline reason and a region cancel request of equal severity (Timeout vs Deadline) as seen by a race member, or which reason the race projects for a member that never ran. Related fixes for budget-quota reconciliation: bdebada (record/task.rs:839-850 tie keeps the Cx's own reason).

title: Child regions: Add asx_region_open_child() public API
description:
Add a new public API for opening a child region under a parent.

## API
asx_status asx_region_open_child(asx_region_id parent, asx_region_id *out_child);

## Semantics
1. Validate parent is alive and in OPEN state (via asx_region_slot_lookup + state check)
2. Validate parent's child_count < ASX_MAX_REGION_CHILDREN (return ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED if full)
3. Call existing asx_region_open(out_child) to allocate the child slot
4. Set child's parent_id = parent
5. Add child's id to parent's children[] array
6. Increment parent's child_count
7. Return ASX_OK

## Error conditions
- ASX_E_INVALID_ARGUMENT: null out_child
- ASX_E_NOT_FOUND: parent not found
- ASX_E_REGION_NOT_OPEN: parent not in OPEN state
- ASX_E_REGION_POISONED: parent is poisoned
- ASX_E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: child slots full or no region slots available

## Files
- include/asx/runtime/runtime.h (add declaration)
- src/runtime/lifecycle.c (implement)

title: Budget-exhaustion cancels stay Cx-only until acknowledged (Rust); C writes them into the task record at once
description: Found by the differential fuzzer (bd-ij9w, seed 2, gen-2-91). In Rust a cancel raised by budget exhaustion (Cx::checkpoint's checkpoint_budget_exhaustion, cx.rs:2824-2836, and the lab's pre-poll quota check, lab/runtime.rs:4663-4670) only sets cancel_requested and the reason on the task's Cx. The TaskRecord stays Running until a checkpoint acknowledges the cancel and the scheduler reconciles it (TaskRecord::consume_checkpoint_cancel_ack, record/task.rs ~1171-1240). A task whose quota runs out inside a masked section and that then waits forever on a wait that is not cancel-aware (gen-2-91: poll_quota 2, sleep, masked checkpoint, notify_wait) therefore ends with record state Running, no cancel_reason and no cleanup_budget. C's asx_task_cancel_budget_internal moves the task to CANCEL_REQUESTED with the reason at once. Visible effects: (1) snapshot state/reason of such stuck tasks; (2) likely trace differences, because a later region cancel finds the Rust record still Running, so it counts as newly cancelled and records cancel.requested, while C only strengthens an existing cancel and records nothing. Fix sketch: keep a Cx-level pending budget cancel (reason, strengthened) beside the record state; asx_checkpoint reports it; an unmasked checkpoint materializes it into the record (request then acknowledge) as consume_checkpoint_cancel_ack does; region and direct cancels see an unmaterialized task as newly cancelled. Check what outcome a task that completes with an unacknowledged Cx cancel gets (Rust's spawn completion policies). Acceptance: gen-2-91 matches, a unit test for the masked case, and no regression in conformance or the fuzz batches.
close_reason: Implemented with unit tests; gen-2-91 and all 1466 fuzz scenarios match Rust

title: perf: per-event trace digest dominates spawn+run (55 -> 190 ns since March at -O2); SLO baselines stale and need an approved refresh
description:
Perf Gates (perf.yml) failed all of its last 200 runs. Findings 2026-10-10 (measured on one worker core, interleaved, -O2 library both sides):

FIXED in a846aa9: (1) the workflow timed and sized a -O0 library: make release then make bench rebuilt every object at -O0 via the build-config stamp (since 66a4c39); bench goals now default to BUILD_TYPE=release. (2) the trace digest fold is exact but folds high zero-byte runs as one multiply: emit 27 -> 20 ns, warm spawn+run 275 -> 190 ns, multi_task median 7.6 -> ~4.5 us, timer_cancel 3.3 -> 1.9 us, channel_recv 1.7 -> ~0.9 us. Digest unchanged (test_trace trace_digest_is_fnv1a_over_le_event_fields).

OPEN, needs a decision:
A. Digest cost. Every trace event is folded into the rolling FNV-1a digest at emit (468d212, bd-9kll.10.1, needed so the digest covers events past the ring). A spawn+run emits 7 events; byte-serial FNV-1a has a floor of ~4 cycles/byte (24 bytes/event), so ~20 ns/event remains: ~140 of the 190 ns warm spawn+run (March baseline 07b1938: 55 ns). A word-wise mix (e.g. xor-multiply per u64 field, ~4 multiplies/event) would cut it to ~5 ns/event, but it changes the digest function: trace.c fold, the telemetry digest that is documented identical at FORENSIC tier (include/asx/runtime/telemetry.h:84), hindsight, snapshot event_hash, the binary trace export, and any recorded digests. Not done without the owner's decision.
B. SLO baselines (tools/ci/slo_baselines.json) were captured 2026-03-01 (223 days; max_age_days 120) at 07b1938, probably from a -O0 library; governance says approval_required. With -O2 on a loaded worker (load ~8/10 cores) the CORE gate still shows 10 violations (scheduler tails, multi_round p99.9 186 us vs 75 us budget). Refresh needs: an agreed capture host (CI runner vs dev host), -O2 (now the default for bench goals), and the owner's approval of the accepted regression in A.
C. asx_runtime_reset went 0.4 -> 8.8 us (-O2): it now clears ~MBs of statics (net/ws/quic tables, task ledgers, error ledger). Not a hot path, but the bench's cold timings run right after it, with caches evicted.

Acceptance: Perf Gates green on main for 3 consecutive pushes with no budget raised beyond the documented headroom policy, and the HFT steps (currently skipped because the CORE step fails first) executed.
notes: 2026-10-12: bounded exact-FNV optimization experiment now executing in isolated main sources, preserving existing digests, canonical fixtures, budgets/baselines and full original acceptance. SCHED_POLL has kind0, allowing its sequence4+kind4 digest bytes to be folded as sequence8. Actual same-CPU interleaved before/candidate benchmarks and byte-loop/digest/replay/conformance checks required; reject if no repeatable benefit or material regression. Original three-green-push acceptance is not met and will remain in_progress even if this narrow optimization lands.

title: [Epic] Win32 Platform Adapter
description:
Replace the empty src/platform/win32/hooks.c stub with a real Win32 platform adapter that populates asx_runtime_hooks for live-mode Windows targets.

## Background
Same hook architecture as POSIX adapter (see POSIX epic for details on asx_runtime_hooks struct). Win32 uses different OS APIs: QueryPerformanceCounter for timing, BCryptGenRandom for entropy, WSAPoll or IOCP for reactor, CreateThread for blocking pool.

## Scope
Wave B/C. Lower priority than POSIX since the primary development environment is Linux.

## Deliverables
1. Clock hooks: QueryPerformanceCounter/QueryPerformanceFrequency for monotonic ns
2. Entropy hook: BCryptGenRandom from bcrypt.h
3. Reactor hook: WSAPoll or CreateIoCompletionPort wrapper
4. Blocking pool worker: CreateThread + event object for completion signaling
5. Export function: asx_win32_hooks_install(asx_runtime_hooks *h)
6. Public header: include/asx/platform/win32.h
7. Cross-compilation tests: verify compilation with mingw-w64 (no runtime execution)
8. Makefile: build-win32 target with conditional linking (-lbcrypt, -lws2_32)

## Files
- src/platform/win32/hooks.c (modify: replace empty stub)
- include/asx/platform/win32.h (new: public declaration)
- Makefile (modify: add build-win32 target)

title: region_limits max_tasks under lab dispatch: check at the next step's admission, refuse late, and treat refused task-group members as cancelled
description: Rust checks a spawn against RegionLimits.max_tasks when the next lab step admits it from the spawn mailbox (record/region.rs add_task_internal via state.rs:4333), after earlier queued spawns and after the spawner's own completion; a refused spawn resolves its handle Cancelled(User, '[ASUP-E006] region admission limit reached: region=RegionId(i:g) limit=N live=M — ...'), which twin_run projects as ASX_E_ADMISSION_LIMIT on the spawn step and joins. C (asx_task_spawn) checks at the call. With max_tasks in generated scenarios, 30 seeds x 200 gave 50 divergences (spawn admitted in Rust, refused in C, and following trace/dispatch drift), all with max_tasks set; child and obligation limits gave none. title: EPIC: Production parallel runtime for 64-core agent swarms
description:

POSIX detached blocking submit exists but is not wired into `asx_runtime_hooks`/`blocking.c`.

Goal:
Graduate parallel execution for massive agent-swarm deployments while preserving the project invariant that profiles alter resource/operational envelopes, not semantic behavior. The target is a runtime path that can exploit 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM without nondeterministic semantic drift, silent drops, unbounded queues, or replay breakage.

Phase 2 top-five ideas selected:
1. Deterministic production parallel scheduler with work-stealing lanes and replay-stable commit ordering.
2. Portable atomics plus seqlock/EBR metadata graduation from research spikes.
3. Lock-free/two-phase MPSC channel graduation for high-contention agent messaging.
4. Hook-backed POSIX bounded worker/reactor integration instead of detached or ghost-only execution.
5. Parallel conformance, fuzz, and large-swarm e2e gates with structured JSONL logs.

Phase 3 next-ten ideas folded in:
NUMA/locality-aware arenas, large-swarm telemetry/admission control, sharded trace/replay logs, scheduler policy isomorphism, timed-lane/waker/reactor routing, 64-worker configuration surface, memory-model litmus/CBMC gates, RCH-backed benchmark baselines, deferred-stub graduation docs, and platform fallback contracts.

title: Define production parallel runtime contract and replay-stable success gates
description:

- Semantic rule: parallel profile may alter throughput, scheduling mechanics, telemetry, and resource ceilings, but shared deterministic fixtures must retain identical canonical digests versus CORE/single-worker mode.

title: Implement deterministic work-stealing parallel scheduler with replay-stable commits
description:
Implement the production parallel scheduler core: worker lanes, deterministic work stealing, and replay-stable event commit order.

Current issue:
`src/runtime/parallel.c` is a single-threaded lane simulation. It does not create workers, steal work, execute concurrently, or scale beyond a small compile-time worker model.

Expected work:
- Add worker-local run queues/deques for READY, CANCEL, and TIMED classes, with bounded stealing and fairness controls.
- Preserve the existing cancellation priority and cancel-streak fairness semantics.
- Ensure all externally visible trace/scheduler events are committed through a deterministic sequence authority so replay digests remain stable for deterministic scenarios.
- Add worker lifecycle state, shutdown/drain behavior, and deterministic error paths for worker startup failure.
- Add unit tests for queue routing, steal ordering, fairness yields, cancellation storms, worker shutdown, and budget exhaustion.
- Add conformance tests comparing single-worker and multi-worker semantic digests for scripted scenarios.

Validation:
`rch exec -- make build PROFILE=PARALLEL`, focused runtime tests, and profile-parity/conformance targets once digest-sensitive behavior changes.

title: Integrate timed lane, wakers, and reactor readiness into parallel scheduling
description:
Integrate timed-lane routing, waker signaling, and reactor readiness into the production parallel scheduler.

Current issue:
`asx_parallel_run()` currently assigns all non-cancel tasks to READY and comments that TIMED assignment requires timer integration. Wakers are single-threaded flags. POSIX reactor hooks exist, but scheduler integration is not production-grade.

Expected work:
- Route timer-blocked tasks to TIMED with deterministic wake ordering.
- Make waker signaling safe across worker/reactor boundaries while preserving stale-handle fail-closed behavior.
- Integrate POSIX reactor readiness and ghost reactor fallback through the hook contract.
- Add tests for equal-deadline ordering, cross-worker wake, stale waker signal, reactor timeout, and deterministic ghost fallback.

title: Prototype locality-aware arena sharding for massive worker counts
description:
Design and validate locality-aware arena sharding for large-memory, many-core deployments without changing handle semantics.

Current issue:
The runtime uses flat static arenas and scans task slots by arena index. That is deterministic and simple, but a poor fit for 64+ cores and massive agent swarms unless locality and scan costs are controlled.

Expected work:

- Add isomorphism tests comparing flat arena and sharded arena behavior for lifecycle, cancellation, quiescence, and trace digests.
- Add microbenchmarks for scheduler scan cost, steal cost, cache locality, and memory footprint at large capacities.
- Keep constrained profiles on the existing compact arena path.

Validation:
Benchmarks via `rch exec -- make bench PROFILE=PARALLEL` and behavior proof via focused tests/profile parity.

title: EPIC: Rust Reference Fixture Capture Pipeline
description:
## Goal
Populate fixtures/rust_reference/ with golden outputs captured from the pinned Rust baseline
(commit 38c152405bd03e2bd9eecf178bfbbe9472fed861, toolchain nightly-2026-02-19).

## Why This Matters
The conformance gate currently runs against the C implementation's own fixtures, which validates
internal consistency but NOT Rust-vs-C behavioral parity. Without Rust-captured reference fixtures,
we cannot prove the C port produces identical semantic outputs for identical inputs. This is the
single highest-value remaining gap — it converts "self-consistent" into "provably equivalent."

## What "Done" Looks Like
- fixtures/rust_reference/ contains captured golden outputs for all 14 E2E fixture families (85+ scenarios)
- Each fixture has full provenance metadata (rust_baseline_commit, toolchain_commit_hash, cargo_lock_sha256)
- make conformance --fixtures-root fixtures/rust_reference passes with 0 semantic deltas
- Fixture schema validation passes against schemas/canonical_fixture.schema.json

## Architectural Context
The conformance infrastructure (tools/ci/run_conformance.sh) already supports --fixtures-root pointing
at Rust-captured data. The fixture schema, provenance map (docs/SOURCE_TO_FIXTURE_PROVENANCE_MAP.md,
28 provenance rows), and semantic delta budget policy (docs/SEMANTIC_DELTA_BUDGET.md, budget=0) are
all in place. This epic is purely about running the Rust side and capturing output.

## Risk
- The pinned Rust baseline may not build cleanly on current nightly (last verified 2026-02-26)
- Cargo.lock SHA must match exactly: 77f4bfaedfe5b8572dfca3181119f9432825ea3d868ee8f5d2793a6c5cdeffdc
- Any Rust-vs-C semantic delta discovered here would be a real bug (in either direction)
notes:
